items.title: Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026
items.summary: This paper describes the emergence and early global spread of SARS-CoV-2 variant BA.3.2, first identified in South Africa in late 2024. The variant carries a notably large number of substitutions and deletions in the spike protein relative to the antigens used in current COVID-19 vaccines, raising concern that it may reduce protection from prior infection or vaccination. Using a multimodal genomic surveillance strategy that combines traveler-based sampling, clinical specimens, airplane wastewater, and community wastewater monitoring, public health authorities tracked the variant's introduction and spread within the United States and internationally. Detection progressed from initial identification in an international traveler to clinical specimens and widespread wastewater signals spanning dozens of states, with the variant also reported across more than two dozen countries. The authors conclude that continued genomic surveillance is essential to monitor the evolution of BA.3.2 and assess its potential public health impact.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Mila Shakya, Kevin C. Ma, Laura J. Hughes et al.. Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.
items.summary: This study addressed the challenge of monitoring *Candida auris*, a multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen that spreads efficiently in healthcare settings through skin colonization and shedding, by exploring wastewater-based surveillance as a scalable alternative to direct patient screening. The researchers validated a quantitative PCR assay, originally developed for clinical colonization screening, for use with wastewater samples. The adapted workflow demonstrated high amplification efficiency, high reproducibility, and a low limit of detection, indicating strong analytical performance in the wastewater matrix. The findings support the integration of this qPCR assay into existing wastewater surveillance programs as a cost-effective means of detecting *C. auris* across entire healthcare systems, including in settings where proactive patient screening is not routinely performed.
items.citation: Rodríguez Stewart RM, Litvintseva AP, Chavez J et al.. Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: A Systematic Review of Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Pathogen Detection in Wastewater in Africa, with Focus on Rwanda: Implications for Early Warning and Public Health Surveillance.
items.summary: This systematic review examined the use of wastewater-based epidemiology for detecting gastrointestinal and respiratory pathogens across Africa, with particular attention to Rwanda as a rapidly urbanizing context where conventional surveillance systems fall short. The authors conducted a narrative systematic review drawing on peer-reviewed literature, global health reports, and surveillance studies retrieved from major academic databases, ultimately synthesizing findings from a substantial body of eligible studies. The review found that wastewater-based epidemiology offers a non-invasive and cost-effective means of capturing both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections at the population level, providing real-time epidemiological intelligence that traditional clinical reporting frequently misses. Key challenges identified include variability in wastewater sampling methods, environmental factors that accelerate pathogen decay, and inconsistencies in laboratory workflows across settings. The authors conclude that integrating wastewater surveillance into existing public health infrastructure in low- and middle-income countries like Rwanda could meaningfully strengthen epidemic preparedness and outbreak response, provided that investment in laboratory capacity, standardized protocols, and multisectoral collaboration is sustained.
items.citation: Bambara S, Isingizwe MC, Adegboyega TT et al.. A Systematic Review of Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Pathogen Detection in Wastewater in Africa, with Focus on Rwanda: Implications for Early Warning and Public Health Surveillance.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Multi-Pathogen Wastewater Surveillance enables Real-Time Targeted Public Health Interventions During the 2025 African Nations Championship Football Tournament
items.summary: This study investigated the feasibility and utility of multi-pathogen wastewater-based surveillance as a public health tool during a major football tournament held in Uganda, a low- and middle-income country context where such approaches have rarely been applied during mass gatherings. Wastewater samples were collected across numerous manholes at a national stadium on multiple match days, then processed and analyzed by quantitative PCR for a broad panel of enteric and respiratory pathogens including mpox. The surveillance detected at least one pathogen in the vast majority of samples, with enteric pathogens such as Shigella, Rotavirus A, and Enterovirus predominating, while mpox was found in a notable share of samples and respiratory pathogens including SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza B appeared at lower frequencies. Importantly, the findings directly informed real-time public health responses including sanitation reinforcement, hygiene promotion, environmental disinfection, and enhanced syndromic surveillance. The authors conclude that integrating multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance into mass-gathering preparedness frameworks is operationally feasible in low-resource settings and can provide actionable population-level intelligence to support outbreak detection and response.
items.citation: Nsawotebba A, Morunyanga I, Nakintu V et al.. Multi-Pathogen Wastewater Surveillance enables Real-Time Targeted Public Health Interventions During the 2025 African Nations Championship Football Tournament. 2026

items.title: Revealing the hidden burden: wastewater-based epidemiology for underreported and emerging infectious diseases in communities.
items.summary: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) is a surveillance approach that analyzes sewage to detect infectious disease signals at the population level, and this review examines its growing role in identifying pathogens that are underreported or missed entirely by clinical case-reporting systems. The authors synthesize evidence showing that wastewater analysis can detect enteric, respiratory, and neglected pathogens across communities, often before cases are clinically recognized, while sequencing-based studies have uncovered extensive diversity within the human virome, including novel and divergent viruses. Frequent co-detection of multiple viral taxa in wastewater suggests that co-infections may influence viral evolution, disease manifestation, and transmission dynamics. Despite methodological challenges in quantification and biological validation, WBE is positioned as a capable early-warning tool that bridges environmental and clinical surveillance. The review concludes that advances in long-read sequencing, bioinformatics, and global data integration will strengthen wastewater genomics as a core component of One Health surveillance frameworks for equitable and scalable global pathogen discovery.
items.citation: Greaves JC, Rodriguez RA. Revealing the hidden burden: wastewater-based epidemiology for underreported and emerging infectious diseases in communities.. Environmental monitoring and assessment. 2026

items.title: Toward a unified approach: Considerations for bioinformatic and sequencing activities & data in wastewater surveillance of biologic public health threats
items.summary: The paper examines the challenges and opportunities of applying next-generation sequencing technologies to wastewater-based epidemiological surveillance as a public health tool. The authors reviewed the full surveillance workflow—from sample collection and sequencing through data analysis and reporting—identifying gaps in existing guidelines, which they argue tend to favor conventional analytical approaches over sequencing-based methods. They found that while falling sequencing costs and lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic have made large-scale wastewater genomic surveillance increasingly feasible, inconsistencies in protocols, variable sample complexity, and uneven access to skilled personnel and IT infrastructure hinder the generation of reliable, comparable data across different settings. The paper offers concrete recommendations for standardizing sampling, sequencing, and bioinformatic protocols, while also emphasizing that technical harmonization alone is insufficient without supportive infrastructure, sustained funding, and enabling government policy frameworks.
items.citation: Psomopoulos F, O’Cathail C, Anastasiadou N et al.. Toward a unified approach: Considerations for bioinformatic and sequencing activities & data in wastewater surveillance of biologic public health threats. 2026

items.title: Traveler-based Genomic Surveillance: A Scalable Approach to Early Pathogen Detection and Global Biosecurity
items.summary: The paper describes the implementation and evaluation of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Traveler-based Genomic Surveillance program, which uses genomic sequencing of nasal swabs from volunteer international air travelers and aviation wastewater to detect infectious disease threats early. Nasal samples were anonymously collected from arriving international travelers at multiple U.S. airports, pooled for RT-PCR testing, and subjected to genomic sequencing for SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory and gastrointestinal pathogens, while wastewater was collected from arriving flights and airport collection points. The program successfully tested samples from nearly seven hundred thousand travelers and nearly one thousand wastewater samples over approximately three years, detecting SARS-CoV-2 in roughly one-fifth of sample pools and in the vast majority of wastewater samples, with sequence data made publicly available within approximately eleven days of collection. The system also identified seasonal patterns of influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, detected gastrointestinal viruses year-round, and was scaled up in response to specific international outbreaks including COVID-19, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and monkeypox. The authors conclude that voluntary, multi-pathogen traveler-based surveillance integrating nasal and wastewater sampling with genomic sequencing is a feasible and adaptable model for global early warning and pandemic preparedness.
items.citation: Bart SM, Smith TC, Rothstein AP et al.. Traveler-based Genomic Surveillance: A Scalable Approach to Early Pathogen Detection and Global Biosecurity. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission rates of different SARS-CoV-2 variants circulating simultaneously during the pandemic. The authors developed a method that jointly analyzes confirmed case counts alongside genomic sequencing data to infer variant-specific effective reproduction numbers, going beyond approaches that rely on sequence frequency data alone. Applied to data from United States states spanning over a year, the method estimates both the relative prevalence of co-circulating variants and their individual reproduction numbers over time. The framework also allows structured relationships between reproduction numbers to be modeled, enabling the estimation of fixed growth advantages that particular variants maintain consistently across different geographic locations. By combining epidemiological and genomic data streams, the approach yields richer insight into variant dynamics than either data source provides independently.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Bacterial defense mechanisms against bacteriophages: an evolutionary arms race
items.summary: This review paper examines the co-evolutionary arms race between bacteria and bacteriophages, focusing on the diverse defense mechanisms bacteria employ at each stage of phage infection. The authors systematically surveyed bacterial antiphage strategies ranging from surface-level defenses such as receptor modification, capsule production, and biofilm formation, to intracellular mechanisms including restriction-modification systems and abortive infection, as well as adaptive immunity through CRISPR-Cas systems. The review also addresses how bacteriophages counteract these defenses through means such as anti-CRISPR proteins, receptor mimicry, and enzymatic degradation of capsules and biofilms. The authors argue that understanding these dynamic interactions illuminates microbial ecosystem structure and provides a foundation for developing novel antimicrobial strategies, including engineered phages and combination therapies. Ultimately, the review positions phage therapy as a promising avenue for combating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.
items.citation: Rafwana Ibrahim, Jesil Mathew Aranjani. Bacterial defense mechanisms against bacteriophages: an evolutionary arms race. Archives of Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance governance across 193 countries to inform the 2026 Global Action Plan update
items.summary: This study evaluated the effectiveness of national action plans for combating antimicrobial resistance across all United Nations member states over a multi-year period using a newly developed One Health governance index. The researchers constructed this multidimensional index through expert consultation, incorporating hundreds of policy documents, weighted indicators, and multinational surveillance datasets, then applied difference-in-differences and joinpoint regression analyses to link governance quality to antimicrobial use, resistance prevalence, and related mortality. Global governance scores improved meaningfully over the study period, but implementation and monitoring consistently lagged behind policy design, particularly in animal and environmental sectors. A notable finding was that measurable reductions in resistance prevalence only emerged approximately five years after national action plan adoption, highlighting the delayed nature of policy impact, while multisector engagement and antimicrobial use surveillance systems showed the strongest associations with improved outcomes. The authors conclude that as the next Global Action Plan update approaches, sustained financing and more robust integration of environmental and agricultural components into One Health surveillance frameworks are critical for translating policy commitments into durable reductions in resistance.
items.citation: Weiye Chen, Yige Zeng, Jinxin Zheng et al.. Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance governance across 193 countries to inform the 2026 Global Action Plan update. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Microbial engineering for pesticide degradation: current insights and future directions for sustainable agriculture
items.summary: This review examines the problem of pesticide contamination in agricultural soils and evaluates microbial-based strategies for remediating these pollutants. The authors synthesize current knowledge on how pesticides affect crop physiology and metabolism, then explore how microorganisms break down these compounds through diverse metabolic and enzymatic pathways under favorable conditions. The review covers both conventional and advanced bioremediation approaches, with particular emphasis on microbial consortia that leverage functional diversity and synergistic interactions to achieve enhanced degradation efficiency, as well as microbiome engineering techniques that allow targeted manipulation of microbial communities. Engineering the rhizosphere with plant growth–promoting microorganisms and genetic modification of microbes are highlighted as integrative approaches that can simultaneously improve pesticide degradation and crop productivity. The authors conclude that these strategies, along with emerging technologies and consortia-based systems, represent a sustainable pathway toward resilient agroecosystems and ecological restoration.
items.citation: S. Sangeeta Srivastava Srivastava, Rakeeb Ahmad Mir, Sofi Javed Hussain et al.. Microbial engineering for pesticide degradation: current insights and future directions for sustainable agriculture. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Nodule–Microbiome Dynamics: Deciphering the Complexities of Nodule Symbiosis and the Root Microbiome
items.summary: This review examines the complex microbial communities associated with legume root nodules and their relationship to plant health and soil fertility. The authors focus on the well-established mutualism between legumes and rhizobia, which provides biologically fixed nitrogen essential for plant growth, while also addressing the emerging recognition that non-rhizobial endophytes colonize nodule tissues alongside rhizobia. The review synthesizes current knowledge on how host selection pressures and compatibility with rhizobial partners shape nodule-associated microbial communities, and investigates whether soil bacteria that stimulate nodulation represent the same functional group as those that ultimately colonize nodule tissues. The authors also explore the molecular signaling and counter-signaling mechanisms that regulate the entry of endophytes into nodules, considering both the facilitative and inhibitory effects these microorganisms can have on the nodulation process. Ultimately, the review argues that understanding nodule microbiome dynamics is critical for optimizing rhizobial symbiosis in crop legumes and for harnessing beneficial plant-microbe interactions to improve plant performance and soil fertility.
items.citation: Raja Ben-Laouane, Mohamed Ait-El-Mokhtar, Abdelilah Meddich et al.. Nodule–Microbiome Dynamics: Deciphering the Complexities of Nodule Symbiosis and the Root Microbiome. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for improved detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* infection in its intermediate snail hosts, which is critical for controlling and eliminating schistosomiasis but hampered by the limited sensitivity of conventional parasitological methods. Researchers developed a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of the parasite, optimized it under simple isothermal conditions, and evaluated its performance using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two endemic countries. The assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity in laboratory settings, outperforming microscopy and performing comparably to real-time PCR. In field surveys, it detected a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR, while microscopy failed to identify any positive individuals, with both molecular methods uncovering infections missed by parasitological techniques. The authors conclude that this assay offers a sensitive, specific, and field-deployable diagnostic tool suitable for routine snail surveillance and early warning of shifts in schistosomiasis transmission.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: You Only Look Once (YOLO) based machine learning algorithm for real-time detection of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper investigated whether a machine learning algorithm could automate the interpretation of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostic results, which are typically subject to subjective human error. The researchers applied the YOLOv8 object detection framework to digital images of LAMP reaction tubes, training it to locate individual tubes and classify them as either positive or negative for amplification. The trained model achieved high overall accuracy, precision, and recall for both positive and negative classifications on the test dataset. The authors conclude that this approach is suitable for real-time LAMP diagnostics, offering rapid, automated, and more objective result interpretation with minimal operational complexity.
items.citation: Mezgebo B, Chaffee R, Castellanos LR et al.. You Only Look Once (YOLO) based machine learning algorithm for real-time detection of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostics.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.
items.summary: This paper investigated nucleic acid amplification methods that can function across a wide range of temperatures rather than requiring precise thermal control. The researchers developed a LAMP-based amplification approach using a Bst polymerase with strong strand displacement activity and broad thermostability, enabling DNA synthesis across a temperature range spanning from below typical isothermal conditions to temperatures approaching those used in conventional PCR. They demonstrated that amplification could be initiated at both high and low starting temperatures and sustained even under dynamic, fluctuating temperature profiles. The system was validated for the detection of SARS-CoV-2 and Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomic material. The authors propose this broad-temperature amplification platform as a promising tool for point-of-care and field diagnostics in settings where maintaining strict thermal regulation is impractical.
items.citation: Hamidizadeh M, Bier FF. Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.
items.summary: This review examines isothermal amplification technologies as diagnostic tools for detecting pathogens in both livestock and companion animals. The authors surveyed recent advances in these nucleic acid amplification methods, which operate at a constant temperature and therefore eliminate the need for thermocycling equipment required by conventional PCR-based approaches. The review covers innovations in assay design and analytical improvements, as well as the integration of these techniques into portable, field-deployable detection platforms suited to resource-limited settings. The authors highlight that isothermal methods offer rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly alternatives to established molecular diagnostics, which are often constrained by the need for expensive instrumentation, specialized laboratory infrastructure, and trained personnel. The review also addresses remaining challenges and outlines future directions for incorporating these technologies into routine veterinary diagnostics and disease surveillance programs.
items.citation: Tooryan F, Enyertornye B, Choudhury FJ et al.. Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Label- and wash-free electrochemical nucleic acid detection via a LAMP platform coupled with silver ion aptamer probes.
items.summary: This paper developed a new electrochemical method for detecting nucleic acids by combining loop-mediated isothermal amplification with silver ion aptamer probes, eliminating the need for labels or washing steps. The system uses specially designed hairpin-shaped probes in which a silver ion-binding aptamer sequence is embedded in the stem and a target-complementary sequence is in the loop; when LAMP amplicons are produced, they hybridize to the loop region, disrupting the hairpin and releasing silver ions that generate a measurable electrochemical signal at an electrode. The approach was validated by detecting the vanA gene, a marker of vancomycin-resistant Enterococci, in genomic DNA from Enterococcus faecium. The method achieved highly sensitive and specific detection at very low copy numbers within a reaction volume of fifty microliters in under an hour from amplification to signal readout. The authors propose this label-free, wash-free, one-step platform as a promising tool for point-of-care molecular diagnostics.
items.citation: Lee S, Lee S, Ju Y et al.. Label- and wash-free electrochemical nucleic acid detection via a LAMP platform coupled with silver ion aptamer probes.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize, as it contains only a bibliographic reference to a technical report and a note about corrections, with no scientific content described.
items.citation: V. Kotov. Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package. Dokumentenrepositorium der RUB (Ruhr University Bochum). 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, in both food safety and clinical healthcare contexts. The authors surveyed advances across electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, with particular attention to how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity and specificity in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning with these biosensor platforms, which the review argues transforms conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic devices capable of real-time analytics, pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing. The review critically identifies persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation approaches including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking forward, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain-integrated data management, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent innovations in microfluidic chip technology and their applications in laboratory medicine, with particular attention to how these systems are being enhanced through artificial intelligence integration. The authors surveyed advances in chip design and fabrication methods, including three-dimensional printing and modular flexible substrates, alongside the incorporation of biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. These developments have expanded clinical utility across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, and personalized medicine. The convergence of microfluidics with machine learning has given rise to smart diagnostic platforms that offer self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support, while emerging applications in neuroscience and microbiome profiling illustrate the technology's broad reach. The review also addresses ongoing challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration that must be overcome before next-generation microfluidic platforms can be routinely deployed in clinical and public health settings.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Taenia solium neurocysticercosis: Its current epidemiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and control landscapes
items.summary: Neurocysticercosis, caused by the cestode *Taenia solium*, is the most prevalent helminthic infection of the human central nervous system and presents with highly variable clinical manifestations. This review synthesizes the current state of knowledge on the disease's epidemiology, noting its global relevance including in industrialized nations where it is encountered among immigrant populations. The authors examine advances made over the past decade in diagnostics, including more specific antigen and antibody detection methods and improved magnetic resonance imaging sequences, as well as therapeutic developments such as combined anti-parasitic drug regimens, strategies to mitigate treatment-associated inflammation, and novel surgical approaches. Despite these advances, diagnostic difficulties remain and treatment strategies can vary depending on disease type, complicating clinical decision-making. The review is intended as a comprehensive practical reference for clinicians in both endemic and non-endemic settings to guide optimal diagnosis, treatment, and understanding of disease variability.
authors: for The Cysticercosis Working Group in Peru (CWGP)
items.citation: Javier A. Bustos, Christina M. Coyle, Kiran T. Thakur et al.. Taenia solium neurocysticercosis: Its current epidemiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and control landscapes. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control
items.summary: This review examines antimicrobial resistance as a public health threat transmitted through the food chain, analyzing how resistance spreads across animal agriculture, aquaculture, and food processing from a One Health perspective. The authors evaluated both established culture-based phenotypic detection methods and advanced molecular approaches, including whole genome sequencing, metagenomics, and CRISPR-based diagnostics. While acknowledging the speed and resolution advantages of molecular tools, the review highlights persistent challenges such as matrix interference, the viable but non-culturable bacterial state, and disconnects between genotype and observed phenotype. The paper also describes integrated mitigation strategies spanning antimicrobial stewardship on farms, biofilm control innovations, and consumer hygiene practices. The authors conclude that closing technical and regulatory gaps in surveillance is essential for developing effective interventions and securing a safer food system.
items.citation: Emílio Gomes, Tomás Gonçalves Mesquita, Patrícia Serra et al.. Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Droplet Digital CRISPR for Nucleic Acid Detection
items.summary: This review paper examines droplet digital CRISPR (ddCRISPR), a nucleic acid detection technology that combines the sequence specificity of CRISPR-based diagnostics with the absolute quantification power of digital droplet microfluidics. The authors surveyed the underlying principles of droplet generation, manipulation, and detection, as well as recent developments in both amplification-dependent and amplification-free detection strategies. By partitioning samples into vast numbers of picoliter-scale droplets, the technology achieves single-molecule resolution while reducing background noise, enabling highly sensitive and precise detection of viral, bacterial, and other nucleic acid biomarkers. The review identifies persistent challenges such as workflow automation, droplet stability, multiplexing capacity, and assay portability, while also outlining future directions including artificial intelligence-assisted data analysis and point-of-care integration. The authors present these findings with the goal of guiding the translation of ddCRISPR platforms from research settings into practical, scalable diagnostic tools.
items.citation: Yang Zhang, Roy S. K. Walker, Anwar Sunna et al.. Droplet Digital CRISPR for Nucleic Acid Detection. Advanced Science. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the diagnostic utility of cystatin C for the early detection of acute kidney injury in patients with sepsis. The researchers systematically retrieved relevant studies from electronic databases, assessed their quality using a standardized tool, and performed a random-effects meta-analysis combined with summary receiver operating characteristic curve analysis to pool diagnostic accuracy estimates across multiple studies. Cystatin C demonstrated good overall diagnostic performance for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, and subgroup analyses revealed that studies adhering to the Sepsis 3.0 diagnostic criteria showed higher specificity and diagnostic odds ratios with less heterogeneity. Combining cystatin C with other biomarkers further improved diagnostic accuracy beyond cystatin C alone. The authors conclude that cystatin C is a promising biomarker for early clinical identification of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, though they acknowledge residual heterogeneity among the included studies.
items.citation: Cheng L, Zhang B, Hu X et al.. Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the diagnostic and prognostic utility of pancreatic stone protein (PSP) as a biomarker for detecting nosocomial and postoperative sepsis in paediatric patients, a context where distinguishing infectious from sterile inflammation is particularly difficult. The authors conducted a structured literature search across two major databases, screening studies published over a recent multi-year period and ultimately synthesising findings from those meeting inclusion criteria. The reviewed evidence indicates that PSP levels rise significantly in children with sepsis compared to those with non-infectious systemic inflammation, and elevated PSP is associated with bacteraemia, organ dysfunction, and mortality. PSP showed diagnostic performance comparable to or exceeding that of conventional markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, including strong sensitivity and specificity in neonatal and other high-risk paediatric populations. The authors conclude that PSP is a promising early biomarker for paediatric sepsis but emphasise that heterogeneity across studies necessitates larger multicentre prospective trials and integration of PSP into multimarker diagnostic frameworks before routine clinical adoption.
items.citation: Ramírez Quintana A, Gaman EL, Badea M et al.. Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the immature platelet fraction, a marker of bone marrow thrombopoietic activity, for the early identification of sepsis. The authors searched two major databases and selected studies meeting predefined inclusion criteria, extracting pooled sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio, with subgroup analysis separating adult from pediatric data. The meta-analysis found that the immature platelet fraction demonstrated only moderate diagnostic accuracy for sepsis, with pooled sensitivity and specificity both around seventy percent and a combined diagnostic odds ratio indicating a modest ability to discriminate sepsis from non-sepsis conditions. Moderate heterogeneity was observed across the small number of included studies, limiting the robustness of the conclusions. The authors conclude that while the immature platelet fraction may serve as a complementary biomarker, its clinical utility remains uncertain and larger, standardized prospective studies are needed before it can be recommended for routine early sepsis diagnosis.
items.citation: Wiranata S, Manuaba IBAP, Supadmanaba IGP et al.. Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Hematology, transfusion and cell therapy. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated and compared the diagnostic accuracy of interleukin-27 (IL-27) and C-reactive protein (CRP) as biomarkers for neonatal sepsis, a condition where existing evidence had been inconsistent. Following PRISMA guidelines, the authors searched multiple major databases spanning nearly three decades and pooled data from controlled studies involving neonates using established statistical tools to calculate sensitivity, specificity, and area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve. The analysis found that IL-27 demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity and specificity than CRP for diagnosing neonatal sepsis, with a notably greater area under the curve. The authors conclude that IL-27 offers superior diagnostic accuracy compared to CRP and may serve as a more reliable biomarker to support early and accurate identification of neonatal sepsis in clinical settings.
items.citation: Liu W, Zhang Y, Liu W et al.. Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Aligning neonatal sepsis triage diagnostics with WHO target product profiles in low- and middle-income countries.
items.summary: This paper examined the landscape of diagnostic approaches for neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries, where the condition remains a leading driver of infant death yet effective diagnostics remain largely inaccessible. The authors synthesized evidence across a range of current and emerging strategies, including clinical algorithms, host-response biomarkers, haematological parameters, continuous monitoring, and artificial intelligence-based digital platforms, evaluating each against the WHO Target Product Profile for neonatal sepsis triage. The analysis assessed not only diagnostic performance but also operational feasibility in resource-constrained settings and suitability for point-of-care use outside hospital environments. The review identified promising technologies, including host-response biomarkers with greater accuracy than those currently in use and affordable tools capable of improving predictive algorithms. The authors conclude that integrated diagnostic strategies combining point-of-care testing, routine clinical data, and digital decision support offer the most viable path toward earlier detection, more rational antibiotic use, and reduced neonatal mortality in these settings.
items.citation: Gleeson B, Blumel B, Ibarz Pavon AB et al.. Aligning neonatal sepsis triage diagnostics with WHO target product profiles in low- and middle-income countries.. BMJ global health. 2026

items.title: Calprotectin as a Diagnostic Marker for Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Sepsis in the Emergency Department.
items.summary: This study investigated whether calprotectin, a neutrophil activation marker measured in plasma, could serve as a useful diagnostic biomarker for sepsis and identifying the source of infection in emergency department patients. Researchers prospectively enrolled several hundred patients presenting with suspected sepsis to a university hospital emergency department and measured calprotectin levels at admission, comparing its performance against established markers such as C-reactive protein. Calprotectin showed modest ability to distinguish sepsis from non-infectious systemic inflammatory response syndrome, but was not an independent predictor of this distinction when C-reactive protein was included in multivariable analysis. However, calprotectin demonstrated meaningful utility in differentiating lower respiratory tract infections from both upper respiratory tract infections and urinary tract infections, and adding calprotectin to C-reactive protein significantly improved discriminatory ability for these comparisons. The authors conclude that calprotectin may enhance identification of lower respiratory tract infection source in sepsis presentations, though further research is needed to determine its value within standard clinical assessment.
items.citation: Wollmer M, Wessman T, Melander O et al.. Calprotectin as a Diagnostic Marker for Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Sepsis in the Emergency Department.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: This paper presents the 2026 update to the Surviving Sepsis Campaign international clinical practice guidelines, which aim to support clinicians managing adult patients with sepsis and septic shock across hospital, prehospital, and post-hospital settings. The guidelines were developed by a large, geographically diverse, multidisciplinary committee that incorporated patient and family input, and followed the GRADE methodology alongside an Evidence to Decision framework to evaluate and synthesize the available evidence. The scope of the guidelines encompasses screening and early management, infection control and antimicrobial stewardship, hemodynamic support, respiratory management, adjunctive therapies, and goals and transitions of care including long-term outcomes. Recommendations range from strong to conditional depending on the certainty of evidence and the balance of desirable versus undesirable effects, with explicit attention to resource availability and applicability in low- and middle-income country settings. The guidelines emphasize early identification and prompt treatment, responsible antimicrobial use with de-escalation strategies, and the importance of standardized care processes to improve patient outcomes in this condition responsible for millions of deaths annually.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Microbiota in cancer: current understandings and future perspectives
items.summary: This review paper examines the relationship between the microbiota and cancer, encompassing its roles in carcinogenesis, tumor progression, and patient prognosis. The authors trace the historical development of this research field and analyze the molecular mechanisms through which microorganisms influence oncogenic pathways, immune responses, and tumor metabolism. The review addresses the dual nature of the microbiota as both a promoter and inhibitor of cancer, and explores how it modulates responses to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the microbiota, including probiotics, antibiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation, are discussed alongside existing approved drugs and ongoing clinical investigations. The authors conclude by advocating for personalized approaches to exploit the anticancer potential of the microbiota and propose a comprehensive framework to guide future research and clinical applications in this area.
items.citation: Yanxi Yao, Yifei Zhu, Keji Chen et al.. Microbiota in cancer: current understandings and future perspectives. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and how its dysregulation contributes to a broad range of diseases. The authors synthesize the research history and key milestones in lipid metabolism, with particular emphasis on how lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways govern the behavior of immune cells including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils. The review explores how lipid metabolites regulate immune cell proliferation, differentiation, and activation across both innate and adaptive immunity, and describes multilevel regulatory mechanisms spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational control. The authors further connect lipid metabolic dysregulation to conditions such as autoimmune diseases, cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, cardiovascular diseases, aging, and metabolic disorders. Finally, the review outlines current therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, ongoing clinical efforts, and future directions including lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Exosomal Biomarker Discovery for Cardiovascular Diseases: Multi-Omics Integration, Reproducibility, and Translational Prospects
items.summary: This review examines the use of artificial intelligence to discover exosomal and extracellular vesicle biomarkers for cardiovascular diseases, focusing on how multi-omics data can be integrated to improve diagnostic capability. The authors surveyed machine learning, deep learning, and network-based approaches applied to vesicle-derived microRNAs, proteins, and lipids, evaluating their ability to perform feature selection, disease subtyping, and interpretable classification. Ensemble methods showed the most consistent classification performance across studies, while graph neural networks showed promise for pathway integration and evolutionary neural networks offered comparable discrimination of vesicle morphological features but with limited interpretability. The review finds that although AI-driven vesicle biomarker panels demonstrate encouraging performance in acute myocardial infarction and heart failure, the current evidence base remains largely exploratory, constrained by small cohorts, lack of external validation, and non-standardized isolation workflows that undermine reproducibility. The authors propose a practical framework—requiring comparison against established clinical standards, standardized protocols aligned with vesicle research guidelines, locked assay plans, and transparent AI reporting—to move exosomal diagnostics from exploratory research into clinical practice.

items.title: Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape and emerging innovations in diagnosing urinary tract infections, a globally prevalent bacterial infection complicated by high recurrence, biofilm formation, polymicrobial involvement, and rapidly growing antimicrobial resistance. The authors identify key limitations of traditional culture-based diagnostics, particularly slow turnaround times and inadequate characterization of resistance and virulence factors, which contribute to overreliance on empirical antibiotic therapy. The review surveys a range of advanced molecular diagnostic technologies, including nucleic acid amplification, biosensor platforms, microfluidic lab-on-chip systems, and omics-based approaches, assessing their capacity for rapid, sensitive, and pathogen-specific detection. A central focus is placed on the integration of these technologies with artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve diagnostic precision, guide targeted antimicrobial therapy, and support antimicrobial resistance surveillance. The authors conclude that the convergence of next-generation molecular tools with AI-assisted diagnostics represents a transformative approach to managing urinary tract infections and controlling antibiotic resistance, while also acknowledging outstanding challenges related to ethics, implementation, and regulatory frameworks.

items.title: Novel Rapid Phenotypic Susceptibility Testing Techniques That Enhance Antimicrobial Stewardship and Clinical Decision-Making.
items.summary: This review paper examined emerging rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing technologies and their role in addressing the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the landscape of these diagnostic approaches, focusing on growth-based methods and the fundamental principles underlying phenotypic testing. The review found that rapid phenotypic susceptibility testing can deliver actionable results significantly earlier than conventional methods, thereby reducing time to effective therapy in severe infections such as sepsis where treatment delays worsen patient outcomes. The authors also highlight the technology's potential to support antimicrobial stewardship programs, while acknowledging persistent barriers to implementation including inconsistent test performance, absence of standardized protocols, and cost-benefit uncertainties.
items.citation: Glover JS, Humphries R. Novel Rapid Phenotypic Susceptibility Testing Techniques That Enhance Antimicrobial Stewardship and Clinical Decision-Making.. Clinical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Rapid Detection of Pathogens and Resistance Genes in Positive Blood Cultures Using BioFire<sup>®</sup> FilmArray BCID2.
items.summary: This study evaluated the performance of a rapid molecular diagnostic panel for detecting pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes directly from positive blood cultures. The researchers compared the BioFire FilmArray Blood Culture Identification panel against conventional culture-based methods, including mass spectrometry identification and automated susceptibility testing, using samples collected at a university hospital. Resistance genes identified by the molecular panel were additionally confirmed through polymerase chain reaction. The panel successfully detected at least one microorganism in the vast majority of samples, with strong overall agreement with culture-based results; complete concordance was observed for certain key organisms, and detected resistance genes correlated well with phenotypic resistance profiles. The authors conclude that the panel provides rapid and reliable pathogen and resistance identification that complements conventional diagnostics, though its interpretation requires clinical context, particularly when evaluating organisms commonly associated with contamination such as coagulase-negative staphylococci.
items.citation: Çinar C, Çayci YT, Atakcan Z et al.. Rapid Detection of Pathogens and Resistance Genes in Positive Blood Cultures Using BioFire<sup>®</sup> FilmArray BCID2.. Polish journal of microbiology. 2026

items.title: Multiplex mismatch amplification mutation polymerase chain reaction assay for the rapid detection of antimicrobial-resistant determinants in Cutibacterium acnes.
items.summary: This study addressed the clinical problem of antimicrobial resistance in *Cutibacterium acnes*, a bacterium central to the pathogenesis of acne vulgaris, by developing a rapid molecular diagnostic method. The researchers designed a multiplex polymerase chain reaction assay combining mismatch amplification mutation assay principles to simultaneously detect resistance-associated mutations in ribosomal RNA and gyrase genes alongside acquired resistance genes in a panel of clinical isolates. The optimised protocol completed detection in approximately one hour, substantially faster than conventional susceptibility testing methods. The assay achieved perfect sensitivity and specificity across all tested resistance determinants. These results support its potential clinical utility for guiding appropriate antimicrobial treatment decisions in acne management and for monitoring the spread of resistant strains.

items.title: A review of bloodstream infections-pathogens, pathogenesis, diagnostic strategies, treatment methods-challenges and future aspects.
items.summary: This review examined bloodstream infections comprehensively, covering their historical development, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostics, treatment, and future directions across bacterial, fungal, viral, and parasitic pathogens. The authors conducted a systematic evaluation of peer-reviewed literature, clinical guidelines, and surveillance reports, critically synthesizing evidence on virulence mechanisms, immune evasion strategies, antimicrobial resistance, and emerging diagnostic and therapeutic innovations. Bacterial pathogens were found to predominate as causative agents, with Candida species representing the leading fungal contributors, while increasing antimicrobial resistance and diagnostic delays continue to drive substantial healthcare burden and mortality. Advances in molecular diagnostics, metagenomic sequencing, biomarker-guided testing, and artificial intelligence-assisted analyses were identified as meaningfully improving pathogen detection and clinical decision-making. The authors conclude that integrating next-generation diagnostics, genomic surveillance, and precision medicine holds considerable promise for enabling rapid, individualized treatment and ultimately improving outcomes in this persistently challenging clinical domain.

items.title: Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines represent a comprehensive update to international recommendations for the identification and management of sepsis and septic shock in adult patients, incorporating evidence published through mid-2025. The guidelines were developed using GRADE methodology, covering domains including screening, infection management, hemodynamic support, respiratory care, adjunctive therapies, and long-term outcomes, resulting in a total of over one hundred statements ranging from strong recommendations to good practice statements. Notable new recommendations include prehospital sepsis screening and antibiotic administration for patients with prolonged transport times, targeted blood pressure management with permissive hypotension in older adults, selective digestive tract decontamination in low-resistance settings, and active fluid removal following the acute resuscitation phase. Key changes from the 2021 guidelines include a shift away from routine empiric antifungal therapy, updated guidance permitting either invasive or noninvasive blood pressure monitoring in septic shock, and a preference for crystalloids alone over supplemental albumin for fluid resuscitation. Several prior recommendations were strengthened, including prolonged beta-lactam infusion and antimicrobial de-escalation, while others such as corticosteroid use and norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor were downgraded in certainty or strength based on updated evidence.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a versatile and sustainable platform material with broad applicability across energy, environmental, and healthcare domains. The authors comprehensively survey the synthesis chemistry, structural properties, and surface functionalization strategies that give graphene oxide its tunable characteristics, including adjustable band gap, high surface area, and configurable dimensionality spanning zero- to three-dimensional architectures. The review covers a wide range of applications, including photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and microplastics, carbon dioxide photoreduction, hydrogen production, energy storage in battery technologies, and ultrasensitive detection using surface-enhanced Raman scattering and gas sensing platforms. The authors highlight that graphene oxide can perform across these diverse fields as a standalone material rather than solely as a supporting component, underscoring its multifunctional nature. However, the review also acknowledges persistent challenges such as scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility, and proposes potential solutions while addressing health and sustainability concerns for future industrial deployment.

items.title: A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms
items.summary: This review examines the field of green synthesis of nanoparticles, focusing on methods that use biological entities such as plants, bacteria, fungi, algae, and yeast as natural reducing and stabilizing agents in place of toxic chemicals and harsh physical or chemical processes. The authors surveyed literature from multiple major scientific databases to critically assess advances in both plant-mediated and microorganism-assisted nanoparticle fabrication, covering the underlying formation mechanisms and the influence of biological constituents on particle size, morphology, and stability. The review also evaluates characterization techniques and the functional performance of biologically synthesized nanoparticles across biomedical, agricultural, catalytic, and environmental applications, including their photocatalytic and pollutant degradation capabilities. Key challenges identified include reproducibility, standardization, and scalability, which currently limit the transition of green nanotechnology from laboratory-scale research to industrial practice. The authors present this structured assessment as a resource to guide future efforts toward practically viable and environmentally sustainable nanomaterial production.

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, with relevance to both food safety and clinical healthcare settings. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, focusing on how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transforms conventional sensors into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. The authors conclude by outlining a forward-looking vision encompassing self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain integration, and standardized validation pipelines to facilitate practical deployment of next-generation food safety monitoring systems.

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent innovations in microfluidic chip technology and their applications in laboratory medicine, with particular focus on how advances in design, fabrication, and biosensor integration have expanded diagnostic capabilities. The authors surveyed developments in chip fabrication approaches, including three-dimensional printing and modular flexible substrates, which have improved device performance, sensitivity, and clinical utility while enabling miniaturized processing of complex assays from minimal sample volumes. Advanced biosensor integration now permits real-time detection of circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes, supporting applications in cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, and personalized medicine. A central theme of the review is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has produced smart diagnostic platforms capable of self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support. The authors also address ongoing challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration, and outline future directions for translating these technologies into routine clinical and public health use.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: A quantitative rapid test for urine creatinine <i>via</i> Fenton's reaction and a self-driven microfluidic device.
items.summary: This paper developed a rapid, quantitative point-of-care test for measuring creatinine in urine, motivated by its importance as a kidney function marker and a normalizer for other urinary biomarkers. The method exploits creatinine's ability to inhibit hydroxyl radicals generated by Fenton's reaction, where these radicals would otherwise cleave an oligonucleotide linker connecting magnetic and polystyrene microparticles. Higher creatinine concentrations preserve more of these particle-particle linkages, and after magnetic separation on a self-driven microfluidic device, the resulting length of accumulated polystyrene microparticles provides a visible readout proportional to creatinine concentration. The system demonstrated a low detection limit, broad pH tolerance, and resistance to common interfering substances. Validation against a standard clinical method using real urine samples showed strong concordance, supporting the test's accuracy and suitability for clinical use.
items.citation: Hartanto H, Li J, Szeto CC et al.. A quantitative rapid test for urine creatinine <i>via</i> Fenton's reaction and a self-driven microfluidic device.. Lab on a chip. 2026

items.title: Fabrication of photoresist SU-8 pyrolyzed carbon electrodes and their integration in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system
items.summary: This paper investigated the fabrication of pyrolytic carbon microelectrodes derived from the photoresist SU-8 and their application in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system. The researchers developed a three-step pyrolysis protocol to overcome adhesion, geometric distortion, and limited surface area problems associated with conventional two-step approaches, producing low-aspect-ratio planar electrodes with both micro- and millimeter-scale features. These carbon electrodes were integrated into a polydimethylsiloxane-based microfluidic device that measured current responses from red blood cells suspended in phosphate-buffered saline to determine hematocrit levels. Surface characterization revealed substantially greater roughness and thickness in the carbon electrodes compared to platinum, yielding increased electroactive surface area that reduced overpotentials and improved electrochemical performance. The resulting device achieved precision and accuracy for hematocrit determination comparable to previously reported platinum-based systems, demonstrating that this cost-effective, noble-metal-free fabrication strategy is a viable alternative for integrated diagnostic microdevices.
items.citation: Lee HY, Rogers J, Kendrick C et al.. Fabrication of photoresist SU-8 pyrolyzed carbon electrodes and their integration in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system. 2026

items.title: Microfluidic and MEMS-Based Biosensing Platforms for Fungal Respiratory Infections in Immunocompromised Patients: Toward Rapid, Specific, and Minimally Invasive Diagnosis.
items.summary: This review examines the challenge of diagnosing invasive fungal respiratory infections in immunocompromised patients, where conventional diagnostic methods suffer from poor sensitivity, specificity, and limited sample accessibility. The paper surveys microfluidic and microelectromechanical systems-based biosensing platforms as emerging alternatives, covering on-chip nucleic acid amplification, antigen immunodetection, and CRISPR-enhanced detection strategies that reduce sample volumes and turnaround times. The authors also describe advances in host response profiling—including transcriptomic, proteomic, and cytokine signatures—alongside MEMS-based approaches for detecting exhaled volatile organic compounds, mechanical biosensing of fungal targets, and biofilm monitoring. The review identifies persistent translational barriers including insufficient multicenter validation, biofouling in complex biological matrices, and absence of standardized biomarker panels. The authors conclude that combining artificial intelligence-driven multianalyte interpretation, multiplexed host-pathogen marker integration, and fully cartridge-based near-patient systems could enable earlier and more precise diagnosis, ultimately improving outcomes in vulnerable populations.
items.citation: Georgakopoulou VE, Pitiriga VC. Microfluidic and MEMS-Based Biosensing Platforms for Fungal Respiratory Infections in Immunocompromised Patients: Toward Rapid, Specific, and Minimally Invasive Diagnosis.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state and challenges of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time health monitoring in personalized and preventive medicine. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and integration with the body, as well as multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing signal processing and generating predictive health insights is also discussed. The review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs. Overall, it synthesizes developments across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to map the landscape of biosensor technologies for health applications.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Commercial Translation of Electrochemical Biosensors: Supply Chain Strategy, Scale-Up Manufacturing, and Regulatory–Quality Considerations
items.summary: This review examines why electrochemical biosensors, despite high analytical maturity in laboratory settings, rarely progress to commercial diagnostic products. The authors analyzed non-analytical factors contributing to this translational gap, focusing on supply chain design, scale-up manufacturing strategies, and regulatory and quality frameworks across major markets including the United States, European Union, and China. The paper compares dominant manufacturing approaches such as roll-to-roll printing and semiconductor-derived microfabrication, evaluating how each suits different product targets, cost structures, and regulatory risk classifications, while arguing that manufacturing and quality should be treated as upstream optimization problems rather than downstream corrections. Case studies involving disposable glucose strips, cartridge-based blood analyzers, and continuous monitoring systems illustrate how identical electrochemical principles can generate very different commercialization challenges depending on clinical context and system integration requirements. The review aims to provide a systems-level framework that aligns research design choices with industrial and regulatory realities to accelerate the path from laboratory prototype to market-ready diagnostic tool.
items.citation: Gao Zhou, Haibin Liu. Commercial Translation of Electrochemical Biosensors: Supply Chain Strategy, Scale-Up Manufacturing, and Regulatory–Quality Considerations. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Exosomal Biomarker Discovery for Cardiovascular Diseases: Multi-Omics Integration, Reproducibility, and Translational Prospects
items.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence can accelerate the discovery and validation of exosomal and extracellular vesicle biomarkers for cardiovascular diseases. The paper addresses the challenge that extracellular vesicle datasets are highly dimensional, heterogeneous, and difficult to reproduce across studies due to non-standardized isolation methods and pre-analytic variability. The authors surveyed and compared multiple AI approaches—including ensemble methods, deep learning, graph neural networks, and evolutionary neural networks—assessing their utility for integrating multi-omics data, selecting features, and classifying disease states such as acute myocardial infarction and heart failure. Ensemble methods showed the most consistent classification performance, while graph neural networks were identified as promising for pathway integration but insufficiently validated, and most existing studies remain exploratory with small cohorts and limited external validation. The review proposes a practical framework specifying reproducibility standards, comparison against established clinical biomarkers, and transparent AI reporting to guide the translation of exosomal diagnostics from research into clinical practice.
items.citation: Rasit Dinc, Nurittin Ardıç. Artificial Intelligence for Exosomal Biomarker Discovery for Cardiovascular Diseases: Multi-Omics Integration, Reproducibility, and Translational Prospects. Cells. 2026

items.title: Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers
items.summary: This review examines extracellular vesicles as mediators of intercellular communication and their potential as diagnostic and therapeutic agents in human disease. The paper synthesizes current knowledge on EV biogenesis, molecular composition, and classification—covering exosomes, microvesicles, apoptotic bodies, and oncosomes—alongside advances in isolation techniques and omics-based profiling. Particular attention is paid to EV involvement in viral infection, inflammation, immune regulation, and cancer biology, as well as the clinical promise of mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in regenerative medicine and the modulation of EV signaling through photobiomodulation. The authors also address critical translational obstacles, including the need for standardization, scalability, and harmonized regulatory frameworks under oversight bodies such as the FDA and EMA. The review concludes that integrating mechanistic understanding with clinical application positions EVs as transformative tools in precision medicine diagnostics and therapeutics.

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research

The review covers applications in environmental remediation such as adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants, plastics, and pathogens, as well as energy technologies including hydrogen production, carbon dioxide photoreduction, and battery systems. The authors conclude that while graphene oxide holds transformative technological potential, practical deployment remains constrained by challenges in scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility, and they propose possible directions for addressing these limitations in sustainable applications.

The authors conducted a comprehensive survey of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including developments in three-dimensional printing, modular architectures, and flexible substrates, alongside progress in biosensor integration for detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the creation of smart diagnostic platforms capable of self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support across applications ranging from cancer diagnostics to point-of-care testing and microbiome profiling. The review finds that these combined technological advances have substantially improved device sensitivity, automation, and clinical applicability, while also identifying persistent challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration. The authors conclude by outlining future directions for translating next-generation microfluidic platforms into routine clinical and public health practice.
