items.title: Conducting Polymers for Electrochemical Sensing: From Materials and Metrology to Intelligent and Sustainable Biointerfaces
items.summary: This review examines conducting polymers as materials for electrochemical sensors and biosensors, tracing their development from classical formulations such as PEDOT:PSS, polyaniline, and polypyrrole through to nanostructured, wearable, and transient device architectures. The authors analyze the fundamental mechanisms governing these materials, including charge transport, doping strategies, and the influence of morphology and biofunctionalization on sensitivity, selectivity, and stability. A central concern of the review is the reliability challenges facing the field, such as signal drift, dopant leaching, environmental degradation, and biofouling, alongside the absence of standardized metrology that prevents meaningful comparison across studies. To address this, the authors propose a framework for rigorous calibration, reference electrode design, and data reporting, and they benchmark performance characteristics across major conducting polymer families and sensing modalities. The review concludes by identifying future directions including organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors, biohybrid interfaces, artificial intelligence-driven modeling, and sustainable transient electronics.
items.citation: Giovanna Di Pasquale, Antonino Pollicino. Conducting Polymers for Electrochemical Sensing: From Materials and Metrology to Intelligent and Sustainable Biointerfaces. Sensors. 2026

items.title: Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid, accurate detection of *Escherichia coli* O157:H7, a significant foodborne pathogen, by developing a one-pot CRISPR/Cas13-based biosensor capable of simultaneously identifying two key genetic markers that define its serotype. The researchers exploited the differing collateral cleavage preferences of two distinct Cas13 proteins to create dual fluorescence channels, integrating target gene amplification via recombinase polymerase amplification, transcription, and CRISPR-mediated biosensing into a single reaction tube. This design eliminated the need for complex instrumentation and reduced contamination risk while achieving high sensitivity at a low detection limit. Validation using a mouse infection model demonstrated that results from fecal samples were consistent with standard PCR methods. The biosensor offers improved serotype discrimination and specificity compared to conventional CRISPR diagnostics, presenting a simple, field-deployable tool for food safety monitoring, clinical diagnostics, and infectious disease surveillance.
items.citation: He Y, Lin X, Zhang X et al.. Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.. JACS Au. 2026

items.title: Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Escherichia coli* in neonatal sepsis, where conventional culture methods are slow and frequently yield false negatives due to low blood volumes or prior antibiotic use. Researchers developed a multiple cross-displacement amplification assay coupled with a lateral flow biosensor targeting the *uidA* gene, using ten primers optimized to react at a fixed temperature within forty minutes. The assay achieved femtogram-level detection sensitivity with no cross-reactivity against non-*E. coli* strains. Clinical validation using blood and cerebrospinal fluid specimens from neonates showed complete concordance with quantitative PCR, and the MCDA-LFB method identified substantially more positive cases than conventional culture. The authors conclude that this approach, completable within approximately one hour with minimal equipment, offers a rapid, sensitive, and cost-effective tool suitable for point-of-care and resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Xiao R, Zou P, Zhou J et al.. Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Salmonella typhimurium*, a major cause of foodborne illness, by developing a novel biosensor combining DNAzyme-catalyzed amplification with CRISPR/Cas12a activity. The approach works through a cascade mechanism in which DNAzyme cleavage generates single-stranded DNA that initiates hybridization chain reaction amplification across three hairpin structures, forming DNA nanowires that present PAM sequences for subsequent CRISPR/Cas12a recognition and cleavage, thereby restoring a quenched fluorescent signal. This dual-stage signal enrichment strategy achieved an exceptionally low detection limit and a broad linear range spanning several orders of magnitude in bacterial concentration. The biosensor demonstrated straightforward operation and rapid response, and because its recognition and primer sequences can be readily modified, the authors propose it as a flexible platform adaptable to the sensitive detection of multiple foodborne pathogens.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Liu Y, Yue X, Li B et al.. Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor platform designed for rapid, point-of-care detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and emerging pathogen targets. The biosensor uses disposable graphene foam electrodes functionalized with pyrene-modified peptide nucleic acid probes, which are attached via π-π stacking to preserve the electrode's electronic properties and high surface area without requiring on-surface chemical reactions. A key advance was a heat-assisted functionalization protocol that reduced preparation time from many hours to just minutes while maintaining detection performance, enabling amplification-free and label-free identification of both the colistin resistance gene and, by simply swapping the probe, a carbapenem resistance gene. The platform demonstrated strong discrimination between complementary and non-complementary sequences and achieved low detection limits for both synthetic single-stranded DNA and bacterial plasmids. Consistent performance across independently fabricated sensors supports its potential for scalable manufacturing as a decentralized diagnostic tool against antimicrobial resistance and pandemic threats.
items.citation: Wang KY, Schulze H, Lozano Sanchez P et al.. Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.
items.summary: This review examined the state of biosensor technology for detecting two major foodborne pathogens, *Salmonella* spp. and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which rank among the leading causes of foodborne illness and death globally. Rather than surveying biosensors broadly across many pathogens, the authors conducted a pathogen-specific analysis mapping trends in bioreceptor development and transducer selection tailored to these two organisms. The review also evaluated, for the first time in this context, how artificial intelligence tools can accelerate biosensor design, optimization, and decision-making for detecting these particular pathogens. A central concern was bridging the gap between laboratory research and practical application, critically assessing which strategies hold genuine potential for scalability, portability, and routine deployment in food industry settings. The authors present their analysis as a practical roadmap intended to guide future research toward field-ready, industry-relevant biosensing solutions.
items.citation: Gumush SE, Al-Attar R, Sandbecker E et al.. Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.. Food chemistry. Molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Deep learning integrated plasmonic electrochemical sensing for fast and accurate pathogen detection.
items.summary: This paper investigated the integration of plasmonic electrochemical biosensing with deep learning algorithms to enable rapid and accurate detection of bacterial pathogens in field-deployable settings. The researchers developed a nanostructured biosensor using gold-nanoparticle graphene oxide hybrid nanocomposites to enhance charge-transfer kinetics via localized surface plasmon resonance, targeting Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhimurium, and Staphylococcus aureus. Voltammetric signals from the biosensor were processed by a combined MobileNet-Transformer and Gated Recurrent Unit deep neural network pipeline, where the MobileNet-Transformer extracted features and the recurrent unit suppressed temporal noise. The platform achieved extremely low picogram-per-milliliter limits of detection for all three pathogens using only a small sample volume and completing the assay in under ten minutes. The integrated system outperformed baseline convolutional and recurrent network models in classification accuracy and demonstrated potential for real-time, on-device decision-making applicable to food safety, environmental monitoring, and point-of-care diagnostics using low-cost portable hardware.
items.citation: Mansour S, Negm N, Alhashmi AA et al.. Deep learning integrated plasmonic electrochemical sensing for fast and accurate pathogen detection.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Precision Farming with Smart Sensors: Current State, Challenges and Future Outlook
items.summary: This review examines the current state, challenges, and future directions of smart sensor technologies in precision farming, motivated by growing global food demand and the inadequacy of traditional agricultural methods. The paper surveys how smart sensors monitoring soil conditions, plant growth, and environmental factors are integrated with the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, robotics, drones, and cloud computing to optimize yield, conserve resources, and improve farm management decisions. The authors explore the various types of smart sensors in use, their agricultural applications, and emerging technologies that could further advance data acquisition and decision-making. Despite meaningful progress in transforming how agricultural data is collected and analyzed, the review identifies persistent obstacles including sensor calibration difficulties, data privacy concerns, interoperability issues, and barriers to widespread adoption. The authors argue that addressing these challenges is essential to fully realizing the potential of precision farming for global food security and sustainable agriculture.
items.citation: Bonface O. Manono, Boniface Mwami, Sylvester Mutavi et al.. Precision Farming with Smart Sensors: Current State, Challenges and Future Outlook. Sensors. 2026

items.title: Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.
items.summary: This study examined how the lifting of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions affected the detection patterns of respiratory pathogens in children presenting with fever or respiratory symptoms at a medical center in Guangzhou, China. Researchers retrospectively analyzed nasopharyngeal swab samples from children tested using a consistent multiplex PCR panel across two periods, using a season-matched design to minimize seasonal bias by directly comparing the same calendar months before and after restrictions were lifted. Following the lifting of restrictions, detection rates of Influenza A, RSV, and human rhinovirus increased substantially in the season-matched comparison, while Influenza B and human metapneumovirus declined markedly. The post-restriction cohort also included a higher proportion of infants and greater rates of lower respiratory tract diagnoses, though the authors caution that changes in healthcare-seeking behavior and admission thresholds may have influenced these clinical comparisons. The findings support ongoing multiplex surveillance and age-targeted prevention strategies, while acknowledging that residual confounding from seasonality, concurrent SARS-CoV-2 circulation, and behavioral factors limits causal attribution to the lifting of restrictions alone.
items.citation: Hua L, Liang W, Li W et al.. Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).
items.summary: This study investigated the causes of severe acute respiratory infections among hospitalized adults in northern Thailand during the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. Researchers retrospectively analyzed respiratory samples from adult patients admitted to a regional hospital in Chiang Mai with SARI symptoms, testing specimens using multiplex real-time PCR capable of detecting a broad panel of respiratory pathogens. Nearly half of patients tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen, with adenovirus and rhinovirus emerging as the most frequently detected viruses, and co-infections occurring in a notable proportion of cases. Seasonal patterns were observed, with influenza A and rhinovirus peaking in January while adenovirus and enterovirus circulated consistently throughout the study period. The authors conclude that enhanced rapid molecular diagnostics and pathogen-specific surveillance are needed to reduce empiric antibiotic overuse and improve evidence-based clinical management in the post-pandemic era.
items.citation: Kham-Kjing N, Kawila R, Tariyo P et al.. Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.
items.summary: This study developed and validated a multiplex quantitative real-time PCR platform capable of simultaneously detecting ten viral and bacterial pathogens associated with bovine respiratory disease in dairy cattle from southern Brazil, filling a gap where only single-plex assays had previously been used. The system was standardized across multiple assay configurations and evaluated for analytical performance, repeatability, and reproducibility before being applied to field-collected nasal swabs. Field testing revealed that a substantial majority of sampled cattle were positive for at least one pathogen, with bacterial agents—particularly *Histophilus somni* and *Pasteurella multocida*—being the most frequently detected, and complex multi-pathogen detection patterns were observed across animals of different ages and clinical statuses. Pathogen occurrence was significantly associated with age, season, and farm-level factors, with specific pathogens showing distinct epidemiological distributions across these variables. The authors conclude that this first validated multiplex qPCR platform for Brazil enables rapid, cost-effective, and simultaneous detection of major bovine respiratory disease pathogens, providing a critical tool for advancing understanding of the disease's pathogenesis and epidemiology in the region.
items.citation: Rodriguez MC, Silva IV, Perotta JH et al.. Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: VisPan: real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection.
items.summary: This paper addressed the bioinformatics bottleneck in real-time pathogen detection using Oxford Nanopore sequencing by developing a visualisation tool called VisPan. The tool was adapted from existing RAMPART software to support multiplex PCR syndromic panels, enabling dynamic visual tracking of sequencing runs and amplicon coverage during diagnostic workflows. The system processes data from raw acquisition to taxonomic assignment within minutes, providing rapid identification of pathogens in complex clinical or environmental samples. Validation experiments confirmed the tool's reliability and accuracy in identifying all pathogens present in tested samples, demonstrating its suitability for genomic surveillance in both field and clinical settings.
items.citation: Lechat P, Kwasiborski A, Vincent R et al.. VisPan: real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection.. Bioinformatics (Oxford, England). 2026

items.title: Performance evaluation of the BioFire respiratory panel 2.1 plus and exploratory analysis of Ct values for respiratory pathogen quantification.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the BioFire FilmArray RP2.1 plus multiplex PCR panel for detecting respiratory pathogens and explored whether its cycle threshold values, made accessible through the FIREWORKS software platform, could serve as a semi-quantitative measure of pathogen load. Using a retrospective collection of specimens, some of which were serially diluted, the panel was compared against established reference assays including Xpert, Xpress, and in-house real-time PCR methods across hundreds of individual PCR results. The BioFire panel showed excellent qualitative agreement with comparator methods, with most discordant results occurring in specimens with high cycle threshold values indicative of low pathogen burden, and the panel additionally detected some samples that reference assays missed. Exploratory quantitative analyses revealed strong correlations between BioFire-derived cycle threshold values and those from comparator platforms, suggesting a reproducible relationship that could support semi-quantitative interpretation. The authors caution that these quantitative findings should be interpreted carefully given the exploratory nature of the study and the inherent challenges of comparing cycle threshold values across different platforms.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Vitale A, Mahler Z, Loup V et al.. Performance evaluation of the BioFire respiratory panel 2.1 plus and exploratory analysis of Ct values for respiratory pathogen quantification.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Post-pandemic resurgence and co-detectiondynamics of respiratory pathogens revealed by syndromic multiplex PCR.
items.summary: This study investigated the distribution, co-detection patterns, and seasonal dynamics of respiratory pathogens in patients with suspected respiratory tract infections at a tertiary-care hospital in Türkiye during the post-pandemic period. Using a syndromic multiplex PCR panel capable of simultaneously detecting a broad range of viral and bacterial pathogens, researchers retrospectively analyzed respiratory samples from several hundred patients over approximately one year. A pathogen was detected in just over half of samples, with Rhinovirus/Enterovirus being the most prevalent organism, followed by influenza A, adenovirus, SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Co-detections occurred in roughly one-fifth of positive samples and were dominated by Rhinovirus/Enterovirus, though sequential sample analysis suggested that many apparent co-infections may reflect residual nucleic acid from prior rather than concurrent infections. The findings confirm marked seasonal variation in pathogen circulation, a strong positive correlation between RSV and influenza A activity, higher positivity rates in women and children, and the overall clinical and epidemiological utility of multiplex PCR-based diagnostics in the post-pandemic era.
items.citation: Aygar IS. Post-pandemic resurgence and co-detectiondynamics of respiratory pathogens revealed by syndromic multiplex PCR.. BMC microbiology. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review paper examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly referred to as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine and diagnostics. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including developments such as three-dimensional printing and flexible modular substrates, as well as the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the creation of smart diagnostic platforms that support automated analysis, self-optimization, and clinical decision support. The review finds that these combined advances have expanded clinical applications across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also address ongoing challenges related to manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration, and outline future directions for translating these technologies into routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Interplay of Microbiome, Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Health and Disease
items.summary: This review examines the complex relationships among the human microbiome, oxidative stress, and inflammation in the context of both health and disease. The authors synthesize existing evidence on how microbial metabolites and specific probiotic strains help maintain redox homeostasis through pathways including immune regulation, modulation of inflammatory processes, and influence over mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production and antioxidant signaling. Conversely, oxidative stress and inflammation can reciprocally alter microbial diversity and function, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that disrupts homeostasis. The paper argues that this bidirectional interplay is increasingly recognized as relevant to the onset and progression of various diseases, though the precise mechanisms governing host-microbe interactions remain incompletely understood.
items.citation: Lourdes Herrera-Quintana, Pablo Iturbe-Sanz, Jorge Olivares-Arancibia et al.. Interplay of Microbiome, Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Health and Disease. Antioxidants. 2026

items.title: Advanced Diagnostic Technologies and Molecular Biomarkers in Periodontitis: Systemic Health Implications and Translational Perspectives
items.summary: This review examined advances in diagnostic technologies and molecular biomarkers for periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease with significant variability between patients and known links to cardiometabolic and other systemic conditions. The authors conducted a narrative review of literature spanning nearly a decade, focusing on point-of-care biosensing platforms and molecular biomarkers derived from saliva, gingival crevicular fluid, blood, and dental plaque. The review found substantial progress in multiplex optical and electrochemical point-of-care platforms, including microfluidic systems and early intraoral wearable sensors capable of quantifying host-response proteins such as matrix metalloproteinase-8 and various cytokines. Omics-derived biomarkers including microRNAs, cell-free DNA, extracellular vesicle signals, proteomic profiles, and microbiome classifiers showed promising diagnostic discrimination and mechanistic connections to systemic inflammation, though clinical translation remains constrained by study heterogeneity, spectrum bias, and insufficient external validation. The authors conclude that while these technologies hold near-term value for adjunctive risk stratification and longitudinal monitoring, they do not yet justify replacement of conventional periodontal examination, and that meaningful clinical impact will require standardized definitions, harmonized protocols, multicenter validation, and regulatory-grade evidence.
items.citation: Sebastian Biesiadecki, Monika Janeczko, Joanna Kozak et al.. Advanced Diagnostic Technologies and Molecular Biomarkers in Periodontitis: Systemic Health Implications and Translational Perspectives. Journal of Clinical Medicine. 2026

items.title: STING controls glycolysis and histone lactylation to drive macrophage metabolic reprogramming in postoperative ileus
items.summary: This paper investigated the role of the innate immune signaling protein STING in controlling macrophage metabolism during postoperative ileus, a condition marked by intestinal inflammation and impaired gut motility following surgery. Using LPS-stimulated macrophages and STING knockout cells, the researchers examined how STING influences glycolysis and the epigenetic modifications that follow from it. They found that STING promotes glycolysis by stabilizing the transcription factor HIF1α, which increases lactate production and drives histone lactylation at the hexokinase 2 gene locus, thereby opening chromatin and enabling IRF3 to bind the hexokinase 2 promoter and further amplify glycolytic activity in a self-reinforcing feedback loop. This work defines a STING-regulated circuit linking metabolic reprogramming to epigenetic changes that sustain pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization. The authors propose that targeting STING to interrupt this loop represents a potential therapeutic strategy for reducing intestinal inflammation and improving recovery in postoperative ileus.
items.citation: Kai Chen, Guofang Li, Ye Cheng et al.. STING controls glycolysis and histone lactylation to drive macrophage metabolic reprogramming in postoperative ileus. Communications Biology. 2026

items.title: Multifunctional biosensors redefining liquid biopsy: advancing simultaneous multianalyte detection
items.summary: This review examines the emerging field of multifunctional biosensors designed for liquid biopsy, which involves detecting circulating biomarkers such as tumor-derived DNA, microRNAs, proteins, exosomes, and circulating tumor cells from body fluids for noninvasive disease diagnosis. The authors argue that conventional single-analyte detection approaches inadequately capture the complexity of disease, motivating a shift toward platforms capable of simultaneous multianalyte measurement. The review surveys recent advances across a range of detection strategies, including optical, electrochemical, plasmonic, and CRISPR-based assays, as well as hybrid platforms incorporating smart surface engineering and nanotechnology. It further addresses how integration with microfluidics, artificial intelligence, and chemometric analysis can enhance sensitivity, reduce signal interference, and improve scalability. The authors conclude by identifying ongoing challenges in clinical translation and standardization, framing multifunctional biosensors as transformative tools for precision medicine and early disease detection.
items.citation: Panagiota M. Kalligosfyri, Antonella Miglione, Ada Raucci et al.. Multifunctional biosensors redefining liquid biopsy: advancing simultaneous multianalyte detection. Trends in biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations
items.summary: The paper examined the dual nature of *Enterococcus* species as both beneficial microorganisms and potential health risks. These bacteria are commensal inhabitants of the gastrointestinal tract and are found across diverse food and environmental sources, where certain strains have been exploited as probiotics, antibiotic alternatives, and protective cultures in food systems. Their beneficial roles include pathogen control, microbiome modulation, food fermentation enhancement, and production of bacteriocins with antimicrobial activity. However, the authors highlight that the same genus is also associated with healthcare-acquired infections and the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance genes, creating significant safety concerns. The review synthesizes current knowledge into a comprehensive overview intended to guide future research, regulatory frameworks, and practical applications in both agrifood and clinical settings.
items.citation: Ojonugwa Precious John, Kayode Olayinka Afolabi, Anayochukwu Chibuike Ngene et al.. Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Multiplexed storage and interaction of Rydberg spinwaves via the gradient echo memory protocol
items.summary: This paper investigated the integration of collective Rydberg excitations with temporally and spectrally multiplexed quantum memory schemes, specifically the Gradient Echo Memory protocol, which had previously been incompatible due to rapid motional dephasing caused by large spinwave wavevectors. The researchers developed a novel multi-photon addressing scheme, where optical fields are arranged at a "magic angle" to form a closed wavevector loop, enabling the generation of collective Rydberg excitations with near-zero momentum transfer. This approach extended the Rydberg spinwave lifetime by nearly an order of magnitude while remaining compatible with the inhomogeneous broadening inherent to the Gradient Echo Memory protocol. By applying microwave coupling between neighboring Rydberg states, the team demonstrated control over the attenuation between stored excitation modes through interaction-induced decay and showed interaction-controlled diffraction of retrieved optical signals. These results restore compatibility between Rydberg excitations and multimode quantum memory, opening pathways toward quantum networks and information processing systems with controllable long-range interactions.
items.citation: Bartosz Niewelt, Stanisław Kurzyna, Bartosz Kasza et al.. Multiplexed storage and interaction of Rydberg spinwaves via the gradient echo memory protocol. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Settlement Infrastructure, Inside Money Elasticity, and the Network Economics of Distributed Ledger Technology
items.summary: This paper investigates how modernizing financial settlement infrastructure affects the elasticity of inside money creation and balance sheet efficiency across advanced economies. The authors constructed a panel dataset of reform events spanning three decades and decomposed them into economic channels and adoption phases, identifying an S-shaped relationship between settlement modernization and inside money elasticity with two distinct inflection points separating a liberation phase, a compliance valley following the global financial crisis, and a mature recovery phase. Using event-study methods around a major European securities settlement integration and a synthetic control approach applied to a Swiss distributed ledger deployment, they demonstrate that settlement modernization generates efficiency gains that are conditional on network connectivity rather than being properties of individual nodes. Applying a framework derived from an established three-layer connectivity taxonomy, the paper forecasts meaningful efficiency recoveries from forthcoming central bank initiatives, with gains contingent on whether major economies join an emerging composability layer. The core theoretical contribution is that atomic settlement efficiencies are a bilateral pair property, implying that network topology fundamentally shapes the distributional consequences of distributed ledger adoption.
items.citation: Michail Samawi. Settlement Infrastructure, Inside Money Elasticity, and the Network Economics of Distributed Ledger Technology. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond Binary Rooftop Mapping: A Four-Class Deep Learning Framework for Green Roof Potential Assessment from Open Swiss Geospatial Data
items.summary: This study developed a deep learning framework to classify urban rooftops into four categories—existing green roofs, rooftops suitable for greening, rooftops with solar panels, and flat rooftops unsuitable for greening—moving beyond the binary approaches common in prior research. The framework modifies an existing convolutional neural network architecture and integrates high-resolution aerial imagery with rooftop slope data derived from a digital surface model, relying exclusively on openly available geospatial datasets. Applied to Bern, Switzerland, the model provides spatial evidence for where green roof expansion is realistically feasible, supporting urban planners in deploying green infrastructure for urban heat island mitigation. Because the framework is fully open source and built on publicly accessible data, it is designed to be transferable to cities beyond Switzerland.
items.citation: Htet Yamin Ko Ko. Beyond Binary Rooftop Mapping: A Four-Class Deep Learning Framework for Green Roof Potential Assessment from Open Swiss Geospatial Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Unfit for stranding assessment: a panel-scale multimodal-LLM audit of building-decarbonisation disclosure (BeDA)
items.summary: This paper investigated whether corporate sustainability disclosures from building-sector firms contain sufficient information to assess carbon stranding risk under emerging regulations such as New York City Local Law 97 and the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive. The researchers developed BeDA, a multimodal large-language-model auditing tool, and applied it to a large global panel of firms over two decades to evaluate standards compliance in building-decarbonisation disclosure. The tool demonstrated reliable scoring across different model families and converged with independent external criteria, lending credibility to its assessments. The central finding is that most corporate disclosure is unfit for stranding assessment: only a small minority of firm-reports disclose operational carbon intensity per square metre, with European disclosure rates roughly double those in the United States, and a substantial share of firms for which intensity could be constructed already exceed science-based pathway limits. The authors conclude that the primary barrier to enforceable building-stranding regulation is a measurable, jurisdiction-specific reporting gap that targeted disclosure mandates could close and that BeDA could monitor.
items.citation: Jingyi Xu, Minghui Cheng, Anchen Sun. Unfit for stranding assessment: a panel-scale multimodal-LLM audit of building-decarbonisation disclosure (BeDA). arXiv. 2026

items.title: Constellation Selection and Power Allocation for Multi-Cell OFDM-ISAC: Managing Inter-Cell Interference and Sensing Sidelobes
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of radar sensing performance in dense multi-cell networks where base stations simultaneously share time-frequency resources for both communication and sensing. The authors develop a framework that accounts for modulation type and receive filter design to manage the interference affecting delay-Doppler sensing in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing integrated sensing and communication systems. By deriving closed-form signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio expressions for matched filtering and reciprocal filtering, they reveal that these two filtering approaches produce structurally distinct interference terms—matched filtering depends on fourth-order constellation moments while reciprocal filtering is governed by inverse-power and ratio-type terms. Building on these expressions, they derive sensing-oriented power allocation strategies, including a ramped water-filling solution and a square-root allocation rule, and formulate joint constellation selection and power allocation problems as tractable mixed-integer convex programs. The analysis further extends to scenarios where inter-cell propagation delays exceed the cyclic prefix, showing how such delay violations redistribute the interference spectrum in a predictable way, and reveals that the two filtering methods exhibit different preferences for spectrally shared versus orthogonalized tones in multi-cell coordination.
items.citation: Kaitao Meng, Kawon Han, Christos Masouros et al.. Constellation Selection and Power Allocation for Multi-Cell OFDM-ISAC: Managing Inter-Cell Interference and Sensing Sidelobes. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Space-division multiplexed quantum key distribution exploiting multi-plane light conversion for few-mode fibers
items.summary: This paper investigates space-division multiplexing of quantum key distribution over few-mode fibers as a way to increase key rates and support multiple users simultaneously. The researchers used multi-plane light conversion to demultiplex entangled photons that were transmitted through a few-mode fiber, with distinct spatial modes serving as independent parallel channels rather than coherent superpositions. They experimentally implemented a spatially multiplexed BBM92 QKD protocol in which modes were selectively excited via separate single-mode fibers and then separated by the multi-plane light converter into distinct output ports. The approach successfully preserved entanglement across both channels while achieving low quantum bit error rates suitable for secure key generation. The authors argue this method offers a practical route toward scalable, multi-user quantum networks and future quantum internet architectures that require parallel quantum channels without degrading the correlations underpinning security.
items.citation: Qian Zhang, Stefan Krause, Felix Kunzmann et al.. Space-division multiplexed quantum key distribution exploiting multi-plane light conversion for few-mode fibers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.
items.summary: This study evaluated a field-deployable serological test for detecting Usutu virus and West Nile virus antibodies in wild birds at bird-ringing sites in the Netherlands, where both arboviruses are an emerging concern. The researchers used a species-independent Lateral Flow Microarray ImmunoAssay capable of simultaneously detecting antibodies against both viruses, testing it on wild birds captured in the field and comparing results against the gold-standard virus neutralization test. The assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for Usutu virus detection and successfully identified seroconversion in a Eurasian blackbird, which was independently confirmed by the reference method. Performance was also formally assessed using the WHO REASSURED framework, scoring well against its criteria for point-of-care diagnostics. The authors conclude that the assay is feasible for on-site serological surveillance of Usutu virus in wild birds, with its rapid, multi-analyte, and equipment-light format making it particularly suitable for resource-limited field settings.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper investigated how antibody orientation on gold nanoparticles affects the analytical performance of lateral flow immunoassays, and sought to overcome the limitations of conventional citrate-capped gold nanoparticles, which rely on random antibody adsorption and require energy-intensive synthesis. The researchers developed a one-pot, room-temperature method to synthesize phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles at large scale, producing uniform, monodisperse particles in large batch volumes within minutes. These nanoparticles exploit boronate-affinity interactions with carbohydrate moieties on antibody Fc fragments to achieve controlled, oriented antibody immobilization, thereby maximizing antigen-binding site accessibility. When tested in a lateral flow immunoassay for fecal occult blood detection, the phenylboronic acid-modified nanoparticles demonstrated dramatically improved sensitivity compared to conventional citrate-capped nanoparticle probes. The authors conclude that this scalable and straightforward synthesis platform has strong potential for clinical translation in high-sensitivity point-of-care diagnostics.
items.citation: Xu J, Li Q, Lu B et al.. Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.. Colloids and surfaces. B, Biointerfaces. 2026

items.title: Dual-enhancement lateral flow immunoassay <i>via</i> gold-decorated ferritin nanoprobes and SpyTag/SpyCatcher site-directed conjugation.
items.summary: This paper addressed the limited sensitivity of conventional lateral flow immunoassays, which stem from weak optical signals, randomly oriented antibodies, and inconsistent nanoprobe fabrication. The researchers developed a dual-enhancement approach combining gold-decorated ferritin nanocages with SpyTag/SpyCatcher chemistry to simultaneously improve the signal-generating nanoprobe and the antibody conjugation strategy. Engineered ferritin displaying SpyTag peptides served as a template for controlled gold nanocluster growth, producing highly uniform core-shell nanostructures, while the preserved SpyTag sites allowed subsequent covalent, site-directed attachment of SpyCatcher-fused antibodies to maximize antigen-binding capacity. Testing this system against human chorionic gonadotropin as a model analyte, the optimized assay achieved a substantially lower detection limit and dramatically improved sensitivity compared to commercial gold nanoparticle-based strips, while also demonstrating reliable performance in urine samples. The authors conclude that this synergistic strategy offers a broadly applicable route to enhancing the sensitivity of point-of-care diagnostic platforms.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Yuan X, Zhu X, Xu Y et al.. Dual-enhancement lateral flow immunoassay <i>via</i> gold-decorated ferritin nanoprobes and SpyTag/SpyCatcher site-directed conjugation.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Ag-rich Ag-Au nanoshells based lateral flow immunoassay for rapid and sensitive detection of bovine viral diarrhea virus.
