items.title: First implementation of a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system to improve lateral-flow immunoassay sensitivity via dextranase integration on paper.
items.summary: This paper investigated whether a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system (ATPS) could be used to preconcentrate protein targets and improve the sensitivity of lateral-flow immunoassays (LFAs), which are widely used for point-of-care diagnostics but are limited by poor detection thresholds. The key barrier to using a poly(ethylene glycol)-dextran ATPS with LFAs was the high viscosity of the dextran-rich phase, which prevents adequate fluid flow through the paper-based test strip. To overcome this, the researchers integrated the enzyme dextranase to degrade dextran in the concentrated sample phase before LFA application, characterizing enzymatic conditions and demonstrating improved fluid imbibition on paper. Combining the ATPS with dextranase achieved a tenfold improvement in detection limit for the model protein transferrin in artificial saliva compared to a conventional LFA. To simplify the workflow for point-of-care use, dextranase was dehydrated directly onto the paper strip, preserving the same sensitivity improvement while reducing manual liquid-handling steps.
items.venue: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
items.citation: Nicklen FD, Hadeed CH, Zhang F et al.. First implementation of a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system to improve lateral-flow immunoassay sensitivity via dextranase integration on paper.. Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Self-Contained Lateral-Flow Microfluidic Bead-Based Assay for Rapid Quantification of Early-Stage Kidney Biomarkers.
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of diagnosing kidney disease early, focusing on two emerging biomarkers—neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and cystatin C—that reflect early disease progression but currently require centralized laboratory analysis. The researchers developed a self-contained lateral-flow microfluidic bead-based assay that combines a microfluidic chip with paper-based components to automate immunoassay detection within a rapid timeframe using only a tiny volume of blood or urine. The system's modular design separates reagent storage and flow control from the binding and readout steps, providing flexibility in assay configuration. When validated against standard laboratory immunoassays, the platform demonstrated comparable sensitivity while achieving an extended dynamic range. The assay was further applied to neonatal mouse models of polycystic kidney disease, successfully detecting biomarker elevations consistent with disease progression, supporting its potential use in both preclinical research and decentralized clinical diagnostics.
items.citation: Porro G, Cristofori MS, Gagnieux C et al.. Self-Contained Lateral-Flow Microfluidic Bead-Based Assay for Rapid Quantification of Early-Stage Kidney Biomarkers.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines advanced biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, including E. coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors surveyed electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, evaluating how innovations in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection. The review critically assesses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability limitations, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic sample pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. The authors conclude by outlining a forward-looking vision encompassing self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain integration, and standardized validation frameworks to advance field-deployable, regulation-ready food safety diagnostics.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, also called lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine. The authors surveyed innovations in chip design and fabrication, including three-dimensional printing and flexible modular substrates, alongside the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of smart diagnostic platforms that can self-optimize, automate analysis, and support clinical decision-making. These combined technologies show broad applicability across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging fields such as neuroscience and microbiome profiling. The review also addresses persistent challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration that must be overcome to translate these platforms into routine clinical and public health use.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Electrochemical Biosensors for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis Using Protein Biomarkers: Current Trends, Advances, and Clinical Translation Potential
items.summary: This review paper examines the use of electrochemical biosensors for detecting cancer-related protein biomarkers in blood, with a focus on their potential for early diagnosis and prognosis through non-invasive liquid biopsy. The authors critically surveyed general strategies for electrochemical detection of serum proteins and catalogued recent advances in biosensor platforms targeting cancer-associated proteins, noting that many approaches have demonstrated impressive analytical sensitivity. The review identifies several critical obstacles hindering the transition from laboratory research to clinical use, including matrix effects in complex biological samples, insufficient validation with real patient samples, interpatient variability, and practical manufacturing and stability challenges. Particular emphasis is placed on the analytical and clinical validation requirements that biosensors must meet to achieve genuine clinical translation and eventual commercialization.
items.citation: Michael E. J. Lopez Mujica, Elena E. Ferapontova. Electrochemical Biosensors for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis Using Protein Biomarkers: Current Trends, Advances, and Clinical Translation Potential. Sensors. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review paper examines the dual biological roles of reactive oxygen species, which serve as essential signaling molecules at physiological levels but drive disease when produced in excess or dysregulated. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the major types, cellular sources, and molecular mechanisms of reactive oxygen species in both normal redox signaling and pathological oxidative stress. The review evaluates contemporary and emerging detection methods for reactive oxygen species and oxidative stress, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging techniques. The contribution of oxidative stress to major diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders is examined across these frameworks. The authors conclude by advocating for precision redox medicine, emphasizing targeted antioxidant-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies informed by improved detection technologies and deeper mechanistic understanding of redox biology.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Advanced Diagnostic Technologies and Molecular Biomarkers in Periodontitis: Systemic Health Implications and Translational Perspectives
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of emerging diagnostic technologies and molecular biomarkers for periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease with known links to cardiometabolic and other systemic conditions. The authors conducted a narrative review of literature spanning roughly the past eight years, focusing on point-of-care biosensing platforms and molecular biomarkers derived from biological matrices including saliva, gingival crevicular fluid, blood, and dental plaque. They found that multiplex optical and electrochemical platforms, including microfluidic systems and early intraoral wearable sensors, have advanced considerably, enabling quantification of host-response proteins such as matrix metalloproteinase-8 and various cytokines. Omics-derived markers including microRNAs, cell-free DNA, extracellular vesicle signals, and microbiome classifiers also show promise for diagnosis, monitoring, and elucidating mechanistic connections to systemic inflammation. The authors conclude that while these technologies hold near-term value for adjunctive risk stratification and longitudinal monitoring, clinical translation is constrained by study heterogeneity, spectrum bias, and insufficient external validation, and that replacing conventional periodontal examination is not yet warranted.
items.citation: Sebastian Biesiadecki, Monika Janeczko, Joanna Kozak et al.. Advanced Diagnostic Technologies and Molecular Biomarkers in Periodontitis: Systemic Health Implications and Translational Perspectives. Journal of Clinical Medicine. 2026

items.title: Emerging liquid biopsy tools to analyse cancer biomarkers: electrochemical sensors and extracellular vesicle analysis
items.summary: This review paper examines emerging technologies for liquid biopsy in cancer diagnostics, focusing on the detection and monitoring of cancer biomarkers from blood and other body fluids. The authors discuss the limitations of widely used methods such as ELISAs, including their cost, storage constraints, and reduced suitability for use outside centralised laboratory facilities, as well as their challenges in detecting low-abundance biomarkers. The paper highlights electrochemical sensors as a promising alternative, offering high sensitivity, direct quantitation, and lower cost, though they require additional adaptation effort for new analytes. The review also explores extracellular vesicles as particularly valuable targets for liquid biopsy, as their ability to protect nucleic acid and protein cargo from degradation may enable the collective enrichment of multiple tumour-derived biomarkers from a single blood sample. The authors argue that continued advances in these analytical platforms, combined with improved understanding of biomarker biology and clinical utility, could meaningfully improve outcomes for cancer patients.
items.citation: Anitha Devadoss, Michael Furness, N. Wu et al.. Emerging liquid biopsy tools to analyse cancer biomarkers: electrochemical sensors and extracellular vesicle analysis. Biochemical Society Transactions. 2026

items.title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of extending monocular 3D reconstruction to dynamic 4D scenes by incorporating the structured geometric nature of physical motion. The authors propose SM4RT, a transformer-based model that represents scene dynamics through a "Structure-of-Motion" framework, decomposing motion into a compact set of rigid-body transformation bases expressed as temporal sequences of six-dimensional twists in SE(3), rather than treating each point's displacement independently. Dense scene motion is recovered by assigning per-pixel weights over these shared motion bases, enforcing the constraint that points belonging to the same object follow a common rigid-body trajectory. The model uses a parallel encoder-decoder architecture to jointly infer geometry, world-coordinate motion, and kinematic structure in a single forward pass from monocular RGB video. SM4RT is claimed to achieve strong motion reconstruction performance while preserving the physically meaningful geometric structure of scene dynamics.
items.citation: Shing Ho J. Lin, Wenzhao Zheng, Dong Zhuo et al.. SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties
items.summary: This study conducted a spectroscopic survey of young stellar objects in Sh2-284, a distant and metal-poor star-forming region located toward the Galactic anticenter, to investigate how reduced metallicity influences stellar and accretion properties during star formation. Candidate young stellar objects were identified using infrared photometry and followed up with optical and near-infrared spectroscopy at the Large Binocular Telescope, covering a wide field and a range of stellar masses. The researchers employed multiple emission line diagnostics to derive accretion rates and compare them with those measured in nearby solar-metallicity star-forming regions, also providing initial estimates of iron and lithium abundances for select targets. A tentative flattening in flux-flux relations was identified for the metal-poor sample relative to solar-metallicity counterparts, a trend appearing consistently across multiple accretion tracers. The overall findings indicate that gas accretion onto young stars can be robustly sustained in sub-solar metallicity environments, with accretion rates spanning several orders of magnitude and a median broadly comparable to those seen in more chemically enriched regions.
items.citation: Katia Biazzo, Juan Manuel Alcalá, Felice Cusano et al.. LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss
items.summary: This paper investigates unified multimodal models that aim to support both image understanding and image generation within a single continuous token space. The authors propose a method called Twins, which forms a unified representation by channel-wise concatenating semantic features from a vision transformer with low-level latent features from a variational autoencoder on the same token grid, avoiding any increase in sequence length or attention cost. When training this unified space within a Diffusion Transformer, they identify a severe optimization imbalance caused by three sources of heterogeneity between the two feature types: frequency bias, intrinsic dimensionality differences, and differences in condition-aligned versus condition-independent uncertainty. To resolve this imbalance, they adapt a focal regression objective for flow matching that upweights dimensions where the model makes large errors, prioritizing the harder-to-fit generative component. The approach yields substantial image generation quality improvements over a naive mean squared error loss baseline and performs competitively on multimodal understanding benchmarks, narrowing the gap between understanding- and generation-oriented representations.
items.citation: Kaixiong Gong, Xin Cai, Bin Lin et al.. Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language models provide consistent and trustworthy evaluations of pseudoscientific claims, focusing on how deployment configurations rather than underlying model weights shape epistemic outputs. The researchers tested four major commercial model families on ethnonationalist pseudoscience derived from a specific biosocial framework, comparing responses across multiple temporal snapshots and across both API and web interfaces. One model family's fast versions, which power a major social media platform's default user experience, consistently assigned credibility scores dramatically higher than all other models, a divergence that did not appear when the same models were tested on uncontroversial scientific consensus or clearly refuted claims. The study also documented a silent, undocumented update that abruptly reversed one model's behavior overnight, and found that the same model identifier produced radically different credibility ratings depending on whether it was accessed via API or web interface. The authors conclude that a commercial model's epistemic stance is not a stable intrinsic property but is contingently shaped by system prompts, safety layers, interface routing, and undisclosed updates, rendering the epistemic reliability of these systems opaque to both users and researchers and constituting a matter requiring public accountability.
items.citation: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina. Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Random-Order Online Facility Location Beyond Uniform Opening Costs
items.summary: This paper studies online metric facility location in the random-order (secretary-style) model, where candidate facilities and their opening costs are known in advance but demand points arrive in a uniformly random sequence chosen by an adversary. The central challenge is handling arbitrary, nonuniform opening costs, a significantly harder setting than the uniform-cost case previously studied. The authors design a deterministic algorithm that, at each step, selects a candidate facility by minimizing a penalized objective that blends connection distance with a time-varying scaling of the opening cost, opening the facility when the current connection distance justifies the penalized cost. Using a monotone one-round charging scheme and an upper-envelope decomposition, they achieve a competitive ratio substantially better than the previous best factor for nonuniform costs, while a refined variant for uniform unit costs achieves an even sharper ratio. They also establish a lower bound showing that no randomized online algorithm can achieve a ratio below three minus a vanishing term, and demonstrate that this lower bound applies even under uniform costs on a prescribed candidate set—creating a provable separation between the full-space uniform-cost and nonuniform-cost models.
items.citation: Bo Peng, Zhihao Gavin Tang. Random-Order Online Facility Location Beyond Uniform Opening Costs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the alleged chaos in periodically forced traveling-wave reductions of fractional WBBM models: a quantitative re-examination
items.summary: This paper critically examines a widespread methodology in the nonlinear dynamics literature whereby fractional nonlinear evolution equations are reduced via traveling-wave substitution to planar Hamiltonian systems, periodically forced, and then assessed for chaos and bifurcations through visual inspection of phase portraits alone. The authors argue this approach is fundamentally flawed because the resulting systems are undamped, near-integrable oscillators governed by KAM theory, which strictly confines any chaos to exponentially thin stochastic layers, making the burden of proof for chaos claims extremely high. Taking a published study of the fractional Wazwaz-Benjamin-Bona-Mahony model as a representative case, they applied four independent quantitative diagnostics—Lyapunov exponent calculations, separation-growth tests over millions of time units, stroboscopic Poincaré sections, and spectral analysis—and found no evidence of chaos in any asserted instance, with exponents effectively zero and invariant curves remaining smooth and closed. They further demonstrate that the original study's linear stability analysis incorrectly identifies neutral stability as instability, and that its "quasi-periodic" unforced system is necessarily periodic by the topology of planar autonomous Hamiltonian flows. The paper closes by documenting how the Gottwald-Melbourne 0-1 test can produce false positives on regular orbits and how parameter sweeps of conservative systems generate misleading chaotic-looking diagrams, and it proposes a checklist of minimum quantitative standards that chaos claims in this literature should satisfy.
items.citation: Kaixuan Niu. On the alleged chaos in periodically forced traveling-wave reductions of fractional WBBM models: a quantitative re-examination. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This study examined the feasibility, acceptability, and diagnostic performance of point-of-care nucleic acid tests for both HIV detection and viral load monitoring in clinical and community settings in the United States. The researchers enrolled participants across two sites — a hospital-based clinic and an LGBTQ+ community center — administering qualitative and semiquantitative whole blood point-of-care nucleic acid tests alongside standard laboratory testing, with a randomized clinical trial component for people living with HIV. Participants also completed acceptability surveys and in-depth interviews, and time-and-motion observations were conducted to assess the impact of point-of-care testing on clinic workflow. The paper describes the study protocols and enrollment outcomes rather than final results, as primary analyses — including test performance, survival analysis for time to viral suppression, and qualitative findings — are anticipated in future publications. The study represents one of the most comprehensive prospective evaluations of point-of-care nucleic acid test implementation for HIV in the United States to date.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.
items.summary: This study examined whether pharmacologic measures of tenofovir adherence could predict future HIV viremia among people living with HIV in South Africa. Researchers compared three adherence metrics — a point-of-care urine tenofovir assay, quantitative urine tenofovir measured by liquid-chromatography-mass-spectrometry, and tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots — and assessed their associations with current and subsequent viral load outcomes at weeks using logistic regression. Tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots were significantly and negatively associated with viremia at the follow-up timepoint, whereas neither the point-of-care urine assay nor quantitative urine tenofovir showed significant associations with future viral load. Participants with undetectable point-of-care urine tenofovir were more likely to be viremic at enrollment and to have lower CD4 counts, suggesting this finding reflects recent treatment initiation or poor recent adherence rather than long-term adherence patterns. The authors conclude that dried blood spot tenofovir-diphosphate measurement holds the greatest promise for identifying patients at risk of future viremia and guiding targeted interventions.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Bodley N, Govender K, Moodley P et al.. Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: Feasibility of integrating a point of care triage test into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique: a qualitative evaluation
items.summary: This study explored the feasibility of integrating a point-of-care triage test measuring interferon-gamma-induced protein 10 into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique, where timely viral load testing remains constrained by laboratory delays and health system limitations. Using a qualitative approach nested within a clinical evaluation at two primary healthcare facilities, researchers conducted multiple rounds of interviews with people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy, as well as healthcare providers and programme stakeholders at various levels of the health system. Participants broadly valued routine viral load monitoring but described significant access barriers, and the point-of-care triage test was found to be acceptable across all groups, with same-day results perceived as reducing patient anxiety and enabling faster clinical decision-making. Providers and stakeholders recognised its potential to improve monitoring efficiency by directing confirmatory viral load testing only to those clients who need it, thereby supporting differentiated care, though concerns about test accuracy and the continued necessity of confirmatory testing were noted. The authors conclude that successful implementation would depend on adequate training, workflow integration, quality assurance, and clear client communication to embed the test effectively within existing antiretroviral therapy monitoring algorithms.
items.citation: Myburgh H, Saura-Lázaro A, van den Bogaart E et al.. Feasibility of integrating a point of care triage test into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique: a qualitative evaluation. 2026

items.title: Implementation bottlenecks of near point of care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people in Tanzania: A Qualitative Study.
items.summary: This qualitative study investigated the implementation bottlenecks of near point-of-care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people living with HIV in Tanzania, as part of a broader cluster-randomised trial conducted across East Africa. Researchers conducted clinic observations and in-depth interviews with healthcare workers at multiple time points over approximately one year, using a deductive thematic framework analysis informed by the Measurement Instrument for Determinants of Innovations supplemented with an inductive approach. The findings showed that near point-of-care testing improved result turnaround times and enabled same-day counselling, which motivated both healthcare workers and patients, while compatibility with existing practices, teamwork, and management commitment served as key facilitators. However, significant barriers were identified, including prolonged patient waiting times, scarcity of physical infrastructure and electricity, staff shortages, and delays caused by transporting samples to nearby laboratories. The authors conclude that sustained investment in staff training, infrastructure, sample handling, and guideline alignment is necessary to fully realize the benefits of near point-of-care viral load monitoring for this population.
items.citation: Msoka P, Mtenga A, Maro R et al.. Implementation bottlenecks of near point of care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people in Tanzania: A Qualitative Study.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Baseline Data on Viral Suppression, Treatment Adherence and Mental Health in Peripartum Girls and Young Women With HIV in Zimbabwe.
items.summary: This study examined viral suppression, treatment adherence, drug exposure, and mental health among peripartum adolescent girls and young women living with HIV in Zimbabwe, a population known to have poorer viral control than older women. Researchers enrolled participants aged fifteen to twenty-four years who were in the peripartum period and on tenofovir-lamivudine-dolutegravir regimens, collecting point-of-care viral load measurements, urine tenofovir assays, and validated mental health assessments at baseline. The study found high rates of viral suppression at enrollment, with detectable urine tenofovir and higher self-reported adherence being the strongest predictors of suppression, while marriage, food security, and financial security were also significantly associated. Mental health outcomes were generally favorable, with the majority of participants showing minimal depression and anxiety, though moderate stigma was common. These baseline findings suggest that dolutegravir-based regimens are associated with strong viral control in this cohort, and that objective adherence measures like urine tenofovir testing may be particularly informative for identifying those at risk of virological failure.
items.venue: Journal of the International AIDS Society
items.citation: Chawana-Mutingwende TD, Ngara B, Mudadi LS et al.. Baseline Data on Viral Suppression, Treatment Adherence and Mental Health in Peripartum Girls and Young Women With HIV in Zimbabwe.. Journal of the International AIDS Society. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the longstanding question of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper structured opposing arguments around four key contested issues: whether athletes experience greater infection susceptibility than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond the influence of confounding factors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, and travel, the validity of biomarkers used to assess immune health in those undertaking arduous exercise, and the overall quality of evidence underpinning claims about exercise-related immune suppression. A prevailing view in the field holds that while moderate exercise benefits immune defense, the high infection burden seen in elite athletes and military personnel reflects suppression caused by intense training loads. However, this view has been challenged on the grounds that many lifestyle and environmental factors unique to these populations activate shared immune pathways, making it difficult to attribute increased infection risk to exercise alone. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial, and the central question of whether exercise is an independent causative factor of increased infection risk remains unresolved, warranting further empirical investigation.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and its dysregulation across a range of diseases. The authors surveyed the research history of lipid metabolism and focused particularly on how lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways govern the behavior of immune cells, including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils, in both innate and adaptive immunity. They explored how lipid metabolites influence immune cell proliferation, differentiation, and activation through genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational regulatory mechanisms. The review also addresses how disrupted lipid metabolism contributes to autoimmune diseases, cancer, neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, aging, and metabolic disorders. Finally, the authors synthesize current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, surveying clinical trial progress and proposing lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches as future directions.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Sepsis
items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent innovations in microfluidic chip technology and their applications in laboratory medicine, focusing on advances in chip design, fabrication, biosensor integration, and artificial intelligence. The authors surveyed developments in fabrication methods such as three-dimensional printing and flexible substrates, which have improved device sensitivity and clinical utility while enabling miniaturized, automated processing of complex diagnostic assays from minimal sample volumes. Advanced biosensor integration now permits real-time detection of circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes, extending the reach of these platforms into cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, and personalized medicine. The convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning has further produced smart diagnostic platforms capable of self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support, with emerging uses in neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The review also addresses persistent challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration, and outlines future directions for translating these technologies into routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review paper examines exosomes — nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate cell-to-cell communication by carrying bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids — with a focus on understanding the molecular mechanisms governing their biogenesis, cargo loading, and functional heterogeneity. The authors synthesize current knowledge of the regulatory machinery involved, including ESCRT complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications, and survey modern omics platforms and machine learning tools used to decode exosomal content. The review assesses the clinical utility of exosomes as liquid biopsy biomarkers across cancer, metabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases, as well as their therapeutic applications in targeted drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, including evidence from ongoing clinical trials. The authors identify persistent translational barriers such as isolation protocol variability, cargo inconsistency, targeting specificity, and regulatory constraints. They propose a forward-looking framework integrating basic biology, engineering approaches such as synthetic exosome mimetics, and AI-driven diagnostics to advance exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines
items.citation: Dong-il Kwon, Sachin Bhagchandani, Stephen A. Ehrenzeller et al.. Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines. Nature reviews. Immunology. 2026

items.title: Plug, Play, and Comply: A Modular Framework for Online Variable Impedance with Arbitrarily Oriented Compliance Axes
items.summary: This paper presents a modular, robot-agnostic software framework for compliant robot control that extends the ROS control ecosystem with standardized joint and Cartesian command interfaces. The framework uses a plugin-based architecture to decouple controller infrastructure from specific control-law implementations, allowing compliant-control algorithms to be developed once and deployed across different manipulators without modification. A key technical contribution is support for arbitrarily oriented compliance axes, where translational and rotational stiffness and damping matrices can be rotated online to align with local task geometry rather than being fixed to the robot base or tool frame. The framework computes robot kinematics and dynamics from standard URDF models and supports variable impedance, nullspace targets, and feedforward terms through unified command interfaces. Real-robot experiments validate task-dependent compliance in contact-rich manipulation, and simulations confirm portability across manipulators with diverse kinematic and dynamic properties, with the complete framework released as open-source software.
items.citation: Mihael Simonič, Xiaocong Li. Plug, Play, and Comply: A Modular Framework for Online Variable Impedance with Arbitrarily Oriented Compliance Axes. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Pulsatile poromechanics in layered soft media controls fluid flow and solute transport: from fundamentals to brain clearance
items.summary: This paper investigated how layered architecture in soft porous biological tissues affects fluid flow and solute transport under oscillatory mechanical loading, with particular attention to brain tissue clearance. The researchers developed a bilayer poromechanical model, systematically selecting material property combinations—porosity, permeability, and p-wave modulus—that preserve an identical poroelastic timescale across multiple layered configurations and a homogeneous reference case. They found that while this timescale governs behavior in homogeneous media, the same parameter produces non-trivial and counterintuitive patterns of strain localization, fluid flow, and solute transport in bilayer media. These results suggest that layered tissue architectures may confer functional advantages for cellular homeostasis compared to homogeneous ones. The study further demonstrates that pathological disruptions to the brain's layered structure substantially impair fluid flow and metabolic waste clearance, offering a mechanical basis for transport deficits observed in neurological disease.
items.citation: Matilde Fiori, Sylvie Lorthois. Pulsatile poromechanics in layered soft media controls fluid flow and solute transport: from fundamentals to brain clearance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: HiKV: Hierarchical Importance-Aware KV Cache with Hardware Acceleration for LLM Decoding
items.summary: This paper addresses the memory bottleneck created by the continuously growing key-value cache during long-context large language model decoding. The proposed system, HiKV, combines an algorithmic two-stage compression strategy with a custom hardware accelerator: the first stage evicts unimportant tokens within a fixed budget, while the second stage selectively loads only significant elements from the remaining tokens, achieving higher compression ratios than either stage could reach alone. The hardware component features a reconfigurable importance sorter that handles the distinct sorting requirements of both stages within a single unified circuit. Evaluated on representative large language models, HiKV delivers substantial speedups and energy reductions in attention computation compared to an uncompressed baseline, while also reducing external memory accesses relative to state-of-the-art importance-based methods under matched accuracy conditions. These gains come with negligible accuracy loss and only a modest increase in system area.
items.citation: Chao Fang, Jun Yin, Man Shi et al.. HiKV: Hierarchical Importance-Aware KV Cache with Hardware Acceleration for LLM Decoding. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Capacitive Loading in Two-dimensional Fluxonium Quantum Processors
items.summary: The paper investigates why fluxonium qubits suffer from capacitive loading when arranged in highly connected two-dimensional architectures, a problem that has hindered scaling beyond one-dimensional layouts. Through analytical derivation, the authors establish a relationship between the qubit capacitance budget and its coupling capacity to external circuit elements, identifying parasitic capacitances from Josephson junctions and Josephson junction arrays as the primary culprits. They further show that the geometry of the qubit pads can be deliberately engineered to counteract this loading effect, turning a problematic degree of freedom into a design resource. Based on these findings, the authors develop practical design guidelines and use numerical simulations to demonstrate ultrafast, high-fidelity two-qubit gates in two-dimensional fluxonium architectures. The central conclusion is that capacitive loading is not a fundamental barrier to building scalable two-dimensional fluxonium quantum processors.
items.citation: Quan Guan, Guo Xuan Chan, Xu Dou et al.. Capacitive Loading in Two-dimensional Fluxonium Quantum Processors. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PIML-OFEM: A New Large-Scale Structural Analysis Method Based on Problem-Independent Machine Learning and Overlapping Finite Element Technique
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently analyzing large-scale heterogeneous structures, where high-resolution computation is costly and existing multiscale or machine learning approaches suffer from limitations such as repeated basis function construction or inaccurate boundary displacement interpolation. The authors developed PIML-OFEM, which combines an overlapping finite element formulation with problem-independent machine learning: oversampled numerical basis functions are computed on extended local domains to avoid prescribed boundary conditions, and these locally constructed bases are blended via a partition-of-unity framework to yield a globally continuous displacement field. A U-Net neural network learns to map local material property distributions to the corresponding numerical basis functions, eliminating repeated local solves during online computation and allowing the trained model to generalize across different load cases and boundary conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method closely reproduces fine-scale finite element solutions in displacement and strain energy while reducing online computational cost compared to direct finite element analysis and improving accuracy over prior substructuring approaches that rely on linear boundary interpolation. Applied to topology optimization, the framework supports stable high-resolution iterations with small filter radii and captures fine-scale structural features, positioning it as an efficient physics-data approach for large-scale structural analysis and design.
items.citation: Yilin Guo, Chang Liu, Zongliang Du et al.. PIML-OFEM: A New Large-Scale Structural Analysis Method Based on Problem-Independent Machine Learning and Overlapping Finite Element Technique. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Baseband-Free Wideband MU-MIMO OFDM via Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces
items.summary: This paper proposes a transmitter architecture for wideband multi-user MIMO OFDM systems that eliminates conventional digital baseband processing by offloading its functions entirely to the electromagnetic wave domain using two cascaded stacked intelligent metasurfaces. The first metasurface handles symbol loading and channel-adaptive multi-user precoding, while the second implements OFDM modulation—specifically the inverse discrete Fourier transform and cyclic-prefix insertion—directly as wave-domain operations on a monochromatic carrier. The authors develop a wave-domain system model capturing how block-level coefficients translate to radiated OFDM subcarriers, and they formulate the design of each metasurface as an operator-fitting optimization problem subject to practical discrete phase constraints. To solve these problems, a quantization-aware training-based gradient descent framework is introduced for both stages. Numerical results demonstrate that the optimized architecture accurately synthesizes the intended wave-domain functionalities and achieves strong end-to-end multi-user MIMO OFDM performance.
items.citation: Zheao Li, Jiancheng An, Chau Yuen. Baseband-Free Wideband MU-MIMO OFDM via Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces. arXiv. 2026

items.title: 'It's Primarily Around Their Viral Load': Public Health Decision-Making and HIV Risk Assemblages in Ontario, Canada.
items.summary: This study examined how public health practitioners in Ontario, Canada determine when the behaviours of people living with HIV constitute "significant" risk warranting official intervention, including enforceable orders. Drawing on assemblage theory and reflexive thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with public health personnel, the researchers explored how HIV risk is co-constructed through the interaction of biomedical technologies, institutional practices, legal frameworks, and social discourses. Five themes emerged, revealing that risk assessments centered on factors such as viral load levels, discontinuity in care, co-infection with other sexually transmissible infections, and noncompliance with public health directives. The study also found that the Undetectable = Untransmittable principle has reshaped how risk is understood and governed, but its uptake was uneven across public health units, resulting in inconsistent and sometimes coercive approaches to managing people living with HIV. The authors argue that conceptualizing HIV risk as relationally produced rather than individually determined challenges punitive frameworks, and they call for broader adoption of equity-based public health practices aligned with current scientific evidence.
items.citation: Daroya E, French M, Hastings C et al.. 'It's Primarily Around Their Viral Load': Public Health Decision-Making and HIV Risk Assemblages in Ontario, Canada.. Sociology of health & illness. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *P. vivax* co-circulate, and where conventional HRP2-based tests are compromised by low parasite densities and *pfhrp2/3* gene deletions. Febrile patients presenting at health facilities during peak transmission season were tested using the new Bioline Malaria multi-antigen RDT alongside conventional RDTs, expert microscopy, and quantitative PCR. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and strong agreement with expert microscopy, but its sensitivity dropped notably when qPCR served as the reference standard, revealing that submicroscopic, low-density infections were frequently missed. qPCR detected the highest overall malaria prevalence and identified more mixed-species infections than either microscopy or the RDT. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is suitable for routine clinical diagnosis, more sensitive tools are needed for malaria surveillance and control in endemic settings where low-density infections are epidemiologically significant.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.
items.summary: This study investigated circulating arboviruses in Haiti using an innovative surveillance approach during a period when conventional monitoring was disrupted by political instability. Researchers extracted nucleic acids from discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes collected from febrile patients at healthcare centers across two Haitian departments over several years. Testing these samples with a series of real-time PCR assays targeting flaviviruses, alphaviruses, and Oropouche virus revealed that a substantial number were positive for dengue virus serotype three, all collected in a single year, while no alphavirus or Oropouche virus positives were detected. Phylogenetic analysis of sequenced samples showed high similarity to strains circulating across the Caribbean during the same period, consistent with the broader dengue serotype three outbreak observed throughout the Americas at that time. The findings demonstrate that discarded malaria rapid diagnostic tests can serve as a practical and valuable tool for arbovirus surveillance in resource-limited or insecure settings where traditional public health infrastructure is compromised.
items.citation: Matulis GA, Smith HP, Hall G et al.. Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: Microbiota in cancer: current understandings and future perspectives
items.summary: This review paper examined the relationship between the microbiota and cancer, synthesizing current knowledge about how microbial communities influence tumor development, progression, and treatment outcomes. The authors traced the historical evolution of research in this field and analyzed the molecular mechanisms by which the microbiota modulates oncogenic pathways, immune responses, and tumor metabolism. The review addressed the dual nature of the microbiota as both a promoter and inhibitor of cancer, and explored how microbial communities influence responses to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the microbiota, including probiotics, antibiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation, were discussed alongside approved drugs and ongoing clinical trials. The authors propose that a comprehensive, personalized framework for understanding microbiota-cancer interactions is needed to advance clinical applications in microbiota-targeted oncology.
items.citation: Yanxi Yao, Yifei Zhu, Keji Chen et al.. Microbiota in cancer: current understandings and future perspectives. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring
items.summary: This paper developed an integrated telehealth monitoring framework combining IoT sensors with cloud-based artificial intelligence to enable real-time, continuous health surveillance for elderly and chronically ill patients. The system used the ZigBee wireless protocol to transmit physiological data—including heart rate, body temperature, and blood oxygen levels—from wearable sensors to a centralized processing unit, where machine learning algorithms including random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression were applied to detect health anomalies. Testing in a real-world care facility demonstrated that the system achieved very low transmission latency and minimal power consumption, making it suitable for long-term deployment. The random forest model performed particularly well in identifying critical health events, achieving high accuracy and near-perfect recall to minimize false negatives. The authors conclude that their modular, scalable architecture addresses key limitations of existing telehealth systems—such as high latency and poor integration—while reducing clinical burden and improving patient autonomy.
items.citation: B. V. Ravi Kumar, Mohammad Shahnawaz Shaikh. ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring. Emerging Science Journal. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent developments in microfluidic chip technology, commonly called lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine. The authors surveyed advances in chip design and fabrication approaches, including three-dimensional printing and flexible substrates, alongside improvements in biosensor integration that enable real-time detection of circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has given rise to smart diagnostic platforms capable of automated analysis, self-optimization, and clinical decision support. The review spans clinical applications ranging from cancer diagnostics and infectious disease detection to point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also identify ongoing challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration that must be addressed before next-generation microfluidic technologies can be routinely adopted in clinical and public health settings.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission
items.citation: Hedvig Hricak, Zachary J. Ward, Fabio Ynoe Moraes et al.. Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission. The Lancet Oncology. 2026

items.title: Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare
items.summary: This paper evaluated the safety of a large language model embedded in electronic medical records to support clinical decision-making at primary care clinics in Kenya. Trained physicians retrospectively reviewed over a thousand patient encounters to assess hallucination rates, guideline adherence, and the safety profile of the system's recommendations. Hallucinations were infrequent and clinical guidance aligned with local guidelines in nearly all cases, suggesting strong baseline performance. However, a notable minority of encounters contained actively harmful recommendations from the model, and a concerning pattern emerged in which clinicians were more likely to adopt harmful outputs than to accept beneficial corrections to their own notes. The authors conclude that while the tool shows promise for quality improvement in resource-limited settings, asymmetric uptake of harmful versus beneficial suggestions highlights the urgent need for usability improvements, locally tailored safeguards, and prospective trials to establish patient-level benefit.
items.citation: Ambrose Agweyu, Paul Mwaniki, Wilkister Musau et al.. Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties
items.summary: This study conducted a spectroscopic survey of young stellar objects in Sh2-284, a distant and metal-poor star-forming region located toward the Galactic anticenter, to investigate how reduced metallicity affects stellar accretion and disk evolution. Candidate young stellar objects were identified using infrared photometry and followed up with optical spectroscopy at the Large Binocular Telescope, characterizing a disk-bearing population spanning a range of stellar masses. The researchers employed multiple emission line diagnostics to derive accretion rates and compare them with those measured in nearby solar-metallicity star-forming regions. A tentative flattening in flux-flux relations was found for the metal-poor sample relative to solar-metallicity counterparts, a trend that appeared consistently across different accretion tracers. Overall, the results demonstrate that robust gas accretion onto young stars can be efficiently maintained in sub-solar metallicity environments, with accretion rates spanning several orders of magnitude and a median comparable to those seen in more metal-rich regions.
items.citation: Katia Biazzo, Juan Manuel Alcalá, Felice Cusano et al.. LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
items.summary: This paper investigates how explainability techniques can be applied to reinforcement learning in the safety-critical domain of air traffic control to help build trust in AI-assisted decision-making. The researchers trained a reinforcement learning agent in a simplified air traffic control environment where the agent learns to select alternative flight routes that avoid no-fly zones. To make the agent's decisions interpretable, they applied saliency maps as a preliminary explainability method, highlighting which input features most strongly influence the agent's choices. The work represents an early-stage exploration of explainable reinforcement learning as a foundation for human-AI collaboration in high-stakes aviation contexts, where transparency and trust are essential prerequisites for deploying automated systems.
items.citation: Anduel Mehmeti, Gabriella Gigante, Salvatore Venticinque. Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up
items.summary: This paper investigates a conjecture about how the mass of light particle towers near the core of effective field theory (EFT) strings scales with the string tension in four-dimensional theories with minimal supersymmetry. The Integral Scaling Conjecture posits that the scaling exponent takes only the discrete values of one, two, or three, and the authors examine whether this restriction can be derived from the bottom-up constraints of the Emergent String Conjecture and its associated brane-taxonomy rules. To test this, they systematically classify relevant duality frames into a large finite set of classes, identify viable EFT string candidates on charge lattices, and exhaustively verify the conjecture across all candidates. They find that integral scaling holds for all leading towers and for subleading towers below the species scale, with minor subtleties matching those seen in explicit top-down constructions, and they also uncover evidence that oscillator modes of EFT string candidates generate the full lattices of particles and strings. Additionally, they establish that a scaling exponent of one implies a perturbative string limit, though the converse does not hold, and they validate their classification against concrete compactifications in type IIA, F-theory, and M-theory.
items.citation: Muldrow Etheredge, Alvaro Herráez, Dieter Lüst et al.. Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
items.summary: This paper investigates how to better align quantum machine learning models with the structural properties of matrix-valued input data by leveraging spectral information. The authors introduce Quantum Spectral Models, in which the data-encoding unitary's generator is constructed directly from each input matrix rather than relying on conventional coordinate-wise rotation gates, resulting in Fourier representations whose frequency carriers and coefficients are shaped by the input's eigenvalues and spectral subspaces. Three variants based on symmetric, global block, and patch-local block Hamiltonians are studied and evaluated on digit recognition benchmarks and controlled synthetic tasks designed around spectral statistics. At the largest circuit depths tested, the proposed models outperform comparison quantum models across all benchmarks, with the patch-local variant excelling on recognition tasks and the global block variant excelling on spectrally defined synthetic tasks. Ablation studies further reveal a task-dependent split between the roles of spectral subspaces and spectral values, offering new design principles for structure-aware quantum machine learning models.
items.citation: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers. Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
items.summary: This paper investigated whether commercial large language models produce consistent and transparent evaluations of contested or pseudoscientific claims, specifically testing their responses to ethnonationalist pseudoscience derived from a biosocial framework. The researchers systematically queried four major model families through both API and web interfaces across multiple temporal snapshots, assigning credibility scores to pseudoscientific claims and comparing responses against control prompts testing established scientific consensus. One model family's fast versions, which power the default experience on a major social media platform, consistently rated the pseudoscientific claims as far more credible than all other models, a divergence not observed for control prompts where all models performed comparably. The study also documented a silent, undocumented update that abruptly reversed one model's behavior, as well as the same model identifier producing radically different outputs depending on whether it was accessed via API or web interface. The authors conclude that a model's epistemic stance is not a stable property of the underlying model but is instead shaped by deployment configurations such as system prompts, safety layers, and interface routing, all of which remain opaque to users and researchers, and they call for new forms of epistemic accountability in how commercial models are deployed.
items.citation: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina. Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset
items.summary: This study examined how well routine cement characterization measurements can predict performance properties of CEM I cement across multiple independent producers. Using a large multi-producer dataset spanning nearly three decades and collected under controlled laboratory conditions, the researchers applied machine learning attribution and producer-transfer tests to routine descriptors including oxide chemistry, Blaine fineness, particle-size distribution, physical properties, and derived Bogue and equivalent-alkali parameters. They found that fineness is the strongest single descriptor family for predicting strength class and water demand, though oxide chemistry contributes comparable predictive signal when considered jointly, and that Blaine surface area and compact particle-size distribution representations are largely interchangeable in this context. Strength class and water demand could be reliably recovered from routine measurements across producers, but the early-strength designation emerged only as a population-level tendency rather than a physically distinct class, reflecting that early strength development arises from multiple interacting factors. Producer-holdout tests revealed that while absolute prediction errors remained broadly consistent across held-out producers, recovery of within-producer strength variation was producer-dependent, suggesting that full characterization of producer-specific behavior may require additional phase speciation beyond routine measurements.
items.citation: Marchellino Ghorayeb, Christiane Rößler, Horst-Michael Ludwig et al.. Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study compared two WHO-endorsed nucleic acid amplification tests, Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance in presumptive tuberculosis patients in India. Using mycobacterial culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing as reference standards, the researchers prospectively enrolled patients at a tuberculosis centre in New Delhi and tested paired sputum specimens on both platforms while also recording operational and cost parameters. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra demonstrated higher sensitivity and specificity for both tuberculosis detection and rifampicin resistance identification, and produced substantially fewer invalid and indeterminate results compared to Truenat MTB Plus. Although Truenat was considerably less expensive per test, its higher rates of invalid and indeterminate results created an increased need for repeat testing that partially offsets its cost advantage. The authors conclude that a tiered diagnostic strategy leveraging Xpert Ultra's superior accuracy in higher-burden settings and Truenat's lower cost for decentralized deployment could best advance access to molecular tuberculosis testing.
items.citation: Sidiq Z, Anand A, Dwivedi KK et al.. Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.
items.summary: This review examines blood-based diagnostic approaches for tuberculosis, a disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that continues to pose a major global public health burden. The authors focus on serological methods, which have gained increasing attention due to their simplicity, rapid turnaround time, and cost-effectiveness compared to conventional sputum culture and molecular assays. The review is particularly motivated by the diagnostic challenges posed by extrapulmonary tuberculosis and cases that yield negative results with standard tests. The authors summarize current biomarkers employed in tuberculosis serodiagnosis, discuss how advanced diagnostic technologies can be integrated with these markers, and assess the potential of these combined approaches to enhance diagnostic accuracy across varied clinical contexts.
items.citation: Yue C, Geng X, Sun X et al.. Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.. Clinical chemistry and laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swabs could serve as accurate, nonsputum-based diagnostics for pulmonary tuberculosis. Using a nested case-control design within a prospective cohort of adults and children at primary care centers in Colombia, researchers applied Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing to saliva samples and nylon-flocked oral swab eluates, comparing results against sputum liquid mycobacterial culture as the reference standard. Saliva demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for culture-confirmed tuberculosis, surpassing the World Health Organization's target threshold for nonsputum diagnostic tests, while oral swabs showed lower sensitivity but comparable specificity. Saliva sensitivity was significantly greater than that of swabs, though the two specimen types did not differ significantly in specificity. Both collection methods were well accepted by participants, supporting their potential as practical alternatives to sputum-based testing for closing gaps in tuberculosis detection.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Vargas DA, Fuertes-Bucheli JF, Sanchez-Hidalgo A et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of GeneXpert MTB/RIF and TB-LAMP for Tuberculosis Detection Among Presumptive Tuberculosis Cases in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
items.summary: This study compared the diagnostic accuracy of two nucleic acid amplification tests, GeneXpert MTB/RIF and TB-LAMP, against the reference standard of solid mycobacterial culture for detecting tuberculosis among presumptive cases at health facilities in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. A cross-sectional design was used, with sputum samples from nearly four hundred participants tested simultaneously by all three methods. TB-LAMP demonstrated higher sensitivity but lower specificity than GeneXpert, and its positivity rate significantly exceeded that of culture, partly due to detection of non-tuberculous mycobacteria that can produce false-positive results. GeneXpert showed strong concordance with culture, high specificity, and the added advantage of simultaneously identifying rifampicin resistance, making it well suited as a confirmatory tool for suspected drug-resistant tuberculosis. The authors conclude that a sequential algorithm using TB-LAMP as an initial low-cost screen at peripheral facilities, followed by GeneXpert confirmation, could improve case detection while making efficient use of available resources in high-burden, resource-limited settings.
items.citation: UMUWE P, Wariso KT, ILOZUMBA J et al.. Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of GeneXpert MTB/RIF and TB-LAMP for Tuberculosis Detection Among Presumptive Tuberculosis Cases in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. 2026

items.title: Field-ready portable rapid nucleic acid test for tuberculosis detection and drug-resistance profiling in resource-limited settings
items.summary: This paper developed a portable, field-deployable nucleic acid diagnostic platform designed to detect tuberculosis and identify drug-resistant strains within a single unified system. The platform combines loop-mediated isothermal amplification targeting dual Mycobacterium tuberculosis genetic markers with an AI-enabled compact device and smartphone-based readout, enabling point-of-care use without laboratory infrastructure. Clinical evaluation across patient samples demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity, and real-world deployment in a primary healthcare setting by minimally trained personnel achieved near-perfect sensitivity and complete specificity relative to a standard commercial benchmark. Notably, the same platform architecture, without hardware modification, was extended to detect mutations associated with rifampicin and isoniazid resistance through a probe-free, allele-specific amplification approach. The authors propose that this integrated molecular diagnostic system can democratize tuberculosis care in high-burden, resource-limited settings by enabling early screening, informing treatment decisions, and supporting drug-resistance surveillance.
items.citation: Nag S, Banerjee S, Banerjee S et al.. Field-ready portable rapid nucleic acid test for tuberculosis detection and drug-resistance profiling in resource-limited settings. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of GeneReady MTB assay on sputum for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis: a prospective multicenter study in China.
items.summary: This prospective multicenter study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a novel molecular assay, GeneReady MTB, for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis in sputum samples from patients with symptoms of active disease across three Chinese hospitals. Participants underwent parallel testing with GeneReady, smear microscopy, mycobacterial culture, and the established Xpert MTB/RIF assay, allowing direct performance comparisons against a microbiological reference standard. GeneReady achieved high sensitivity and specificity against the reference standard, with performance stratified by bacterial load showing stronger sensitivity in smear-positive compared to smear-negative patients. Agreement between GeneReady and Xpert MTB/RIF was strong in both positive and negative classifications. The authors conclude that GeneReady offers diagnostic accuracy comparable to Xpert MTB/RIF while providing advantages of lower cost, faster turnaround, and simpler operation, suggesting potential utility as an initial diagnostic tool for pulmonary tuberculosis in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Shang Y, Tang Z, Deng Y et al.. Diagnostic accuracy of GeneReady MTB assay on sputum for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis: a prospective multicenter study in China.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and how its dysregulation contributes to a broad range of diseases. The authors synthesize the research history of lipid metabolism with particular emphasis on how immune cells—including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils—depend on lipid metabolites for proliferation, differentiation, and activation in both innate and adaptive immunity. The review covers lipid transport, signaling pathways, and multilevel regulatory mechanisms spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational processes that govern immune cell function. The authors then connect these mechanisms to pathological conditions such as autoimmune diseases, cancer, neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, aging, and metabolic disorders. Finally, the review surveys current therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, ongoing clinical trials, and future directions including lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disorder characterized by pain, inflammation, and structural bone and cartilage deterioration. The authors analyzed how nociceptive pathways connecting the knee joint to the central nervous system contribute to OA-associated pain, alongside pathological changes driven by inflammatory cytokines and dysfunction of key organelles, including mitochondria, lysosomes, and the endoplasmic reticulum. Specifically, they describe how accumulated damaged mitochondria with excessive reactive oxygen species, lysosomal destabilization from hydroxyapatite digestion, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress collectively drive cartilage degradation and chondrocyte apoptosis. Building on these mechanistic insights, the review outlines emerging pharmacological strategies that simultaneously target inflammatory cascades, restore organelle homeostasis through approaches such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and attenuate pain signaling. The authors also highlight organelle-targeted drug delivery systems as a means to improve therapeutic efficacy, proposing a multimodal framework for future osteoarthritis interventions.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026
