items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years
items.summary: This paper reports on the implementation and outcomes of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme, which uses low-dose computed tomography to detect lung cancer early in high-risk individuals aged 55 to 74 who have ever smoked and meet risk thresholds determined by multivariable models. The programme launched in 2019 and operates through regionally federated clinical infrastructure guided by national strategic, clinical, and economic frameworks. Over five years, more than two million people were invited, resulting in thousands of lung cancer diagnoses, the majority of which were caught at early tumour stages, representing an improvement in the early-stage proportion of lung cancer diagnoses across England, particularly in socioeconomically deprived regions. The authors conclude that large-scale lung cancer screening is feasible and scalable through centralised protocols and effective project management, though inequalities in participation remain an ongoing challenge. They argue these findings support broader adoption of lung cancer screening across the UK and internationally, and offer practical tools for global adaptation.
items.citation: Richard W. Lee, Arjun Nair, Haval Balata et al.. Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), immune cell receptors whose aberrant signalling is linked to chronic low-grade inflammation and non-communicable diseases associated with sedentary behaviour. The authors searched multiple databases and identified studies in which exercise was used as an isolated intervention in humans, ultimately including dozens of articles categorised by exercise type and duration, spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined training modalities. They found that acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise generally produced neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs were predominantly associated with unchanged or decreased TLR levels, whereas chronic aerobic training yielded mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise modulates TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise characteristics, but emphasise that substantial heterogeneity across study designs limits firm conclusions and that further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review paper examines recent developments in microfluidic chip technology, commonly known as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their applications in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including advances such as three-dimensional printing and flexible modular substrates, alongside the integration of biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the creation of smart diagnostic platforms that support automated analysis, self-optimization, and clinical decision support across areas including cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, and personalized medicine. The review also addresses emerging applications in neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling, underscoring the broad clinical reach of these technologies. Current challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration are discussed alongside future directions for translating these platforms into routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties
items.summary: This study presents a spectroscopic survey of young stellar objects in Sh2-284, a distant and metal-poor star-forming region toward the Galactic anticenter, aimed at characterizing how reduced metallicity affects stellar accretion and disk evolution. Candidate young stellar objects were identified using infrared photometry from Spitzer and ground-based observations, then followed up with multi-object optical spectroscopy at the Large Binocular Telescope across a wide field. The researchers derived stellar and accretion properties using nine emission-line diagnostics spanning hydrogen Balmer and Paschen series lines as well as the calcium infrared triplet, covering a range of stellar masses, and also provided initial estimates of iron and lithium abundances for a subset of targets. Compared to solar-metallicity star-forming regions, the metal-poor young stellar objects show tentative evidence for a flattening in emission-line flux-flux relations across multiple diagnostics, suggesting a metallicity-driven difference in accretion behavior. The authors conclude that gas accretion is efficiently sustained in this sub-solar metallicity environment, with accretion rates spanning several orders of magnitude and a median rate broadly consistent with those seen in nearby, more metal-rich regions.
items.citation: Katia Biazzo, Juan Manuel Alcalá, Felice Cusano et al.. LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
items.summary: This paper investigates how explainability techniques can be applied to reinforcement learning agents operating in safety-critical aviation environments, specifically Air Traffic Control. The researchers trained a reinforcement learning agent in a simplified Air Traffic Control simulation where the agent learns to select alternative flight routes that avoid no-fly zones. To make the agent's decision-making interpretable, they applied saliency maps as a preliminary explainability method to identify which input features most strongly influence the agent's choices. The work is motivated by the broader challenge of building trust in AI systems deployed in high-stakes domains, where explainability is seen as a key prerequisite for meaningful human-AI collaboration and higher levels of automation. The study represents an initial step toward integrating explainable AI into Air Traffic Control assistance tools, rather than presenting a fully deployed or extensively validated solution.
items.citation: Anduel Mehmeti, Gabriella Gigante, Salvatore Venticinque. Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up
items.summary: This paper investigates a conjecture about the mass scaling behavior of towers of states that become light near the core of effective field theory (EFT) strings in four-dimensional theories with minimal supersymmetry. The Integral Scaling Conjecture proposes that the exponent governing how the mass of these towers scales with string tension in Planck units is restricted to only three integer values. Working from the bottom-up perspective using the brane-taxonomy rules of the Emergent String Conjecture, the authors systematically classify duality frames into dozens of distinct classes and exhaustively test the conjecture across all viable EFT string candidates. They find that integral scaling holds for all leading towers and for subleading towers below the species scale, with only half-integral subtleties that are also present in top-down constructions, and they provide evidence that oscillator modes of EFT string candidates generate the relevant particle and string lattices. The analysis also reveals an asymmetry in the relationship between one of the allowed scaling values and perturbative string limits, and the classification is validated against concrete string theory compactifications.
items.citation: Muldrow Etheredge, Alvaro Herráez, Dieter Lüst et al.. Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental design challenge in quantum machine learning: how to encode matrix-valued input data in a way that respects the matrix's structural properties rather than treating it as a flat collection of coordinates. The authors introduce Quantum Spectral Models, which construct the generator of the data-encoding unitary directly from each input matrix, producing Fourier representations where input-dependent spectral gaps and subspaces naturally shape the model's frequency content and coefficient structure. Three variants are studied, differing in how they partition the Hamiltonian construction across the input matrix. Evaluations on digit recognition datasets and controlled synthetic tasks defined by spectral statistics show that the proposed models outperform comparison quantum models at the largest tested circuit depths, with the most appropriate variant depending on whether the task is governed primarily by spectral subspaces or spectral values. The work argues that aligning a quantum model's inductive bias with the spectral structure of its inputs provides both improved performance and a more interpretable framework for understanding expressivity in quantum machine learning.
items.citation: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers. Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
items.summary: This paper investigated whether commercial large language models provide consistent and reliable evaluations of pseudoscientific claims, focusing specifically on ethnonationalist biosocial theory as a test case. The researchers systematically tested four major model families through both programming interfaces and consumer-facing web interfaces across multiple time points spanning several months. They found dramatic instability and inconsistency: one model's fast variants assigned credibility scores to the pseudoscientific content that were two to five times higher than all competing models, while the same model identifier produced radically different scores depending on whether it was accessed via the programming interface or the web interface. The study also documented a silent, undocumented update that abruptly reversed one model's behavior overnight, and observed that the most defensible response—refusing to rate the claims at all—appeared in some models but eroded in their successor versions. The authors conclude that a model's epistemic stance toward contested claims is not a fixed property of the underlying model but is instead shaped by opaque deployment factors such as system prompts, safety layers, and interface routing, and they argue this opacity constitutes a public accountability concern.
items.citation: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina. Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset
items.summary: This study investigated how much information routine cement quality control measurements contain for predicting the performance of CEM I Portland cement, and whether predictive models trained on one producer's data transfer reliably to others. Using a large multi-producer dataset spanning nearly three decades and covering oxide chemistry, fineness, particle-size distribution, and derived compositional descriptors, the researchers applied machine learning methods including attribution analysis and producer-holdout validation. They found that fineness is the dominant descriptor family for predicting strength class and water demand, but oxide chemistry contributes a comparable signal when considered jointly, and that equivalent alkali shows a consistent negative association with late-age strength primarily through potassium oxide. Strength class and water demand can be recovered from routine measurements across producers, but early-strength designation emerges only as a population-level tendency rather than a physically separable class, because early strength depends on interacting factors including fineness, sulfate-alkali chemistry, and plant practice. Producer-holdout tests revealed that while absolute prediction errors remain broadly comparable across held-out producers, recovery of within-producer strength variation is producer-dependent, suggesting that full characterization of producer-specific behavior may require additional phase speciation data beyond routine measurements.
items.citation: Marchellino Ghorayeb, Christiane Rößler, Horst-Michael Ludwig et al.. Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.
items.summary: This study examined the cost of integrating point-of-care screening for three curable sexually transmitted infections into antenatal care in Zimbabwe, compared to the standard syndromic management approach. Researchers implemented screening at two primary healthcare clinics in Harare and collected economic cost data through staff interviews, time-and-motion studies, and review of study records, subsequently modelling implementation in a low-volume routine care setting over a twelve-month period. A substantial proportion of pregnant women screened tested positive for at least one of the three infections, confirming the relevance of screening in this population. The largest cost drivers were test kits and personnel, which together accounted for the majority of total intervention costs. The authors conclude that while point-of-care antenatal STI screening is feasible, the incremental costs relative to syndromic management highlight the need for less expensive point-of-care diagnostic tools to make such programmes more viable.
items.citation: Martin K, Bath D, Nyamwanza R et al.. Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote Australian First Nations communities, where the burden of chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and trichomonas is disproportionately high among young people. Using a decision analytic model with a government payer perspective and a ten-year time horizon, the researchers compared point-of-care testing against standard laboratory-based testing in terms of costs and quality-adjusted life years gained. The point-of-care programme was found to be cost-effective relative to standard care, generating an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio well below the willingness-to-pay threshold considered. The programme was also predicted to substantially reduce rates of pelvic inflammatory disease and preterm or low birth weight births among those with infections, with the results being most sensitive to the probability of infection and the likelihood of receiving treatment within two days. The authors conclude that sustaining and scaling this community-led point-of-care testing approach represents good value for money and is likely to improve reproductive health outcomes in remote primary care settings.
items.citation: Watts CG, Causer LM, Matthews SJ et al.. Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: From syndromic management to diagnostic-led management: a report from an expert meeting on introducing sexually transmitted infection testing in low-resource settings.
items.summary: This paper reports on an expert meeting convened to address the transition from syndromic to diagnostic-led management of sexually transmitted infections in low-resource settings, with a particular focus on sub-Saharan Africa. Syndromic management, while inexpensive, leads to overtreatment, undertreatment, and poor surveillance, whereas advances in point-of-care testing for key STI pathogens now offer a practical alternative. Experts from across disciplines in global and national STI care gathered to identify barriers and priorities for introducing and scaling up STI point-of-care diagnostics. Recommendations spanned multiple levels, including improving patient knowledge and uptake, optimising clinical workflows and expanding testing beyond formal health facilities, updating national treatment guidelines, and harmonising regulatory requirements and manufacturing capacity at the global level. The authors conclude that coordinated cross-level efforts are essential to ensure equitable access to point-of-care STI diagnostics, which they argue would improve care quality, curb antimicrobial resistance, and strengthen STI control.
items.citation: Manguro GO, Ray J, Schocken C et al.. From syndromic management to diagnostic-led management: a report from an expert meeting on introducing sexually transmitted infection testing in low-resource settings.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Use of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in community outreach settings in Dallas, Texas, USA.
items.summary: This study examined the implementation of rapid point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in non-clinical, community outreach settings in an urban environment. Researchers conducted a program evaluation and retrospective data review of individuals tested at these sites, using chi-squared and Fisher's exact tests to explore whether demographic characteristics or symptom presence were associated with testing positive. The testing platform delivered results within thirty minutes, and all diagnosed cases were successfully referred for treatment within one day, demonstrating the feasibility of rapid diagnosis and linkage to care outside clinical settings. No statistically significant associations were found between test positivity and demographic or symptom variables, though this finding was limited by a small sample size. The authors conclude that point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing holds promise for community-based STI screening, while calling for further research into scalability, cost-effectiveness, and treatment completion rates.
items.citation: Blanchard HL, Gonzalez E, Chow J. Use of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in community outreach settings in Dallas, Texas, USA.. Sexual health. 2026

items.title: The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria
items.summary: This paper presents an updated international clinical guideline for urticaria, a mast cell-driven disease characterized by wheals, angioedema, or both. The guideline was developed using Cochrane methodology and the GRADE framework, with a large multinational consensus process involving delegates from numerous national and international societies across many countries. The document covers the definition and classification of urticaria, distinguishing between acute urticaria and chronic forms — the latter subdivided into chronic spontaneous and chronic inducible urticaria — while addressing the significant burden these conditions place on quality of life and daily functioning. The guideline provides expert-guided, evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis and management across the different urticaria subtypes, incorporating novel therapeutic options that have become available. It was formally acknowledged and accepted by the European Union of Medical Specialists.
items.citation: T. Zuberbier, Z. Abdul Hameed Ansari, A. H. Abdul Latiff et al.. The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria. Allergy. 2026

items.title: Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines
items.citation: Dong-il Kwon, Sachin Bhagchandani, Stephen A. Ehrenzeller et al.. Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines. Nature reviews. Immunology. 2026

items.title: An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening
items.summary: This thesis examined methods for identifying and controlling sexually transmitted diseases, with particular focus on contact tracing and screening for asymptomatic infections. The research evaluated contact tracing routines across several disease contexts, compared epidemiological characteristics of chlamydia-infected women identified through different clinical settings, and investigated whether contact tracing data could inform mathematical models of partner choice and disease spread. Key findings included that contact tracing effectively controlled a gonococcal microepidemic, that integrating contact tracing into HIV care identified many previously unknown cases, and that screening at family planning clinics revealed meaningful chlamydia prevalence linked to specific risk factors including younger age, short relationship duration, and inconsistent condom use. Comparison of chlamydia cases found through screening versus those presenting at a dedicated clinic showed only minor epidemiological differences, supporting equally rigorous partner management in both settings. Partner choice analysis revealed that steady partnerships were selected in a restricted manner while casual partnerships followed a more random pattern, meaning the data did not support a purely random mixing model for disease transmission.
items.citation: Kristina Ramstedt. An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening. Acta Dermato Venereologica. 2026

items.title: Integrative Proteomics Reveal Neuroimmune and Dopaminergic Alterations Across the Nociceptive Neuraxis in Neuropathic Pain
items.summary: This study investigated the molecular changes occurring across the full pain-processing pathway in neuropathic pain, from peripheral nerve to spinal cord to brain regions involved in emotional processing. Using a chronic constriction injury rat model, the researchers applied high-resolution mass spectrometry-based quantitative proteomics to characterize protein expression changes in the sciatic nerve, spinal cord, and orbitofrontal cortex, complemented by behavioral assessments and immunofluorescence validation. Proteomic profiling revealed neuroinflammatory pathway enrichment across all three regions, with consistent elevation of S100 proteins alongside markers of astrocyte and microglial activation, indicating a widespread inflammatory state spanning the nociceptive neuraxis. Notably, the orbitofrontal cortex showed pronounced upregulation of dopamine-regulating proteins, implicating reward-related analgesic circuits in the affective dimension of chronic pain. The authors propose that the interplay between neuroimmune activation and dopaminergic adaptation defines a molecular framework for neuropathic pain chronification, and they identify glial S100 proteins and dopamine modulators as candidate therapeutic targets.
items.citation: Shreyasi Majumdar, Santosh Kumar Prajapati, Aishwarya Dande et al.. Integrative Proteomics Reveal Neuroimmune and Dopaminergic Alterations Across the Nociceptive Neuraxis in Neuropathic Pain. Cells. 2026

items.title: A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks
items.summary: This study examined the relationship between housing instability and drug overdose risk among young people who inject drugs, arguing that existing research has been limited by treating housing instability as a single-dimensional construct. Using baseline data from a network-based longitudinal study of young people who inject drugs and their social networks in metropolitan Chicago, the researchers developed a multi-dimensional housing instability risk index composed of five dichotomous variables and tested its association with lifetime overdose count through negative binomial regression. After adjusting for multiple covariates, the study found a significant positive association between the composite housing instability risk score and lifetime number of overdoses. The findings support the value of conceptualizing housing instability as a multi-dimensional construct and suggest that interventions aimed at reducing overdose risk should adopt a more holistic approach to addressing housing precarity.
items.citation: Kathleen Kristensen, Leslie D. Williams, Charlie Kaplan et al.. A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks. Journal of Urban Health. 2026

items.title: Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions
items.summary: This narrative review examined the current state of scientific knowledge on Compulsive Sexual Behavior Disorder and Problematic Pornography Use, two widely studied but contested constructs related to dysregulated sexual behavior. Drawing contributions from experts across psychology, psychiatry, sexology, addiction science, and neuroscience, the authors synthesized empirical and theoretical literature spanning eleven key domains, including historical context, conceptualization, assessment, epidemiology, co-occurring conditions, etiology, consequences, and treatment. The review also addressed underrepresented groups such as adolescents, women, and LGBTQ+ individuals, as well as the role of cultural factors in shaping how these behaviors are understood and experienced. The authors identify persistent methodological challenges and ongoing controversies regarding classification and measurement that continue to complicate the field. The work aims to advance interdisciplinary dialogue, improve clinical practice, and inform public health policy surrounding these conditions.
items.citation: Campbell Ince, Stephanie Antons, Sarah Ashton et al.. Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions. Journal of Behavioral Addictions. 2026

items.title: Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up
items.summary: This paper investigates the Integral Scaling Conjecture, which asserts that for EFT strings in four-dimensional theories with minimal supersymmetry, the mass scaling exponent relating a tower of light states to the string tension takes only the integer values one, two, or three. The authors approach this conjecture from the bottom-up perspective by leveraging the brane-taxonomy rules associated with the Emergent String Conjecture, systematically classifying relevant duality frames into dozens of distinct classes and identifying viable EFT string candidates on their charge lattices. Through exhaustive testing across all candidate classes, they confirm that integral scaling holds with the exponent at most three for both leading and subleading towers below the species scale, with minor half-integral subtleties consistent with known top-down constructions. Additional findings include evidence that oscillator modes of EFT string candidates generate the full lattices of particles and strings, and that while a scaling exponent of one implies a perturbative string limit, the reverse implication does not hold. The results are cross-checked against explicit compactifications in type IIA, F-theory, and M-theory, lending further support to the conjecture's validity.
items.citation: Muldrow Etheredge, Alvaro Herráez, Dieter Lüst et al.. Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
items.summary: This paper addresses a gap in quantum machine learning where standard data-encoding approaches fail to capture matrix-level structural relationships in matrix-valued inputs. The authors introduce Quantum Spectral Models, which construct the generator of the data-encoding unitary directly from each input matrix rather than applying coordinate-wise rotation gates, resulting in Fourier representations whose frequency carriers and coefficients are determined by the input's spectral gaps and spectral subspaces respectively. Three variants are proposed based on symmetric, global block, and patch-local block Hamiltonians, each encoding different aspects of matrix spectral structure as an inductive bias. The models are evaluated on digit recognition datasets and controlled synthetic tasks designed around spectral statistics, where the proposed variants outperform comparison quantum models at the largest tested circuit depths. Results further reveal a task-dependent split between the utility of spectral subspace information versus spectral values alone, suggesting that matching the form of spectral encoding to the structure of the target task is an important design consideration.
items.citation: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers. Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
items.summary: This paper investigated whether commercial large language models provide consistent and transparent evaluations of pseudoscientific claims, focusing on ethnonationalist biosocial theories as a test case. The researchers systematically queried four major model families through both API and web interfaces across multiple time points, recording how each model rated the credibility of contested claims. They found that one model family's fast versions, which power a widely used social media platform's default experience, consistently assigned credibility scores dramatically higher than all other models for the pseudoscientific content, while performing comparably to peers on control prompts testing genuine scientific consensus. Additional findings revealed that a model's epistemic stance could be silently reversed overnight without public documentation, that the same model identifier produced radically different outputs depending on whether it was accessed via API or web interface, and that the most defensible response of refusing to validate pseudoscience appeared and then eroded across successive model versions. The authors conclude that a commercial model's stance on contested knowledge is not a stable property of the underlying model but rather a contingent outcome of deployment configurations such as system prompts, safety layers, and interface routing, and they argue this opacity constitutes a matter of public concern requiring new forms of epistemic accountability.
items.citation: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina. Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset
items.summary: This study investigated how much information routine cement characterization measurements contain for predicting the performance of CEM I Portland cement, and whether predictive models trained on data from some producers transfer reliably to others. The researchers applied machine learning attribution and producer-holdout tests to a large multi-producer dataset spanning European cement manufacturers, collected over nearly three decades, combining oxide chemistry, fineness, particle-size distribution, physical properties, and derived descriptors. Fineness emerged as the strongest single descriptor family for strength class and water demand, though oxide chemistry contributed a comparable signal when assessed jointly, and Blaine surface area measurements proved largely interchangeable with more detailed particle-size distribution representations. Strength class and water demand could be recovered from routine measurements, but early-strength designation could not be identified as a physically separable class because it arises from multiple interacting factors including fineness, sulfate–alkali chemistry, and plant practice. Producer-holdout tests showed that absolute prediction errors remained broadly consistent across held-out producers, while recovery of within-producer strength variation was producer-dependent, suggesting that fully capturing producer-specific behaviour may require additional compositional or microstructural characterization beyond routine measurements.
items.citation: Marchellino Ghorayeb, Christiane Rößler, Horst-Michael Ludwig et al.. Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fully Convergent Projection-based Methods with Momentum under Nonconvex Geometric
items.summary: This paper addresses nonlinear optimization problems subject to nonconvex but geometrically structured constraints, focusing on how to incorporate momentum terms into projected-gradient methods while preserving strong convergence guarantees. The authors identify a fundamental issue that arises when the negative gradient is naively replaced by a general descent direction in the projection-based framework, and they develop backtracking mechanisms applied to the pre-projection step to safely integrate momentum. Under weak regularity conditions and without smoothness assumptions, the proposed algorithms are shown to converge to Mordukhovich stationarity when the base directions asymptotically approach the negative gradient for small stepsizes, with stronger guarantees of Bouligand and Proximal stationarity achievable under more specific conditions on the search direction. The theoretical results are validated numerically on sparsity-constrained and bounded-rank constrained problems, where the momentum-enhanced method demonstrates improved computational performance by exploiting the additional curvature information provided by the momentum term.
items.citation: Matteo Lapucci, Diego Scuppa. Fully Convergent Projection-based Methods with Momentum under Nonconvex Geometric. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
items.summary: The paper introduces "bag-of-waves," an interpretable machine learning framework for analyzing electroencephalography signals without relying on predefined spectral features or opaque deep neural networks. The method learns a compact dictionary of recurring waveform templates (atoms) from unlabeled continuous EEG using shift-invariant k-means, then converts signals into token sequences whose statistical properties feed lightweight classifiers or clustering algorithms. The framework is extended to capture temporal context through atom-to-atom transition sequences (n-grams) and spatial structure through multichannel atoms spanning brain regions. The approach was evaluated on three datasets targeting distinct challenges: low-data single-channel clustering, multichannel dementia classification, and a large-scale six-way clinical event benchmark against strong deep learning and foundation model baselines. Across all settings the method achieved competitive performance while using far fewer parameters, and crucially recovered interpretable waveform morphologies recognizable to neurophysiologists, with particular advantages in low-data regimes where large models are poorly suited.
items.citation: Athanasios Papastathopoulos-Katsaros, Steven T. Lee, Lin Yao et al.. Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Association between menstrual-related disorders and sexually transmitted infections: A nationwide cross-sectional study in Japan.
items.summary: This nationwide cross-sectional study investigated whether menstrual-related disorders are associated with sexually transmitted infections among young women in Japan, and whether this relationship differs by disorder type or hormonal therapy use. Using a large insurance claims database, researchers identified women under forty with diagnoses of endometriosis or dysmenorrhea and compared the prevalence of five sexually transmitted infections against women without these conditions. Women with menstrual-related disorders had substantially higher prevalence of all examined sexually transmitted infections, with endometriosis showing the strongest association, particularly for genital chlamydia infection. Hormonal therapy use made little difference to the prevalence of sexually transmitted infections within the group of women with menstrual-related disorders. The authors conclude that sexually transmitted infection screening and reproductive health education should be integrated into routine gynecologic care for women with these conditions, while noting that healthcare-seeking behavior and diagnostic patterns may influence the observed associations.
items.citation: Yoshihara T, Owada S, Arita H et al.. Association between menstrual-related disorders and sexually transmitted infections: A nationwide cross-sectional study in Japan.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a CRISPR-Cas12a diagnostic assay for the rapid detection of *Shigella flexneri 2a*, the most prevalent cause of shigellosis and a major public health burden in resource-limited settings. The assay pairs recombinase polymerase amplification with Cas12a-mediated collateral cleavage, using two guide RNAs targeting serotype-specific genes to drive either fluorescence or lateral flow readout at room temperature within one hour. Analytical testing showed a detection limit of ten copies per microliter and complete specificity with no cross-reactivity to other bacteria, performance comparable to conventional PCR. Clinical validation against a large cohort of stool specimens demonstrated diagnostic sensitivity and specificity approaching those of PCR, without requiring specialized laboratory equipment. The authors conclude that the assay's speed, accuracy, and operational simplicity make it well suited for point-of-care diagnostics and field-based outbreak surveillance.
items.citation: Liao J, Su Y, Jiang F. CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.
items.summary: This review examined the translational progress of CRISPR-Cas systems across three major applications in infectious disease management: diagnostics, therapeutic genome editing, and vaccine development. The authors surveyed key platforms and strategies developed over the past decade, including rapid pathogen detection tools, CRISPR-based approaches to directly target viral genomes and address antimicrobial resistance, and the use of CRISPR-Cas9 in engineering live-attenuated and personalized neoantigen vaccines. The review found that diagnostic applications have advanced furthest toward clinical evaluation, with proof-of-concept tools progressing to preclinical stages, while therapeutic and personalized vaccine approaches remain at earlier, more exploratory phases. The authors attribute this uneven maturity to persistent challenges in delivery efficiency, off-target effects, and regulatory and ethical constraints that continue to hinder therapeutic translation. The review concludes that although CRISPR-Cas holds transformative potential for infectious disease management, these technical and governance barriers must be resolved to achieve safe and equitable clinical implementation.
items.citation: Mayuri K, Saravanan KM, Somala CS et al.. CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.. Biochemical genetics. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for accessible, decentralized testing capable of rapid pathogen identification outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors organized their analysis around the three core operational steps of such diagnostics: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. They surveyed extraction strategies including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic approaches, emphasizing designs that remain simple, rugged, and equipment-free. Key amplification methods were reviewed, including both thermal cycling and isothermal approaches that have been adapted for portable, low-power conditions, alongside a broad range of detection platforms spanning colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors employing CRISPR-Cas systems and toehold switch principles. The review concludes that these combined technological advances are driving point-of-care nucleic acid diagnostics toward increasingly sensitive, selective, programmable, and economically viable solutions for infectious disease detection beyond centralized facilities.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies for bacterial infections, with particular emphasis on their utility in the context of rising antimicrobial resistance. The authors conducted a structured comparative analysis of major platforms, including various forms of PCR, isothermal amplification, next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and digital PCR, evaluating each against parameters such as sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, turnaround time, and multiplexing capability. The review also critically assessed how artificial intelligence and machine learning are being integrated into diagnostic workflows to support resistance prediction and clinical decision-making. Additionally, the translational potential of these technologies for point-of-care deployment was discussed, accounting for clinical validation requirements and real-world operational constraints. The authors conclude that advancing culture-independent bacteriological diagnostics requires carefully balancing analytical performance with clinical interpretability, and they outline key challenges and future directions for the field.
items.citation: Cotelici AM, Bălășoiu AT, Boldeanu MV et al.. Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Wax-in-a-Tube: A Simple, Rapid, One-Pot Platform for Molecular Detection.
items.summary: This paper developed a one-pot molecular diagnostic platform that combines isothermal amplification with CRISPR-based detection to overcome the workflow limitations of conventional two-step assays. The researchers created a wax-in-a-tube system in which a molded wax separator physically partitions different reaction components within a single tube, melting away during thermal cycling to enable sequential reactions without manual mixing, centrifugation, or vortexing steps. The platform integrates recombinase polymerase amplification with CRISPR detection and was tested against HSV-2 DNA targets, achieving attomolar-level sensitivity comparable to standard two-step methods. Clinical validation using patient swab samples demonstrated performance on par with conventional PCR. The authors conclude that this approach offers a simple, rapid, contamination-minimized solution well suited for point-of-care infectious disease diagnostics.
items.citation: Hou C, Yang R, Guan X et al.. Wax-in-a-Tube: A Simple, Rapid, One-Pot Platform for Molecular Detection.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Topology-Gated λ Exonuclease Enables Amplification-Free Signal Boosting.
items.summary: This study investigated a previously unrecognized topological property of λ exonuclease, finding that duplex substrates with 5' phosphates at both termini can undergo self-sustained cyclic cleavage and reforming without external amplification. Through systematic biochemical and structural analyses, the researchers characterized this topology-gated mechanism and harnessed it by designing a dumbbell-shaped probe that conceals 5' phosphates within dual RNA hairpin loops until CRISPR/Cas13 target recognition cleaves the loops and exposes the phosphates, triggering the cyclic reaction. The resulting platform, called Topo-CRISPR, achieves attomolar sensitivity within a short timeframe and without preamplification steps. Applied to clinical samples, the system detected enterovirus RNA, a microRNA, and a circular RNA with performance comparable to conventional RT-qPCR, and was further extended to non-nucleic-acid targets through aptamer-based conformational gating. The work reframes λ exonuclease as a topology-driven cyclic signal transducer and provides a general framework for amplification-free ultrasensitive molecular diagnostics.
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.citation: Feng H, Wang Y, Zhao J et al.. Topology-Gated λ Exonuclease Enables Amplification-Free Signal Boosting.. Journal of the American Chemical Society. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, with an emphasis on translating laboratory advances into practical, field-deployable diagnostic tools. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic detection platforms, analyzing how innovations in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, which enables intelligent pattern recognition, real-time data analysis, and high-throughput multiplexing that transforms conventional detectors into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking ahead, the authors outline a vision for self-powered biosensors, modular multi-pathogen detection panels, blockchain-integrated data management, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly known as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive survey of innovations in chip design and fabrication—including three-dimensional printing, modular constructs, and flexible substrates—as well as the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of smart diagnostic platforms that can self-optimize, automate analysis, and support clinical decision-making. The review highlights clinical applications spanning cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also address persistent challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration, outlining future directions for translating these technologies into routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers
items.summary: This review examines extracellular vesicles as mediators of intercellular communication and their potential as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in human disease. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning the biogenesis, molecular composition, and classification of extracellular vesicle subtypes, alongside advances in their isolation, characterization, and omics-based profiling. The review pays particular attention to the roles of these vesicles in viral infection, inflammation, immune regulation, and cancer biology, while highlighting clinical applications of mesenchymal stem cell-derived vesicles in regenerative medicine and oncology. The authors also discuss the emerging use of photobiomodulation as a means of therapeutically modulating vesicle signaling. Critically, the review identifies key translational barriers including the need for standardization, scalability, and harmonized regulatory frameworks under oversight bodies such as the FDA and EMA, framing extracellular vesicles as promising next-generation platforms for precision medicine.
items.citation: Dragan Primorac, Petar Brlek, Luka Bulić et al.. Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Cell death in cancer
items.summary: This review paper examines the diverse cell death programs relevant to cancer biology and their implications for treatment. The authors survey how the field has expanded beyond apoptosis to encompass additional modalities including necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis, situating each within a unified framework of cancer development, progression, and therapeutic response. While apoptosis remains the predominant mechanism triggered by conventional radiation and chemotherapy, non-apoptotic programs are highlighted for their capacity to drive inflammatory responses and modulate interactions between tumor cells, stromal components, and the immune system, thereby influencing immunotherapy outcomes. Ferroptosis receives particular attention as a distinct iron-dependent, lipid peroxidation-driven modality that arises from metabolic perturbations rather than a canonical induction signal. The review ultimately addresses how resistance to cell death and immune suppression pose central challenges, framing the restoration of cancer cell death as a promising therapeutic strategy contingent on deeper mechanistic understanding.
items.citation: Marcus Conrad, Andreas Strasser, Philipp J. Jost et al.. Cell death in cancer. Cell. 2026

items.title: New approach methodologies for drug discovery
items.summary: This review examines the growing field of new approach methodologies as alternatives to traditional animal-based drug discovery, which suffers from persistently high failure rates. The authors survey recent advances in stem cell-based systems, organoids, and computational approaches, situating these developments within evolving regulatory frameworks from major health agencies. The review traces how these methodologies apply across the full drug-discovery continuum, from disease modeling and drug design through efficacy testing, and also considers their potential as therapeutic interventions in their own right. Key biological, technical, and regulatory bottlenecks limiting broader translational adoption are identified and discussed. The authors conclude by addressing societal considerations and outlining future human-centric pipelines they argue could fundamentally reshape drug discovery.
items.citation: Wenqiang Liu, Paul Pang, Catherine A. Wu et al.. New approach methodologies for drug discovery. Cell. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, which use light-activated mechanisms to treat a broad spectrum of diseases by leveraging the unique properties of nanomaterials to enhance therapeutic efficacy. The authors survey the core components, classification schemes, and delivery platforms—including gold nanoparticles, liposomes, and dendrimers—that enable improved light absorption, targeted reactive oxygen species generation in photodynamic therapy, and localized heating in photothermal therapy. At the molecular level, the review dissects how light-triggered interventions induce oxidative stress, activate apoptotic and autophagic pathways, and modulate immune responses, with relevance not only to cancer but also to cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune conditions. The authors also critically evaluate clinically approved agents and recent trial findings, identifying key translational obstacles such as nanoparticle optimization, effective light delivery to target tissues, and regulatory challenges. The review concludes that integrating molecular understanding with clinical progress positions nanoparticle-based phototherapy as a transformative noninvasive strategy with broad therapeutic potential.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of extending monocular 3D reconstruction to dynamic 4D scenes, where existing methods fail to capture the structured, collective nature of physical motion. The authors propose SM4RT, a Structured Motion 4D Reconstruction Transformer that represents scene dynamics through a "Structure-of-Motion" framework, decomposing motion into a compact set of rigid-body motion bases expressed as temporal sequences of six-dimensional twists in SE(3). Dense scene motion is recovered by assigning pixels to these bases with sparse, time-shared weights, ensuring that points belonging to the same physical object share a common rigid-body motion trajectory rather than moving independently. The model uses a parallel motion geometry encoder-decoder to jointly infer 3D geometry, world-coordinate motion, and kinematic structure in a single forward pass from monocular RGB video. SM4RT is reported to achieve strong motion reconstruction performance while maintaining the geometric structure inherent to physical scene motion.
items.citation: Shing Ho J. Lin, Wenzhao Zheng, Dong Zhuo et al.. SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties
items.summary: This paper presents a spectroscopic survey of young stellar objects in Sh2-284, a distant and metal-poor star-forming region located toward the Galactic anticenter, to investigate how reduced metallicity influences stellar and accretion properties during early stellar evolution. Candidate young stellar objects were identified using mid-infrared Spitzer photometry combined with optical and near-infrared data, and followed up with optical spectroscopy from the Large Binocular Telescope. The study employed a multi-diagnostic approach using nine emission line tracers spanning hydrogen Balmer lines, calcium infrared triplet lines, and Paschen series lines to derive accretion rates and compare them with those measured in nearby solar-metallicity star-forming regions. Tentative evidence was found for a flattening in the flux-flux relations of the metal-poor young stellar objects relative to solar-metallicity counterparts, a trend consistent across multiple diagnostics. The results demonstrate that disk accretion remains robust and efficiently sustained in this sub-solar metallicity environment, with the sample spanning a wide range of accretion rates and showing no fundamental suppression of gas accretion due to reduced metal content.
items.citation: Katia Biazzo, Juan Manuel Alcalá, Felice Cusano et al.. LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Critical Sensing with Autonomous Devices: The Self-Oscillation Threshold of a Frequency-Locked NV-Centre Magnetometer
items.summary: The paper investigates what happens when a nitrogen-vacancy ensemble magnetometer operating in frequency-modulation lock mode is deliberately pushed beyond the stability boundary of its feedback control loop. Rather than keeping the loop gain within the stable operating regime, the researchers drive the system through a period-doubling bifurcation by increasing the software loop gain, transforming the locked sensor into a self-sustained oscillator. They derive an analytical threshold condition relating the critical gain to the ratio of the transduction slope at calibration time versus its current value, providing a direct physical interpretation of the bifurcation point as a self-calibration diagnostic. An identifiability analysis characterizes what physical information this scalar threshold can and cannot distinguish, and the statistical properties of threshold estimators under realistic noise are examined. Experimental measurements confirm the predicted onset of the bifurcation and demonstrate sub-threshold critical fluctuations that diverge according to the theoretically predicted scaling, supporting the concept of using instability thresholds as a sensing resource in autonomous quantum devices.
items.citation: Joan Toledo Aguilera, Gonzalo Reina Rivero, Marcel Morillas-Rozas et al.. Critical Sensing with Autonomous Devices: The Self-Oscillation Threshold of a Frequency-Locked NV-Centre Magnetometer. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Is S301 the Captured Companion of the Hypervelocity Star S5-HVS1?
items.summary: This paper investigates whether a recently discovered star near the Galactic center, S301, could be the captured companion of the hypervelocity star S5-HVS1, the only known hypervelocity star with an unambiguous Galactic center origin. The Hills mechanism, which describes how a supermassive black hole disrupts a stellar binary, predicts two remnants: one star ejected at extreme velocity and one left tightly bound to the black hole. The authors use the known mass and velocity of S5-HVS1 to derive a constraint on the orbital properties of its putative captured companion, and find that S301's orbit and photometrically inferred mass satisfy this relation better than any other known S-star. A forward model comparing the Hills origin hypothesis against a null hypothesis confirms that S301's orbit is far more consistent with being S5-HVS1's companion than a typical S-star, though the overall Bayes factor remains near unity due to uncertainties in survival and detection probabilities. The authors conclude that S301 is a compelling but not yet confirmed candidate, and that definitive association will require improved mass measurements, chemical abundance comparisons, and better-calibrated observational selection functions.
items.citation: Andrea Caputo, Giovanni Maria Tomaselli. Is S301 the Captured Companion of the Hypervelocity Star S5-HVS1?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental design challenge in quantum machine learning: how to encode matrix-valued input data in a way that captures meaningful structural relationships rather than treating inputs element-wise. The authors introduce Quantum Spectral Models, which construct the generator of the data-encoding unitary directly from each input matrix, allowing the model's inductive bias to align with the spectral properties of the data. Three variants are studied, based on different Hamiltonian structures, whose outputs admit Fourier representations where input-dependent spectral gaps and subspaces shape both the frequency content and the coefficients of the learned function. Evaluating these models on digit recognition benchmarks and controlled synthetic tasks defined by spectral statistics, the proposed models outperform comparison quantum models at the largest tested circuit depths, with different variants excelling depending on whether the task requires sensitivity to spectral subspaces or spectral values alone. The results demonstrate that input-conditioned spectral representations can serve as an analysable and effective inductive bias in quantum machine learning, offering broader lessons for structure-aware model design.
items.citation: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers. Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of automating theoretical research in causal inference while ensuring reliable evaluation of generated results. The authors developed CausalForge, a framework that combines a foundational formal library for causal inference built in the Lean proof assistant with a self-improving agentic pipeline that selects research topics, proposes results, formalizes statements, and constructs machine-checked proofs. A key motivation was overcoming the unreliability of large language model reviewers, which can accept fabricated work at near-chance detection rates, by grounding evaluation in formal verification rather than LLM judgment alone. Because machine-checked proofs only confirm that a formal statement follows from its assumptions without guaranteeing the statement captures the intended scientific meaning, the framework supplements formal verification with a statement audit that compares each formal theorem against the informal claim it was meant to express. The system was evaluated using artifacts from completed autonomous research runs, offering a formally grounded approach to automated theoretical discovery in causal inference.
items.citation: Jiyuan Tan, Vasilis Syrgkanis. CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference. arXiv. 2026

A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of smart diagnostic platforms that can self-optimize, automate analysis, and support clinical decision-making. The review highlights applications across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, neuroscience diagnostics, and microbiome profiling. The authors also address persistent challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration, and outline future directions for translating these technologies into routine clinical and public health use.
