items.title: Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a low-cost, noninvasive electronic nose could detect SARS-CoV-2 infection as an alternative to conventional diagnostic methods that are often uncomfortable, slow, or inaccurate in early infection. The researchers built a device using an array of commercially available metal-oxide gas sensors designed to detect volatile organic compounds in both saliva and exhaled breath, which change in composition in the presence of the virus. Multiple machine learning algorithms were applied to the sensor data to distinguish between infected and non-infected individuals in a real-world hospital cohort. Classification accuracy varied across algorithms and sample types, with exhaled breath generally performing slightly better than saliva, and the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm achieving the best discrimination. The findings support proof-of-concept feasibility for this approach as a rapid, point-of-care screening tool for SARS-CoV-2 detection.
items.venue: The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases
items.citation: Fialkovitz G, Sousa PL, Hidifira AM et al.. Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.. The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Multiniche mycobiome profiling identifies distinctive fungal dysbiosis in common variable immunodeficiency.
items.summary: This study investigated the fungal microbiome (mycobiome) across multiple body compartments in patients with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), a condition previously associated with bacterial dysbiosis but not well characterized in terms of its fungal ecology. Using amplicon sequencing of saliva, sputum, and stool samples from adults with CVID and healthy controls, the researchers profiled fungal community composition and applied diversity analyses, differential abundance testing, and machine learning approaches. They found that mycobiome composition differed significantly between CVID patients and controls across all three sampled niches, with reduced fungal richness and evenness particularly in respiratory and oral samples. A consistent pattern of enrichment in opportunistic yeasts, most notably *Candida albicans*, accompanied by depletion of commensal and environmental taxa, was observed in both CVID subgroups regardless of whether patients had immune dysregulation or purely infectious manifestations. Machine learning models built on fungal profiles discriminated CVID patients from controls with high accuracy across niches, supporting the potential utility of mycobiome signatures as non-invasive biomarkers and implicating *C. albicans* as a possible pathobiont in this immunodeficiency.
items.citation: Cabanero-Navalon MD, Carda-Diéguez M, Mira A et al.. Multiniche mycobiome profiling identifies distinctive fungal dysbiosis in common variable immunodeficiency.. Frontiers in immunology. 2026

items.title: Extraoral Detection of Biomarkers and Pathogens in Saliva: Comprehensive, Panoramic Review.
items.summary: This paper reviews methods for detecting disease biomarkers and pathogens in human saliva through extraoral analysis, motivated by saliva's complex biological composition and the practical advantages of non-invasive sample collection. The authors systematically compared a broad range of detection platforms—including mass spectrometry, PCR, ELISA, electrochemical methods, and optical techniques such as fluorescence, surface plasmon resonance, and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy—by compiling limits of detection from a large body of analytical studies and clinical performance metrics from clinical investigations. Using cortisol as a focal analyte for comparing analytical sensitivity, electrochemical platforms, particularly voltammetric approaches, achieved the lowest limits of detection, outperforming immunoassay- and mass spectrometry-based methods. In clinical settings, direct SERS and ELISA demonstrated the strongest overall diagnostic performance in terms of balanced accuracy and area under the curve, with PCR and mass spectrometry performing comparably. The review concludes that while electrochemical and direct SERS methods show exceptional promise, broader clinical adoption of SERS in particular is contingent on resolving standardization challenges.
items.citation: Dyussupova A, Ilyas A, Boranova A et al.. Extraoral Detection of Biomarkers and Pathogens in Saliva: Comprehensive, Panoramic Review.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that facilitate long-term device comfort and seamless integration with the body, alongside multimodal sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. It also considers how artificial intelligence contributes to signal processing and predictive health insights when integrated with these sensing platforms. Despite notable progress, the review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and clinical interpretability of AI-generated outputs. Overall, the paper synthesizes current knowledge across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to outline both the capabilities and remaining obstacles in this field.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers
items.summary: This review examines extracellular vesicles as mediators of intercellular communication, covering their biogenesis, molecular composition, and therapeutic relevance across human diseases. The authors survey the major classes of extracellular vesicles, recent advances in their isolation and omics-based characterization, and their roles in viral infection, inflammation, immune regulation, and cancer biology. Particular attention is given to mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles in regenerative medicine and oncology, as well as the modulation of vesicle signaling through photobiomodulation. The review also addresses translational obstacles including standardization, scalability, and regulatory validation under frameworks such as those imposed by the FDA and EMA, arguing that harmonized quality controls and rigorous safety evaluation are prerequisites for clinical translation. Overall, the authors propose that extracellular vesicles hold transformative potential as next-generation diagnostic and therapeutic tools within precision medicine.
items.citation: Dragan Primorac, Petar Brlek, Luka Bulić et al.. Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Clinical Applications of Extracellular Vesicles: Promises and Pitfalls
items.summary: This narrative review examines the current state and future prospects of extracellular vesicles as clinical tools across a broad range of medical specialties. The authors surveyed the emerging roles of these membrane-bound nanoparticles — which transfer proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids between cells — in fields spanning oncology, neurology, cardiology, dermatology, and reproductive medicine, among others. The review highlights their appeal as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic carriers owing to their biocompatibility, stability in biological fluids, and capacity for targeted drug delivery and tissue regeneration, with exosomes drawing particular attention as nanocarriers for precision medicine. Despite this promise, the authors identify substantial barriers to clinical translation, including the lack of standardized isolation and characterization protocols, challenges in defining appropriate doses, and the need for GMP-compliant large-scale production and regulatory approval. The review concludes that sustained interdisciplinary collaboration and rigorous clinical testing will be necessary before extracellular vesicles can be established as transformative instruments in personalized healthcare.
items.citation: Dragan Primorac, Petar Brlek, Luka Bulić et al.. Clinical Applications of Extracellular Vesicles: Promises and Pitfalls. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Gastroduodenal Disorders
items.summary: This paper presents a classification framework for gastroduodenal disorders, focusing on symptoms attributable to the gastroduodenal region. The authors organized these disorders into five categories: functional dyspepsia, nausea and vomiting disorders, excessive belching disorders, inability to belch syndrome, and rumination syndrome. Each category is further defined by its clinical characteristics and, where applicable, divided into subcategories based on symptom patterns or underlying mechanisms. Notable inclusions are cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome within the nausea and vomiting disorders and the inability to belch syndrome as a newly recognized category. The abstract is primarily classificatory in nature, offering a structured diagnostic taxonomy rather than reporting findings from an empirical study.
items.citation: H. Tornblom, Florencia Carbone, William L. Hasler et al.. Gastroduodenal Disorders. Gastroenterology. 2026

items.title: The Oral Microbiome and Systemic Health: Current Insights into the Mouth–Body Connection
items.summary: This narrative review examined the relationship between the oral microbiome and systemic health, focusing on how disturbances in oral microbial communities may contribute to diseases beyond the oral cavity. The authors conducted a comprehensive search across multiple databases, covering studies from roughly the past six years and ultimately synthesizing findings from selected articles spanning systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and mechanistic studies. The review found clear associations between oral dysbiosis and cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic respiratory infections, and adverse pregnancy outcomes, with emerging links also identified for neurodegenerative disorders, chronic kidney disease, autoimmune conditions, and cancer. Proposed mechanisms underlying these connections include bacteraemia, systemic inflammation driven by microbial metabolites and endotoxins, immune homeostasis disruption, molecular mimicry, and modulation of host metabolic pathways. The authors caution that most evidence remains observational, leaving causal relationships unestablished, and call for longitudinal and interventional research to clarify how targeting oral microbial activity might inform systemic disease prevention and treatment.
items.citation: Ana Glavina, Dora Martić, Mark Perko et al.. The Oral Microbiome and Systemic Health: Current Insights into the Mouth–Body Connection. Life. 2026

items.title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of extending monocular 3D reconstruction to dynamic 4D scenes, where existing approaches inadequately model motion by treating each point as moving independently rather than capturing the rigid-body structure inherent in physical objects. The authors propose SM4RT, a Structured Motion 4D Reconstruction Transformer that represents scene dynamics through a "Structure-of-Motion" framework, decomposing motion into a compact set of bases expressed as temporal sequences of rigid-body transformations in SE(3), with per-pixel assignment weights linking scene points to these shared motion trajectories. The model features a parallel encoder-decoder architecture that jointly infers 3D geometry, world-coordinate motion, and kinematic scene structure in a single forward pass from monocular RGB video. By enforcing that points on the same object share a common rigid-body motion trajectory, SM4RT explicitly captures the structured, collective nature of physical motion rather than unstructured point-wise displacements. The authors report that SM4RT achieves strong motion reconstruction performance while preserving the geometric structure of scene motion.
items.citation: Shing Ho J. Lin, Wenzhao Zheng, Dong Zhuo et al.. SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties
items.summary: This study conducted a spectroscopic survey of young stellar objects in Sh2-284, a distant and metal-poor star-forming region located toward the Galactic anticenter, to investigate how reduced metallicity influences stellar accretion and disk evolution. Candidate young stellar objects were identified using infrared photometry and then observed with a multi-object spectrograph at the Large Binocular Telescope, representing the first wide-field spectroscopic investigation of this region. The researchers characterized stellar and accretion properties across a range of stellar masses using nine independent emission-line diagnostics, and provided preliminary estimates of iron and lithium abundances for select targets. Comparing their results to solar-metallicity star-forming regions, they found tentative evidence for a flattening in flux-flux relations among the metal-poor sample, suggesting subtle metallicity-driven differences in accretion behavior. Overall, the study concludes that gas accretion can be efficiently sustained in sub-solar metallicity environments, with the surveyed objects displaying a broad range of accretion rates and robust accretion activity.
items.citation: Katia Biazzo, Juan Manuel Alcalá, Felice Cusano et al.. LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up
items.summary: This paper investigates a conjecture about the mass scaling behavior of light particle towers that appear near the core of effective field theory (EFT) strings in four-dimensional theories with minimal supersymmetry. The Integral Scaling Conjecture proposes that the exponent governing how tower masses scale with string tension takes only the integer values one, two, or three, and the authors set out to derive this from the bottom-up using the brane-taxonomy framework associated with the Emergent String Conjecture. By classifying duality frames into dozens of distinct classes and systematically identifying candidate EFT strings on charge lattices, they exhaustively test integral scaling across all such candidates. They find that integral scaling holds for all leading towers and also for subleading towers below the species scale, with minor half-integral subtleties that also arise in explicit top-down constructions, and they further find evidence that oscillator modes of EFT string candidates generate the full lattices of particles and strings. The results are compared against concrete string theory compactifications, and a noteworthy asymmetry is uncovered: the exponent value of one implies a perturbative string limit, but a perturbative string limit does not conversely require this value.
items.citation: Muldrow Etheredge, Alvaro Herráez, Dieter Lüst et al.. Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental design challenge in quantum machine learning: how to encode matrix-valued input data in a way that captures meaningful matrix-level structure rather than treating inputs element-wise. The authors introduce Quantum Spectral Models, which construct the generator of the data-encoding unitary directly from each input matrix, rather than using conventional coordinate-wise rotation-gate encodings. Three variants are studied, differing in how they partition the Hamiltonian structure, and their outputs are analyzed as truncated Fourier representations where input-dependent spectral gaps and subspaces determine the frequency content and coefficients respectively. The models are benchmarked on handwriting digit data represented as matrices and on synthetic tasks explicitly defined by spectral statistics, where the proposed variants outperform comparison quantum models at the largest evaluated circuit depths. Ablation studies reveal a task-dependent distinction between the contributions of spectral values and spectral subspaces, suggesting that input-conditioned spectral representations provide an interpretable and structure-aware inductive bias for quantum machine learning.
items.citation: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers. Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
items.summary: This paper investigated whether commercial large language models provide consistent and transparent evaluations of pseudoscientific claims, focusing on ethnonationalist content derived from a specific biosocial framework. The researchers systematically tested four major model families through both API and web interfaces across multiple temporal snapshots, measuring how each model rated the credibility of these contested claims. One model family's default consumer-facing versions consistently assigned credibility scores dramatically higher than all other models tested, a disparity that did not appear when the same models evaluated uncontested scientific claims, suggesting the divergence was specific to pseudoscientific content rather than a general calibration difference. The study also documented that a model's epistemic stance could reverse overnight without public acknowledgment, and that the same model identifier produced radically different outputs depending on whether it was accessed via API or web interface. The authors conclude that a commercial model's position on contested knowledge is not a stable property of the underlying model but rather an artifact of opaque deployment configurations—including system prompts, safety layers, and undisclosed updates—and argue this instability constitutes a matter requiring formal epistemic accountability.
items.citation: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina. Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset
items.summary: This study investigated how much information about cement performance can be reliably extracted from routine quality control measurements and whether that information transfers across different cement producers. The researchers assembled a large dataset of CEM I cement records from numerous European producers, collected in a single laboratory over nearly three decades, combining oxide chemistry, fineness, particle-size distribution, physical properties, and derived descriptors with machine learning attribution and producer-holdout validation. Fineness emerged as the strongest single descriptor family for predicting strength class and water demand, though oxide chemistry contributed a comparable signal when both were used together, and Blaine surface area and compact particle-size distribution representations proved largely interchangeable. Strength class and water demand could be reliably recovered from routine data, but early-strength designation could not be resolved as a physically distinct class because it arises from multiple interacting factors including fineness, sulfate-alkali chemistry, and plant practice. Producer-holdout tests showed that absolute prediction errors were broadly consistent across held-out producers, yet recovery of within-producer strength variation was producer-dependent, suggesting that capturing finer-grained producer-specific behavior may require more detailed phase speciation beyond routine characterization.
items.citation: Marchellino Ghorayeb, Christiane Rößler, Horst-Michael Ludwig et al.. Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the need for accessible, decentralized testing capable of rapid pathogen identification outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors structured their analysis around the three core operational steps of such diagnostics: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluated approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, emphasizing designs that are simplified, rugged, and equipment-free. For amplification, they reviewed established and modified techniques such as PCR, NASBA, RPA, and LAMP, highlighting adaptations that enable rapid, low-power, and portable operation. Finally, they surveyed detection platforms ranging from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors employing CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch mechanisms, which offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition suitable for point-of-care deployment.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.
items.summary: The paper evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A assay, a rapid quantitative PCR test originally designed for throat swabs, when applied to pediatric pleural fluid specimens for detecting Group A Streptococcus in the context of invasive disease. Researchers compared the assay against a composite reference standard comprising bacterial culture and a laboratory-developed PCR targeting a different gene, using a convenience sample of pleural fluid specimens from children. The Xpert assay detected all positive specimens, achieving perfect agreement with the composite reference standard and the laboratory-developed PCR, whereas culture alone identified only a minority of positive cases. These findings demonstrate that the Xpert assay is substantially more sensitive than culture for identifying Group A Streptococcus in pleural fluid, likely because many patients had received antibiotics before sample collection. The authors conclude that the assay offers both superior sensitivity and faster turnaround time, supporting its clinical utility for guiding therapy and enabling timely public health responses to invasive Group A streptococcal infections.
items.citation: Amaral G, Gadkar VJ, Almodahka A et al.. Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Microbiota in cancer: current understandings and future perspectives
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between the microbiota and cancer, covering how microbial communities influence carcinogenesis, tumor progression, and patient prognosis. The authors trace the historical development of this research field and investigate the molecular mechanisms by which microbiota modulate oncogenic pathways, immune responses, and tumor metabolism. The review addresses the dual nature of the microbiota as both a promoter and inhibitor of cancer, and explores how microbial communities affect responses to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Emerging therapeutic strategies that target the microbiota, including probiotics, antibiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation, are discussed alongside approved drugs and ongoing clinical trials. The authors conclude by advocating for personalized approaches to exploit the anticancer potential of the microbiota and propose a comprehensive framework to guide future research and clinical applications in this area.
items.citation: Yanxi Yao, Yifei Zhu, Keji Chen et al.. Microbiota in cancer: current understandings and future perspectives. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide as a multifunctional two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, focusing on its synthesis chemistry, property modification, and potential across energy, environmental, and healthcare applications. The authors surveyed the material's distinctive layered architecture, which enables extensive surface functionalization and tunable properties spanning a wide range of dimensional configurations and surface chemistries. The review covers applications including photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and microplastics, energy storage and conversion technologies such as hydrogen production and battery systems, and advanced sensing platforms including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for biological and environmental detection. The authors conclude that graphene oxide holds transformative technological potential as a standalone material, demonstrating versatile performance across diverse scientific domains. However, the review also identifies persistent challenges including scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility that must be resolved before its full industrial and real-world deployment can be realized.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: Interplay of Microbiome, Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Health and Disease
items.summary: This review examines the complex relationships among the human microbiome, oxidative stress, and inflammation in the context of both health and disease. The authors synthesized current evidence on how microbial metabolites and specific probiotic strains help maintain redox homeostasis through pathways including immune regulation, modulation of inflammatory processes, and influences on mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production and antioxidant signaling. Conversely, oxidative stress and inflammation can alter microbial diversity and function, creating a feedback loop that further disrupts homeostasis. The paper highlights how these bidirectional interactions are shaped by various environmental and biological factors, and how their dysregulation is thought to promote the development of multiple diseases. Overall, the review underscores that the interplay among these three systems is increasingly recognized as central to understanding both physiological regulation and pathological states.
items.citation: Lourdes Herrera-Quintana, Pablo Iturbe-Sanz, Jorge Olivares-Arancibia et al.. Interplay of Microbiome, Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Health and Disease. Antioxidants. 2026

items.title: Health Effects of Bee Products: A Comprehensive Review
items.summary: This review paper examined the health-related properties and therapeutic mechanisms of eight bee-derived products used in apitherapy, including honey, propolis, royal jelly, and bee venom, among others. The authors surveyed existing evidence on how these products exert biological activities such as antibacterial, antiviral, antifungal, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antitumor, and cardiovascular effects, attributing these properties to their rich content of amino acids, fatty acids, flavonoids, polyphenols, and other bioactive compounds. The review found that bee products show promise in supporting the immune system and positively influencing conditions such as cancer, diabetes, and cardiovascular and neurological diseases linked to oxidative stress. However, the authors conclude that a lack of standardization across bee products limits the clarity and comparability of existing studies. They call for future clinical trials using standardized preparations with defined dosages and durations, as well as epidemiological studies, to more rigorously establish the health impacts of these substances in humans.
items.citation: Nevin Sanlier, Elif Yildiz Kaya, Ikbal Irem Yucel. Health Effects of Bee Products: A Comprehensive Review. Food Science & Nutrition. 2026

items.title: Digital Biomarkers for Precision Early Detection of Lung Cancer: Integrating <scp>AI</scp> ‐Driven Multi‐Omics Into Clinical Pathways
items.summary: This review examined the current landscape of digital biomarkers and artificial intelligence approaches for the early detection of lung cancer, which remains the top cause of cancer-related mortality globally. The authors systematically evaluated biomarkers spanning multiple omics layers—including genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiomics—alongside machine learning and deep learning methods for integrating these complex datasets. They found that multi-omics strategies are accelerating the identification of molecular signatures relevant to early-stage disease, with AI enabling risk stratification, diagnostic refinement, histological subtyping, and treatment planning from high-dimensional data. Despite this promise, the review identifies substantial barriers to clinical translation, including data heterogeneity across centres, limited model interpretability, regulatory challenges, and insufficient prospective validation. The authors conclude that emerging approaches such as single-cell and spatial multi-omics combined with federated learning frameworks could help bridge the gap between computational discovery and real-world clinical implementation of personalised early detection strategies.
items.citation: Fan Bu, Zhi‐Qiang Ling. Digital Biomarkers for Precision Early Detection of Lung Cancer: Integrating <scp>AI</scp> ‐Driven Multi‐Omics Into Clinical Pathways. Cancer Medicine. 2026

items.title: LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties
items.summary: This study investigated the stellar and accretion properties of young stellar objects in Sh2-284, a distant and metal-poor star-forming region located toward the Galactic anticenter. Candidate young stellar objects were identified through mid-infrared Spitzer photometry combined with optical and near-infrared data, then followed up with wide-field optical spectroscopy using the Large Binocular Telescope. The researchers characterized disk-bearing stars across a range of stellar masses, employing multiple emission-line diagnostics spanning hydrogen Balmer lines, calcium infrared triplet lines, and Paschen series lines to derive accretion rates and compare them with solar-metallicity star-forming regions. A tentative flattening in flux-flux relations was found for the metal-poor sample relative to solar-metallicity counterparts, a trend consistent across multiple accretion diagnostics. The results demonstrate that robust gas accretion onto young stars can be sustained in sub-solar metallicity environments, with measured accretion rates spanning several orders of magnitude and a median comparable to those seen in nearby star-forming regions.
items.citation: Katia Biazzo, Juan Manuel Alcalá, Felice Cusano et al.. LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Supermoiré-trapped quadrupolar exciton
items.summary: The paper investigates quadrupolar excitons in van der Waals heterotrilayer systems, where extending beyond bilayers creates multipolar excitons formed as superpositions of vertically aligned phase-coherent interlayer excitons. A key experimental challenge is that unintentional twist-angle mismatches between layers weaken the vertical Coulomb coupling needed to form these states. The authors propose that the supermoiré effect — arising from the interference of moiré patterns at successive interfaces — naturally creates periodic pockets of well-aligned atomic registries that trap quadrupolar excitons, partially circumventing the need for precise angle alignment. Using a specific tungsten-based heterotrilayer stack, they demonstrate that interactions between confined levels at the top and bottom moiré interfaces produce electric-field-tunable bright and dark hybridized quadrupolar states. This finding highlights the supermoiré effect as a constructive mechanism for stabilizing complex excitonic states in multilayer heterostructures and opens avenues for exploring higher-order multipolar excitons without stringent fabrication constraints.
items.citation: Anish Kumar, Suman Chatterjee, Kenji Watanabe et al.. Supermoiré-trapped quadrupolar exciton. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Optomechanical systems with a Fano membrane in the middle
items.summary: This paper investigates cavity optomechanical systems in which a conventional dielectric membrane is replaced by a photonic-crystal Fano membrane placed at the center of a Fabry-Pérot cavity. Unlike a standard membrane, the photonic-crystal membrane supports a localized optical resonance that hybridizes with the cavity field, enabling spectral engineering of the optical modes beyond what is possible in conventional membrane-in-the-middle systems. The membrane's mechanical motion couples to the system both through the usual dispersive optomechanical mechanism and by modifying the Fano-mode resonance itself, and the authors analyze two limiting regimes depending on membrane reflectivity, finding that only the symmetric cavity mode hybridizes with the Fano mode while the antisymmetric mode remains decoupled. Using quantum Langevin equations combined with a transfer-matrix description of optical scattering, the authors show that Fano-induced hybridization can produce narrow optical normal modes that remain efficiently driven by an external field under experimentally realistic conditions. These narrow modes effectively provide sideband resolution even when the bare cavity is in the unresolved-sideband regime, enabling ground-state cooling of the membrane motion and establishing Fano membrane-in-the-middle systems as a versatile platform for optomechanical and spectral engineering.
items.citation: Lei Du, Aymeric Frerejean, Witlef Wieczorek et al.. Optomechanical systems with a Fano membrane in the middle. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
items.summary: This paper investigates the application of explainability techniques to reinforcement learning in the safety-critical domain of air traffic control, motivated by the need to build trust in AI systems operating in high-stakes environments. The researchers trained a reinforcement learning agent in a simplified air traffic control environment to make routing decisions that avoid no-fly zones. To shed light on the agent's decision-making process, saliency maps were employed as a preliminary explainability method, highlighting which input features most strongly influenced the agent's actions. The work represents an initial step toward making AI-driven air traffic control assistance more transparent and interpretable, with the broader goal of supporting human-AI collaboration and higher levels of automation in aviation.
items.citation: Anduel Mehmeti, Gabriella Gigante, Salvatore Venticinque. Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Gridnberg: A Topography-Aware Pedestrian Routing Dataset for New York City
items.summary: This paper addresses the common simplification in urban network analysis of treating city streets as flat, which distorts route modeling and accessibility assessments in hilly terrain. The authors created a topography-aware pedestrian routing dataset for New York City called Gridnberg, which enriches an existing pedestrian network with vertex-level elevation data derived from a municipal planimetric database. The workflow spatially averages nearby elevation observations for each network vertex and computes direction-specific cumulative ascent and descent along segments to derive three routing cost metrics: horizontal distance, a comfort-oriented slope score, and an accessibility-sensitive slope score. Nearly all source segments were retained in the final dataset, demonstrating high coverage. The dataset is intended to support reproducible, terrain-aware pedestrian network analysis and improved accessibility modeling in New York City and potentially other urban environments.
items.citation: Ariel Noyman. Gridnberg: A Topography-Aware Pedestrian Routing Dataset for New York City. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up
items.summary: This paper investigates the Integral Scaling Conjecture, which posits that near the core of an effective field theory (EFT) string in a four-dimensional theory with minimal supersymmetry, a tower of states becomes light with its mass scaling with the string tension in a constrained way, specifically that the scaling exponent takes only integer values. The authors approach this conjecture from the bottom-up perspective by leveraging the brane-taxonomy rules associated with the Emergent String Conjecture, classifying the relevant duality frames into dozens of distinct classes and identifying which lattice sites qualify as viable EFT string candidates. Through an exhaustive test across all such candidates, they find that integral scaling holds for all leading towers as well as subleading towers below the species scale, with the exponent bounded as required, modulo some half-integral subtleties that also arise in explicit top-down constructions. Additional findings include evidence that oscillator modes of EFT string candidates generate the lattices of particles and strings, and that while a scaling exponent of one implies a perturbative string limit, the reverse implication does not hold. The results are compared against concrete string theory compactifications, providing consistency checks between the bottom-up classification and known top-down examples.
items.citation: Muldrow Etheredge, Alvaro Herráez, Dieter Lüst et al.. Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Innovative epitope-based ELISA assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women.
items.summary: The paper investigated three synthetic peptide epitopes derived from *Streptococcus agalactiae* proteins—GroEL, enolase, and EF-Tu—as potential components of an ELISA-based immunodiagnostic test for detecting Group B Streptococcus (GBS) carriage in pregnant women. The researchers developed prototype assays using these epitopes individually and in combinations, measuring IgG, IgM, and IgA antibody responses in serum samples from GBS-positive and GBS-negative subjects. All three epitopes, whether used alone or mixed, significantly distinguished between the two groups, with the enolase- and EF-Tu-derived peptides performing best as individual candidates due to their higher immunoreactivity at lower concentrations. Combining the epitopes in various mixtures further improved overall immunoreactivity, suggesting a synergistic diagnostic benefit. The authors propose this epitope-based ELISA as a promising alternative to the current culture-based gold standard, which is time-consuming and can yield ambiguous results.
items.citation: Brzychczy-Włoch M, Dobrut A, Drożdż K et al.. Innovative epitope-based ELISA assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women.. Applied microbiology and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Bridging the diagnostic gap: the role of culture methods in the era of syndromic panels for central nervous system infections.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a syndromic molecular panel for central nervous system infections by comparing it against conventional culture methods using cerebrospinal fluid samples collected over three years at a national reference center. The researchers assessed concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values across a large dataset of paired molecular and culture results. They found moderate overall agreement between the two approaches, with the syndromic panel demonstrating high specificity but limited sensitivity when all culture-identified pathogens were considered; however, when analysis was restricted to bacterial targets actually included in the panel, sensitivity and agreement improved substantially. Critically, conventional culture detected clinically relevant pathogens absent from the syndromic panel, including organisms such as Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes, underscoring that the panel cannot serve as a standalone diagnostic tool. The authors conclude that optimal management of central nervous system infections requires systematic integration of syndromic molecular testing with conventional culture, and they call for next-generation multiplex platforms with broader pathogen coverage guided by real-world epidemiological data.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Sberna G, D'Arezzo S, Valli MB et al.. Bridging the diagnostic gap: the role of culture methods in the era of syndromic panels for central nervous system infections.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-positive blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the LIAISON PLEX Gram-Positive Blood Culture Assay, a multiplexed molecular test designed to rapidly detect and differentiate gram-positive bacterial pathogens and antibiotic resistance markers directly from positive blood culture bottles. The assay was assessed across multiple sites using a combination of prospective clinical samples, pre-selected samples, and contrived specimens, along with inclusivity and cross-reactivity panels. The assay demonstrated very high overall sensitivity and specificity for identifying the targeted gram-positive organisms and resistance markers, with a near-perfect valid test rate. Performance was maintained across different blood culture bottle types from multiple manufacturers, in the presence of potential interfering substances, and in polymicrobial infection scenarios. The authors conclude that the assay offers fast, accurate, and reliable detection of gram-positive pathogens and their resistance genes, with potential to support antibiotic stewardship and timely patient management in bloodstream infection care.
items.citation: Chow S-K, Stevig C, Granato P et al.. Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-positive blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Validation of an in-house developed rapid assay for Group B Streptococcus detection in pregnancy.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for faster and simpler detection of Group B Streptococcus colonization in pregnant women, which poses serious risks of neonatal infection and preterm stillbirth. The researchers developed and validated an in-house rapid diagnostic assay combining CRISPR/Cas12a technology with recombinase polymerase amplification, allowing isothermal nucleic acid detection without complex laboratory equipment. The assay was evaluated for specificity against other common reproductive tract pathogens, its detection limit was established using serially diluted plasmid standards, and its clinical performance was assessed against a commercial quantitative real-time PCR method using vaginal-rectal swabs from pregnant women. The platform completed testing within one hour and produced results interpretable either by visual inspection of colloidal gold test strips or with a fluorescence reader, demonstrating high specificity and a low detection limit. The assay showed strong agreement with the established PCR reference method in clinical samples, supporting its potential utility as a rapid, accessible tool for prenatal GBS screening.
items.venue: International journal of medical microbiology : IJMM
items.citation: Hu S, Xie J, Liu L et al.. Validation of an in-house developed rapid assay for Group B Streptococcus detection in pregnancy.. International journal of medical microbiology : IJMM. 2026

items.title: Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance and real-world clinical utility of multiplex polymerase chain reaction panels designed to detect multiple pathogens simultaneously from cerebrospinal fluid in patients with suspected meningitis or encephalitis. Researchers retrospectively reviewed cerebrospinal fluid samples tested with these panels over a five-year period at a tertiary care hospital, examining test results, co-detections, repeat testing patterns, and whether positive results led to documented changes in diagnosis or treatment. Viral pathogens dominated the positive findings, with human herpesvirus-6, enterovirus, and herpes simplex virus type-1 most frequently identified, while Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most common bacterial detection, and co-detections occurred in a notable proportion of positive cases. Despite the panels' capacity for rapid pathogen identification, fewer than half of positive results were associated with a clinically relevant action, repeat testing after an initial negative yielded little additional diagnostic benefit, and some tests were ordered for conditions outside the panels' scope. The authors conclude that while these multiplex panels offer clear advantages for rapid detection, inappropriate utilisation and insufficient clinician familiarity with panel contents limit their clinical impact, underscoring the need for clearer testing criteria and improved education.
items.venue: The Indian journal of medical research
items.citation: Gürler M, Karaoğlu Ç, Yurtcu EE et al.. Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections.. The Indian journal of medical research. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review paper examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technologies, commonly called lab-on-a-chip systems, and their expanding role in laboratory medicine. The authors surveyed innovations in chip design and fabrication approaches, including three-dimensional printing and modular or flexible substrates, alongside the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled so-called smart diagnostic platforms capable of self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support. The review finds that these combined advances have broadened clinical applicability across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also address persistent challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration, and outline future directions for translating these technologies into routine clinical and public health use.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for rapid, decentralized testing outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors organized their analysis around the three core operational steps of such diagnostics: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluated approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, emphasizing their suitability for simplified and equipment-free deployment. For amplification, they reviewed how established methods such as PCR, NASBA, RPA, and LAMP have been adapted for portable, low-power, and rapid use. On the detection side, they surveyed platforms ranging from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors leveraging CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles, concluding that these emerging technologies offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition for point-of-care applications.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: A Novel Voltammetric Point-of-Care Device for Rapid and Accurate Nucleic Acid and Viral Pathogen Detection.
items.summary: This paper investigated an electrochemical approach to nucleic acid detection for rapid infectious disease diagnostics, motivated by the limitations of existing methods such as lateral flow assays and optically detected isothermal amplification. The researchers developed a device combining loop-mediated isothermal amplification with real-time voltammetric detection, where amplification-associated proton release is monitored through redox probing of a pH-sensing compound. The system was evaluated against multiple respiratory pathogens including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B viruses, RSV A, and equine herpesvirus, using both purified RNA from clinical samples and an extraction-free workflow with nasal swabs. The method demonstrated high concordance with RT-qPCR across tested sample types and pathogens, achieving a low limit of detection for influenza A virus. The authors conclude that real-time voltammetric LAMP is feasible across diverse sample types, while acknowledging that broader point-of-care validation in additional matrices and prospective cohorts is still needed.
items.citation: Munita R, Lyttleton R, Danefur E et al.. A Novel Voltammetric Point-of-Care Device for Rapid and Accurate Nucleic Acid and Viral Pathogen Detection.. ACS omega. 2026

items.title: Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies for bacterial infections, with a focus on improving the speed and accuracy of etiological diagnosis in the context of rising antimicrobial resistance. The authors conducted a structured comparative analysis of major platforms, including various forms of PCR, isothermal amplification, next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and digital PCR, evaluating each against key performance metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, turnaround time, and multiplexing capacity. The review also critically assessed the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into diagnostic workflows to support antimicrobial resistance prediction and clinical decision-making. Additionally, the translational potential of these technologies for point-of-care deployment was discussed, weighing clinical validation requirements and real-world operational constraints. The authors conclude that advancing culture-independent bacteriological diagnostics requires carefully balancing analytical performance with clinical interpretability, and they outline remaining challenges and future directions for the field.
items.citation: Cotelici AM, Bălășoiu AT, Boldeanu MV et al.. Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: A nested PCR-based point-of-care multiplex test for detection of bacterial pathogens in cerebrospinal fluids.
items.summary: This study developed and evaluated a multiplexed one-tube nested real-time PCR assay integrated with a point-of-care testing instrument for detecting three bacterial pathogens—*Streptococcus pneumoniae*, *Streptococcus agalactiae*, and *Streptococcus pyogenes*—directly from cerebrospinal fluid. The assay was designed to achieve a fully automated sample-to-result workflow without requiring culture, and its sensitivity and specificity were characterized using plasmid standards and common CSF pathogens before being tested on both simulated and clinical samples. The point-of-care system matched or exceeded the detection limits achieved with manual nucleic acid extraction while substantially reducing total testing time, and when applied to clinical samples it identified additional positive cases that conventional real-time PCR had missed. The authors conclude that the integrated system offers a simpler, faster, and more sensitive approach to diagnosing bacterial meningitis compared to standard PCR-based methods.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Wu J, Zhao Z, Pang P et al.. A nested PCR-based point-of-care multiplex test for detection of bacterial pathogens in cerebrospinal fluids.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Isothermal nucleic acid amplification techniques: A comprehensive overview on their principle & applications as alternative to PCR.
items.summary: This review paper examined isothermal nucleic acid amplification methods as alternatives to conventional PCR-based diagnostics. The authors surveyed a range of established techniques, including loop-mediated isothermal amplification, helicase-dependent amplification, rolling circle amplification, strand displacement amplification, nucleic acid sequence-based amplification, and recombinase polymerase amplification, all of which operate at a constant temperature without requiring a thermal cycler. The paper synthesized information on each technique's underlying reaction principles, product detection strategies, and practical applications in disease diagnosis, addressing a gap in the literature where no single comprehensive review had previously covered these elements together. The authors conclude that isothermal amplification methods offer significant advantages in speed, simplicity, and cost-effectiveness, making them particularly well suited for molecular diagnostics in resource-limited settings. The review also outlines future perspectives for these technologies in expanding access to genomic testing across research and clinical contexts.
items.citation: Amare Amdiyee A, Sisay Tessema T. Isothermal nucleic acid amplification techniques: A comprehensive overview on their principle & applications as alternative to PCR.. Practical laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: A Multiplex One-Tube Nested Real-Time PCR Assay for the Point-of-Care Testing of Infectious Meningitis.
items.summary: This study developed a multiplex one-tube nested real-time PCR assay integrated with a portable, fully automated point-of-care testing platform for detecting three key meningitis pathogens — *Haemophilus influenzae*, *Listeria monocytogenes*, and *Cryptococcus neoformans* — directly from cerebrospinal fluid samples. The closed-system nested amplification design was intended to reduce contamination risk and operational complexity compared with conventional approaches. Analytical testing demonstrated very low detection limits, no cross-reactivity against a broad panel of non-target microorganisms, and maintained sensitivity in simulated cerebrospinal fluid. Clinical evaluation against conventional quantitative PCR using patient samples showed near-perfect agreement, with the new assay additionally detecting *C. neoformans* cases missed by standard qPCR, suggesting superior sensitivity in a clinical setting. The assay delivers results in under two hours, supporting its potential as a rapid, sensitive, and practical tool for point-of-care meningitis diagnostics, though the authors note that validation in larger patient cohorts is still needed.
items.citation: Zhang D, Wang J, Zhao Z et al.. A Multiplex One-Tube Nested Real-Time PCR Assay for the Point-of-Care Testing of Infectious Meningitis.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Data-Centric Foundation Models in Computational Healthcare: A Survey
items.summary: This survey examines the intersection of foundation models and computational healthcare through a data-centric lens, focusing on how these models can address persistent challenges in clinical data acquisition, quality, and processing. The authors review a broad range of data-centric approaches spanning the full pipeline from model pre-training through inference, considering issues such as data quantity, annotation, patient privacy, and ethics. The survey also addresses critical concerns around AI security, evaluation, and alignment with human values as they apply to healthcare settings. The authors conclude with an outlook on how foundation model-based analytics may improve patient outcomes and clinical workflows, and provide a curated repository of healthcare-relevant foundation models and datasets.
items.citation: Yunkun Zhang, Jin Gao, Zheling Tan et al.. Data-Centric Foundation Models in Computational Healthcare: A Survey. ACM Computing Surveys. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, with particular emphasis on clinical and food safety applications. The authors surveyed advances across electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, evaluating how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity and specificity in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transform conventional sensors into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically assesses practical challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability limitations, and the absence of regulatory standardization, proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-based data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward deployable, regulation-ready food safety monitoring systems.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Virulence arsenal of Acinetobacter baumannii: mechanisms driving persistence and resistance
items.summary: This review examines the virulence and antimicrobial resistance mechanisms of *Acinetobacter baumannii*, a Gram-negative opportunistic pathogen responsible for a range of serious healthcare-associated infections. The authors surveyed the molecular structures and systems that enable the bacterium to persist in hospital environments and cause disease, including surface attachment structures such as Csu pili and outer membrane protein A, biofilm-promoting factors, iron acquisition systems, and quorum sensing. The review also describes how resistance to last-resort antibiotics such as polymyxins arises through lipid A modifications and how broad multidrug resistance is achieved via carbapenemases, efflux pumps, and aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes encoded on a highly adaptable genome. Additionally, mechanisms of immune evasion, including phase variation and reduced TLR4 recognition, are discussed as contributors to the pathogen's clinical persistence. The authors conclude by highlighting the molecular targets identified through this analysis as candidates for future therapeutic strategies against this critical-priority pathogen.
items.citation: K. Ayswarya, Rafwana Ibrahim, Vimal Veetilvalappil et al.. Virulence arsenal of Acinetobacter baumannii: mechanisms driving persistence and resistance. Archives of Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Dairy cows infected with influenza A(H5N1) reveals low infectious dose and transmission barriers
items.citation: Carolyn M. Lee, Natalie N. Tarbuck, Hannah J. Cochran et al.. Dairy cows infected with influenza A(H5N1) reveals low infectious dose and transmission barriers. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by *Candida* species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infections with high mortality and healthcare costs. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside a critical appraisal of conventional diagnostic methods and their limitations in achieving timely detection. The review evaluates both established and emerging diagnostic technologies, with emphasis on susceptibility-guided therapy as a means of improving outcomes and countering antifungal resistance. Therapeutic strategies are analyzed comprehensively, including empiric and targeted treatment regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the potential role of combination therapy. Looking forward, the review highlights promising developments in antifungal drug pipelines and explores future directions including artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics and vaccine-based prophylaxis as strategies to address the evolving challenges of candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up
items.summary: This paper investigates a conjecture about the mass scaling behavior of towers of light states that appear near the core of so-called EFT strings in four-dimensional theories with minimal supersymmetry. The Integral Scaling Conjecture posits that the exponent governing how these mass towers scale with string tension takes only the integer values one, two, or three, and the authors explore whether this restriction can be derived from the bottom-up using the brane-taxonomy rules of the Emergent String Conjecture. To do so, they systematically classify the relevant duality frames into a large finite set of classes, identify candidate EFT string lattice sites, and exhaustively verify the conjecture across all candidates for both leading and subleading towers below the species scale. They find that integral scaling holds throughout, with the exponent never exceeding three, and they also uncover evidence that oscillator modes of EFT string candidates generate the full lattices of particles and strings. Additionally, they establish that a scaling exponent of one implies a perturbative string limit but that the converse does not hold, and they validate their classification against explicit compactifications in type IIA, F-theory, and M-theory.
items.citation: Muldrow Etheredge, Alvaro Herráez, Dieter Lüst et al.. Integral Scaling for EFT Strings from the Bottom-Up. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
items.summary: This paper investigates how to better align quantum machine learning models with the intrinsic structure of matrix-valued input data by leveraging spectral properties. The authors introduce Quantum Spectral Models, in which the data-encoding unitary's generator is constructed directly from each input matrix rather than using conventional coordinate-wise rotation gates, resulting in three variants based on symmetric, global block, and patch-local block Hamiltonians. The model outputs admit truncated Fourier representations where input-dependent spectral gaps serve as frequency carriers and spectral subspaces shape their coefficients, providing an interpretable inductive bias. Evaluating across digit-recognition and controlled synthetic benchmarks designed around spectral statistics, the proposed models outperform comparison quantum models at the largest tested circuit depths, with the patch-local variant excelling on the recognition task and the global block variant leading on the spectral synthetic tasks. Ablation studies further reveal a task-dependent split between the contributions of spectral subspace information and spectral values alone, clarifying which aspects of the spectral representation drive performance in different settings.
items.citation: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers. Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
items.summary: This paper investigated whether commercial large language models provide stable and consistent evaluations of pseudoscientific claims, focusing on how deployment configurations rather than model architecture shape epistemic outputs. The researchers tested four major model families across multiple time points and through both API and web interfaces, using ethnonationalist pseudoscience as the target claim alongside control prompts about established evolutionary consensus. They found dramatic inconsistencies both within and across model families, with one model's fast versions assigning credibility scores several times higher than all competitors, a pattern that did not appear for scientifically uncontroversial control claims. Particularly notable was the discovery of silent, undocumented updates that abruptly reversed a model's behavior overnight, as well as cases where the same model identifier produced radically different outputs depending on whether it was accessed via API or web interface. The authors argue that an LLM's stance on contested claims is not a fixed property of the underlying model but an opaque, contingent outcome of system prompts, safety layers, and interface routing, and they call for new forms of epistemic accountability given that users and researchers cannot readily detect or anticipate these shifts.
items.citation: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina. Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset
items.summary: This study investigated how much useful performance information can be extracted from routine cement characterization measurements and whether that information transfers reliably across different cement producers. The researchers analyzed a large multi-producer dataset of CEM I cement records spanning nearly three decades and collected from numerous European producers, applying machine learning attribution methods alongside producer-holdout transfer tests. They found that fineness is the strongest predictor of strength class and water demand, but oxide chemistry contributes a comparable signal when considered jointly, and that different fineness descriptors such as Blaine surface area and particle-size distribution metrics are largely interchangeable. Strength class and water demand could be recovered from routine measurements across producers, but early-strength designation emerged only as a population-level tendency rather than a physically distinct class, because early strength arises from multiple interacting factors including fineness, sulfate-alkali chemistry, and plant-specific practice. Producer-holdout tests revealed that absolute prediction errors remain broadly consistent across held-out producers, while recovery of within-producer strength variation is producer-dependent, suggesting that full characterization of producer-specific behavior may require additional mineralogical or phase-speciation data beyond routine measurements.
items.citation: Marchellino Ghorayeb, Christiane Rößler, Horst-Michael Ludwig et al.. Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fully Convergent Projection-based Methods with Momentum under Nonconvex Geometric
items.summary: This paper investigates how momentum terms can be incorporated into projection-based gradient methods for nonlinear optimization problems subject to nonconvex but geometrically structured constraints. The authors first identify a fundamental difficulty that arises when the negative gradient is directly replaced by a general descent direction in the projected-gradient framework, then develop backtracking mechanisms applied to the pre-projection step to safely integrate momentum. By requiring that the base search direction asymptotically reverts to the negative gradient for small stepsizes, they establish convergence to Mordukhovich stationarity without smoothness assumptions, and prove convergence to stronger notions of stationarity—Bouligand and Proximal—under progressively stricter conditions on the search direction. Numerical experiments on sparsity- and bounded-rank-constrained problems confirm that the momentum-enhanced algorithm is computationally effective and benefits from the additional curvature information provided by the momentum term.
items.citation: Matteo Lapucci, Diego Scuppa. Fully Convergent Projection-based Methods with Momentum under Nonconvex Geometric. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
items.summary: The paper introduces a method called bag-of-waves, an interpretable framework for EEG analysis that learns a compact dictionary of recurring waveform templates from unlabeled data using shift-invariant k-means. Rather than relying on predefined spectral features or opaque deep neural networks, the approach converts continuous EEG signals into sequences of discrete waveform tokens whose frequencies and transitions are used for downstream classification or clustering. The framework is extended to capture temporal context through n-gram transition statistics and spatial structure through multi-channel and cross-channel atom representations. The method was evaluated on three datasets spanning different challenges, including a very small animal cohort, resting-state dementia classification, and a large-scale clinical EEG event benchmark, achieving performance competitive with state-of-the-art deep learning and foundation models while using far fewer parameters. A key claimed advantage is interpretability, as each learned atom corresponds to an inspectable waveform that recovers known clinical EEG morphologies, and the approach is particularly well suited to low-data regimes where large models are impractical.
items.citation: Athanasios Papastathopoulos-Katsaros, Steven T. Lee, Lin Yao et al.. Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV antigen test for rapid simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a novel lateral flow immunoassay-based antigen rapid diagnostic test designed to simultaneously detect four major respiratory viruses — SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus — in a single test. Researchers tested nearly four hundred archived nasopharyngeal swab specimens using both the QuickFinder assay and real-time reverse transcription PCR as the reference standard, and also assessed potential cross-reactivity against a panel of other respiratory pathogens. The test demonstrated high sensitivity for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A, somewhat lower sensitivity for influenza B and RSV, and perfect specificity for all four targets, with no cross-reactivity observed. Performance was consistently strong in specimens with high viral loads, but sensitivity declined in low viral load samples. The authors conclude that the assay is a reliable rapid screening tool for differentiating major respiratory viruses but should complement rather than replace molecular testing.
items.citation: Kim JA, Kang M, Yu HJ et al.. Evaluation of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV antigen test for rapid simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients
items.summary: This study investigated the disease burden of respiratory syncytial virus in adult patients at a Japanese clinic by testing nasopharyngeal swabs collected from individuals presenting with acute respiratory infection symptoms. Samples were analyzed using rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests capable of simultaneously detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B viruses, and RSV. While the tests identified positive cases for SARS-CoV-2 and both influenza strains, no RSV-positive patients were detected among the cohort. Comparison with prior studies that used polymerase chain reaction testing revealed a statistically significant difference in RSV detection rates, with PCR identifying a notable proportion of positive cases that the antigen tests missed. The authors conclude that rapid immunochromatographic antigen testing has limited diagnostic utility for RSV infections in Japanese adults, likely reflecting insufficient sensitivity compared to PCR-based approaches.
items.citation: Kajiwara N, Tsunetoshi Y, Shiode S. No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients. 2026

items.title: Performance of an antigen test for detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus-a prospective study.
items.summary: This prospective study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a rapid multiplex antigen test capable of simultaneously detecting four respiratory viruses — SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus — in patients presenting with acute respiratory infections, including both adults and children. Over a thousand patients were tested using the nasal swab antigen kit alongside reference PCR testing of nasopharyngeal samples, with antigen tests interpreted by emergency department staff and PCR performed centrally. The test demonstrated high sensitivity across all four viral targets when compared against a PCR cycle threshold reference cutoff, and achieved perfect specificity for every agent. The study also found that nasal swabs absorbed less viral RNA than nasopharyngeal swabs, a difference that was statistically significant for influenza A in adults but not apparent in children. The authors conclude that the test's performance profile supports its use as an indicator of infectiousness in acute clinical care settings.
items.venue: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
items.citation: Berger K, Vang SH, Bekkeseth RHO et al.. Performance of an antigen test for detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus-a prospective study.. Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases. 2026
