items.title: Analytical comparison of over-the-counter multiplex tests for influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2.
items.summary: This study evaluated the analytical performance of over-the-counter lateral flow tests designed to detect influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2, filling a gap in comparative data available to consumers and clinicians. Researchers conducted a head-to-head benchtop assessment of multiple commercially available tests using contrived specimens prepared from propagated viral stocks diluted in clinical matrix, with results read by blinded evaluators following manufacturer instructions. All eight tests performed comparably across the four viral targets, with detection limits falling within a fourfold dilution range. A notable finding was that at low viral concentrations, many tests initially appeared negative at the start of the interpretation window but converted to a positive result by the window's end. The authors therefore recommend that users allow the full manufacturer-specified incubation time to elapse before concluding a test is truly negative.
items.citation: Lohsen S, Hoy-Schulz Y, Taing A et al.. Analytical comparison of over-the-counter multiplex tests for influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients
items.summary: This study investigated the burden of respiratory syncytial virus infection among adult patients at a Japanese clinic by testing nasopharyngeal swabs collected from adults presenting with acute respiratory symptoms. Samples were analyzed using rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests capable of simultaneously detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, and RSV. While positive cases were identified for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses, not a single RSV-positive result was obtained across all patients tested. Comparing this outcome against prior studies that used polymerase chain reaction testing revealed a statistically significant difference in RSV detection rates, with PCR studies identifying RSV in a meaningful proportion of adult patients. The authors conclude that rapid immunochromatographic antigen testing is likely insufficient for diagnosing RSV infections in Japanese adults, implying that more sensitive molecular methods such as PCR may be necessary for accurate detection.
items.citation: Kajiwara N, Tsunetoshi Y, Shiode S. No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the longstanding question of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper structured opposing arguments around several contested issues, including whether high-performance athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, and whether exercise independently alters immunity or whether confounding factors such as sleep disruption, travel, anxiety, and nutritional deficits account for observed effects. Both sides agreed that moderate, short-duration exercise appears beneficial for immune defense, particularly in older adults and those with chronic disease, while arduous exercise typical of elite athletes and military personnel has long been associated with elevated infection burden. A key point of consensus was that infection susceptibility is multifactorial, making it difficult to isolate exercise as an independent causal variable, and the debate highlighted concerns about the reliability of biomarkers and the quality of evidence used in the field. The article concludes that whether exercise per se causally increases infection risk remains unresolved, and calls for more rigorous empirical research to address this fundamental question in exercise immunology.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise
items.summary: This review paper examines how spinal cord injury affects immune function, with particular focus on the immune response to exercise. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search to gather existing research on exercise immunology across patient, recreationally active, and athlete populations with spinal cord injury. The paper explores how autonomic dysfunction following spinal cord injury alters catecholamine concentrations at rest and after exercise, which may directly suppress immune cells given that most lymphoid cells express adrenergic receptors, while also considering contributions from altered muscular, endocrine, and cardiovascular function. The authors found that the picture is not uniformly negative, as some immune responses such as natural killer cell cytotoxicity increases and mucosal immunity changes following exercise appear either unaffected or potentially offset by compensatory mechanisms including sympathetic reflex activity, receptor hypersensitivity, and neuroendocrine adjustments. The review concludes that exercise and rehabilitation can improve certain immune and autonomic measures in individuals with spinal cord injury, and calls for further research to clarify the mechanisms underlying these responses and their implications for infection susceptibility.
items.citation: Christof A. Leicht, Victoria L. Goosey‐Tolfrey, Nicolette C. Bishop. Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise. PubMed. 2026

items.title: The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria
items.summary: This paper presents an updated international clinical guideline for urticaria, a mast cell-driven skin condition characterized by wheals, angioedema, or both. The guideline was developed using Cochrane methodology and the GRADE framework, incorporating input from a large international consensus conference involving delegates from numerous national and international societies across many countries. It covers the definition, classification, diagnosis, and management of both acute and chronic forms of urticaria, including chronic spontaneous and chronic inducible subtypes. The guideline highlights that chronic urticaria is disabling and substantially impairs quality of life, while also noting the availability of novel therapies. The resulting recommendations are evidence-based and expert-guided, and have received formal acknowledgment from a European medical specialists body.
items.citation: T. Zuberbier, Z. Abdul Hameed Ansari, A. H. Abdul Latiff et al.. The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria. Allergy. 2026

items.title: Microbiota in cancer: current understandings and future perspectives
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between the microbiota and cancer, covering how microbial communities influence carcinogenesis, tumor progression, and patient prognosis. The authors trace the historical development of this research field from early observations of microbes in tumors to mechanistic discoveries, and they synthesize current understanding of how the microbiota modulates oncogenic signaling pathways, immune responses, and tumor metabolism. The review addresses the dual nature of the microbiota as both a promoter and suppressor of tumor growth, and it explores how microbial communities influence responses to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Therapeutic strategies targeting the microbiota — including probiotics, antibiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation — are discussed alongside approved drugs and ongoing clinical trials. The authors conclude by calling for personalized approaches to exploit the anticancer potential of the microbiota and propose a comprehensive framework to guide future research and clinical application in this area.
items.citation: Yanxi Yao, Yifei Zhu, Keji Chen et al.. Microbiota in cancer: current understandings and future perspectives. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients
items.summary: This paper reviews graft-versus-host disease, a multi-systemic complication arising when donor lymphocytes attack host tissues following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, with particular focus on its chronic form and the resulting burden on patients' physical capacity. The authors examined the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the disease and synthesized available evidence from both animal models and human studies on the effects of exercise as an adjunct therapy in affected patients. Their review found that exercise training shows promise for improving physical fitness and potentially immune function while reducing fatigue in this population, though the evidence base remains limited and the authors call for more randomized controlled trials specifically targeting patients with this condition.
items.citation: Carmen Fiuza‐Luces, Nuria Garatachea, Nathan A. Berger et al.. Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Tumour–brain crosstalk restrains cancer immunity via a sensory–sympathetic axis
items.summary: This paper investigated how tumours in peripheral organs communicate with the brain and how this communication affects anti-tumour immunity. Using genetically engineered mouse models combined with neural tracing, tissue imaging, and single-cell transcriptomics, the researchers mapped a bidirectional signalling circuit in the context of lung adenocarcinoma. They found that lung tumours promote innervation and activation of vagal sensory neurons expressing a specific receptor, which transmit signals to brainstem nuclei that in turn elevate sympathetic nervous system activity within the tumour microenvironment. This heightened sympathetic output suppresses anti-tumour immune responses through adrenergic signalling in alveolar macrophages, thereby facilitating tumour growth. Disrupting this sensory-to-sympathetic axis through genetic, pharmacological, or chemogenetic interventions significantly restrained tumour growth by unleashing immune responses, suggesting that targeting this tumour–brain circuit could represent a new therapeutic strategy for visceral organ cancers.
items.citation: Haohan Karen Wei, Chuyue Yu, Bo Hu et al.. Tumour–brain crosstalk restrains cancer immunity via a sensory–sympathetic axis. Nature. 2026

items.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
items.summary: This paper investigates the application of explainability techniques to reinforcement learning in the safety-critical domain of air traffic control, motivated by the need to build trust in AI systems operating in high-stakes environments. The researchers trained a reinforcement learning agent in a simplified air traffic control environment to make routing decisions that avoid no-fly zones. To shed light on the agent's decision-making process, saliency maps were applied as a preliminary explainability method, identifying which input features most strongly influenced the agent's choices. The work positions explainability as a foundational requirement for advancing human-AI collaboration and higher levels of automation in aviation.
items.citation: Anduel Mehmeti, Gabriella Gigante, Salvatore Venticinque. Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers. arXiv. 2026

Through an exhaustive analysis of these candidates, they confirm that integral scaling holds for all leading towers and for subleading towers below the species scale, with minor half-integral subtleties that also appear in top-down constructions. They additionally find evidence that oscillator modes of EFT string candidates generate the full lattices of particles and strings, and establish that while a scaling exponent of one implies a perturbative string limit, the converse does not hold. The results are cross-checked against concrete compactifications in type IIA, F-theory, and M-theory.

items.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
items.summary: This paper addresses the mismatch between how quantum machine learning models encode data and the structural properties of matrix-valued inputs, where existing coordinate-wise rotation-gate encodings fail to capture matrix-level spectral structure. The authors introduce Quantum Spectral Models, a family of quantum machine learning architectures in which the data-encoding unitary is generated directly from each input matrix, creating an explicit spectral representation. Three variants are studied, differing in how they construct their Hamiltonians from symmetric, global block, or patch-local block structures, and their outputs are shown to admit truncated Fourier representations where input-dependent spectral gaps and subspaces shape both the frequency content and coefficients. The models are benchmarked against standard quantum comparison models on handwritten digit data and controlled synthetic tasks designed around spectral statistics, with the proposed variants achieving leading mean test accuracy across all benchmarks at the largest evaluated circuit depth. Ablation experiments reveal a task-dependent distinction between the contributions of spectral values and spectral subspaces, suggesting that input-conditioned spectral representations offer an analysable and practically useful inductive bias for structure-aware quantum model design.
items.citation: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers. Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language models provide consistent and reliable evaluations of pseudoscientific claims, focusing on how deployment configurations rather than model architecture itself shape epistemic outputs. The researchers systematically tested four major commercial language model families across multiple temporal snapshots and through both API and web interfaces, using ethnonationalist pseudoscience derived from a specific biosocial framework as the test case alongside control prompts about established evolutionary consensus. They found that one model family's fast versions assigned credibility scores dramatically higher than all other models for the pseudoscientific claims, while performing comparably to peers on control prompts, revealing that this disparity was specific to contested fringe content. Further, the study documented that a silent, undocumented update reversed one model's behavior overnight, and that identical model identifiers produced radically divergent outputs depending on whether the API or web interface was used. The authors conclude that a commercial model's stance on contested knowledge is not a stable intrinsic property but a contingent product of system prompts, safety layers, interface routing, and undisclosed updates, and they argue this opacity constitutes a public concern demanding new forms of epistemic accountability.
items.citation: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina. Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Machine Learning Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset
items.summary: This study investigated how well routine cement quality control measurements can predict performance properties of CEM I cement and whether those predictions transfer across different manufacturing sources. Using a large dataset of cement records from numerous European producers spanning nearly three decades, the researchers applied machine learning methods combined with oxide chemistry, fineness measurements, particle size descriptors, and derived mineralogical parameters. They found that fineness is the dominant predictor of strength class and water demand, though oxide chemistry contributes a comparable signal when considered jointly, and that standard Blaine surface area and more detailed particle size representations are largely interchangeable. Strength class and water demand could be reliably recovered from routine data, but early-strength designation could not be identified as a physically distinct class because it arises from multiple interacting factors including fineness, sulfate-alkali chemistry, phase assemblage, and plant practice. Producer holdout tests revealed that while absolute prediction errors remain broadly consistent across producers, recovery of within-producer strength variation is producer-dependent, suggesting that full characterization of producer-specific behavior may require additional speciation beyond routine measurements.

items.title: Fully Convergent Projection-based Methods with Momentum under Nonconvex Geometric
items.summary: This paper studies nonlinear optimization problems subject to complicated, nonconvex but geometrically structured constraints, focusing on how momentum acceleration techniques can be incorporated into projected-gradient methods without sacrificing theoretical convergence guarantees. The authors first identify a fundamental difficulty that arises when the negative gradient is naively replaced by a general descent direction in the projection-based framework. They then develop backtracking mechanisms applied at the pre-projection step that allow momentum terms to be integrated, and prove that the resulting algorithms converge to strong stationarity conditions—specifically Mordukhovich, Bouligand, or Proximal stationarity—depending on how closely the search direction reverts to the negative gradient as stepsizes shrink, and without requiring smoothness assumptions in the most general case. Numerical experiments on sparsity-constrained and bounded-rank constrained problems demonstrate that the momentum-enhanced methods are computationally effective, exploiting the additional curvature information provided by the momentum term.
items.citation: Matteo Lapucci, Diego Scuppa. Fully Convergent Projection-based Methods with Momentum under Nonconvex Geometric. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AI-Enhanced Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Infectious Diseases in Resource-Limited Settings: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: This scoping review systematically mapped research on artificial intelligence-enhanced point-of-care and rapid diagnostic technologies for infectious diseases in resource-limited settings, examining gaps in disease coverage, geographic representation, and validation rigor. Following established scoping review methodology, the authors searched five major databases spanning roughly a decade of literature, ultimately including several hundred studies after screening and deduplication. The field was found to be growing rapidly, with nearly half of all publications appearing in the most recent period reviewed, though research was heavily concentrated on a narrow triad of diseases—COVID-19, malaria, and tuberculosis—while neglected tropical diseases remained substantially underrepresented. Convolutional neural networks were the dominant artificial intelligence approach, and microscopy and molecular diagnostic modalities were most commonly studied, yet the vast majority of studies lacked prospective field validation, with only a small fraction reporting this rigor. The authors conclude that despite exponential growth in the field, critical deficiencies in validation standards, equitable disease coverage, and geographic inclusivity—particularly the underrepresentation of West Africa and Latin America—must be addressed before these technologies can meaningfully benefit the populations they are intended to serve.
items.venue: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
items.citation: Farquhar H. AI-Enhanced Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Infectious Diseases in Resource-Limited Settings: A Scoping Review.. Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care testing (POCT) for Infectious diseases: technological innovation, effectiveness evaluation, and application strategies in resource-limited regions.
items.summary: This review paper examines point-of-care testing technologies for infectious diseases, focusing on their role in early screening, epidemic surveillance, and public health prevention. The authors systematically surveyed recent advances across molecular diagnostics, microfluidic systems, biosensing technologies, and artificial intelligence as applied to rapid diagnostic platforms. The review also analyzes quality assessment frameworks encompassing sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, stability, and field applicability. Particular emphasis is placed on strategies for deploying these technologies in resource-limited settings, addressing technical optimization, resource allocation, and local support infrastructure. The paper concludes by proposing future development directions intended to guide further research and implementation of infectious disease point-of-care diagnostics.
items.citation: Zhang YX, Ru JF. Point-of-care testing (POCT) for Infectious diseases: technological innovation, effectiveness evaluation, and application strategies in resource-limited regions.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Infectious disease diagnostic competencies of medical students as a fundamental basis for physicians' resilience in addressing future infectious disease challenges.
items.summary: This paper examines the role of infectious disease diagnostic training in building long-term resilience among medical students and future physicians in the face of ongoing and emerging infectious disease challenges. The authors argue that competencies in infection diagnostics, including correct sample collection, appropriate test selection, and critical interpretation of microbiological and virological findings, form the foundation for evidence-based clinical practice. They emphasize that these skills are inseparable from rational antimicrobial therapy and are therefore critical to combating the development of multidrug-resistant pathogens. The paper contends that such competencies cannot be acquired through self-directed learning alone but require structured, hands-on practical training within the framework of medical microbiology, virology, and hygiene education. Drawing on the One-Health concept, the authors stress that understanding pathogen-associated risks across individual, societal, animal, and ecosystem levels is essential and must be central to medical curricula.
items.citation: Brandt C, Becker K, Ciesek S et al.. Infectious disease diagnostic competencies of medical students as a fundamental basis for physicians' resilience in addressing future infectious disease challenges.. GMS infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: From Control to Eradication: The Role of Point-of-Care Testing in Modernising Australia's Bovine Viral Diarrhoea (BVD) Disease Management.
items.summary: This review examines the current state of bovine viral diarrhoea virus management in Australia and proposes a pathway toward national eradication. The authors focus on the central role of persistently infected animals as the primary transmission reservoir and the challenge posed by Australia's decentralised, non-compulsory biosecurity framework, which has resulted in a fragmented and inconsistent national response. The review evaluates point-of-care diagnostic technologies, including lateral flow assays, nucleic acid amplification tests, and biosensors, as field-deployable tools capable of real-time, crush-side identification of persistently infected animals. The authors argue that strategic deployment of these rapid diagnostics, when combined with coordinated biosecurity protocols and optimised vaccination strategies, could serve as the transformative mechanism needed to shift Australia from disease control toward systematic eradication. The paper concludes that such an integrated approach represents both a scientifically sound and commercially viable route to eliminating the disease's substantial economic burden on Australian beef and dairy industries.
items.citation: Ogada S, Naseem MN, Ranjbar S et al.. From Control to Eradication: The Role of Point-of-Care Testing in Modernising Australia's Bovine Viral Diarrhoea (BVD) Disease Management.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Establishing an EU-compliant diagnostic facility for infectious diseases under war conditions in Poltava, Ukraine.
items.summary: This paper describes the establishment of advanced infectious disease diagnostic capabilities in a regional hospital in Poltava, Ukraine, during the ongoing war with Russia. The authors formed a German-Ukrainian hospital partnership to implement EU-compliant serological testing, automated PCR, and bacterial identification with antibiotic susceptibility testing, replacing the low-sensitivity rapid tests previously in use. Key elements of the initiative included participatory equipment selection, hands-on training of Ukrainian staff in Germany, jointly developed standard operating procedures, and adaptive reagent supply chains. The newly established laboratories successfully identified previously unrecognized cases of HIV, Hepatitis B and C, Lyme disease, Toxoplasmosis, and antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections across thousands of tests conducted over the project period. The authors argue that this partnership model—emphasizing shared decision-making, straightforward solutions, and contingency planning—demonstrates that high-quality diagnostic infrastructure can be built under wartime conditions and may serve as a template for expansion to other regions of Ukraine.
items.citation: Zelinskyy G, Koval T, Schrammel U et al.. Establishing an EU-compliant diagnostic facility for infectious diseases under war conditions in Poltava, Ukraine.. Frontiers in public health. 2026

items.title: The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria
items.summary: This paper presents an updated international clinical guideline for urticaria, a mast cell-driven condition characterized by the rapid onset of wheals, angioedema, or both. The guideline was developed using Cochrane methodology and the GRADE framework, with consensus achieved through a large international conference involving delegates from numerous national and international societies across many countries. The document covers the definition and classification of urticaria, distinguishing between acute and chronic forms, with chronic urticaria further categorized as either spontaneous or inducible. It provides evidence-based and expert-guided recommendations for diagnosing and managing the various subtypes of urticaria, noting that while chronic urticaria significantly impairs quality of life and daily functioning, novel therapeutic options are now available. The guideline was formally acknowledged and accepted by the European Union of Medical Specialists.
items.citation: T. Zuberbier, Z. Abdul Hameed Ansari, A. H. Abdul Latiff et al.. The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria. Allergy. 2026

items.title: EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update
items.summary: These updated recommendations address the management of rheumatoid arthritis using synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, incorporating the most recent clinical evidence. An international task force conducted systematic literature reviews on the safety and efficacy of available treatments, then used a voting process to revise and consolidate guidance from the previous iteration. The resulting framework was streamlined to fewer recommendations covering conventional synthetic agents, glucocorticoids, biologic DMARDs, and targeted synthetic DMARDs including Janus kinase inhibitors, with particular attention to treat-to-target strategies and tapering in remission. The recommendations retain methotrexate combined with short-term glucocorticoids as the preferred initial therapy, with addition of a biologic DMARD after insufficient response, while Janus kinase inhibitors remain an option subject to careful individualized risk assessment for cardiovascular events, malignancies, and thromboembolic complications. The task force emphasizes that sustained remission may permit cautious tapering of therapy, though complete cessation frequently leads to disease flare, and that safety, efficacy, and cost considerations should all inform treatment sequencing.
items.citation: Josef S. Smolen, Christopher J. Edwards, Victoria Konzett et al.. EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update. Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and how its dysregulation contributes to a broad spectrum of diseases. The authors surveyed the research history of lipid metabolism and focused particularly on how lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways govern the behavior of immune cells including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils. They explored how lipid metabolites regulate immune cell proliferation, differentiation, and activation across multiple levels of control, encompassing genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational mechanisms. The review connects these findings to disease contexts such as autoimmune conditions, cancer, neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, aging, and metabolic disorders. The authors conclude by summarizing current therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, ongoing clinical efforts, and future directions including lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Digital twins in oncology: From predictive modelling to personalised treatment strategies
items.summary: This narrative review examines the application of digital twin technology in oncology, a concept borrowed from engineering that creates dynamic virtual replicas of a patient's physiological and pathological state to support personalised cancer care. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search across multiple major databases, including grey literature and conference proceedings, to synthesise evidence on how digital twins are being developed, validated, and applied across different cancer types. The review finds that digital twins have demonstrated utility throughout the cancer care continuum, encompassing precision treatment selection, radiotherapy optimisation, drug development, immuno-oncology modelling, surgical planning, and survivorship care, with artificial intelligence and multi-omics data integration enabling simulation of tumour behaviour and treatment response. Despite this promise, the authors identify persistent challenges in data integration, model validation, computational scalability, and ethical governance that currently hinder clinical translation. They conclude that realising the potential of digital twins in precision oncology will require interdisciplinary collaboration and the development of appropriate regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: David B. Olawade, Emmanuel O. Oisakede, Oluwakemi Jumoke Bello et al.. Digital twins in oncology: From predictive modelling to personalised treatment strategies. Critical Reviews in Oncology/Hematology. 2026

items.title: Food and Medicine Homology Focus in 2026
items.summary: This perspective paper examines the field of food and medicine homology, which encompasses the traditional and scientific study of substances that serve dual roles as food and medicine. The authors outline a forward-looking framework for how the field is expected to develop, emphasizing a shift from empirical traditional knowledge toward rigorous scientific methodologies grounded in mechanistic understanding and evidence-based standards. Key research directions identified include identifying active components, elucidating multisystem interaction mechanisms involving gut microbiota, and exploring emerging biological processes such as phase separation and immunometabolic reprogramming. Applications are anticipated to advance toward precision and dynamic health management through artificial intelligence and multidimensional personal data, with particular relevance to chronic disease and aging populations. The industrial dimension of the field is also expected to evolve through synthetic biology, intelligent delivery systems, and sustainable manufacturing practices.
items.citation: Mengyao Li, Gui-Fen Wu, Feng Lu et al.. Food and Medicine Homology Focus in 2026. Food & medicine homology.. 2026

items.title: LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties
items.summary: This study conducted a spectroscopic survey of young stellar objects in Sh2-284, a distant and metal-poor star-forming region located toward the Galactic anticenter, to investigate how reduced metallicity affects the properties of accreting young stars. Candidate young stellar objects were identified using mid-infrared and optical photometry, then followed up with multi-object spectroscopy at the Large Binocular Telescope, covering a wide field and a range of stellar masses from sub-solar to nearly three solar masses. The team characterized stellar and accretion properties using nine emission-line diagnostics, including hydrogen Balmer and Paschen series lines as well as calcium infrared triplet lines, and provided initial estimates of iron and lithium abundances for select targets. Comparing the metal-poor sample with solar-metallicity star-forming regions, the authors find tentative evidence for a flattening in flux-flux relations across multiple accretion diagnostics, suggesting a metallicity-related difference in accretion behavior. Despite the sub-solar metal content, the young stellar objects display robust accretion activity spanning several orders of magnitude in accretion rate, indicating that gas accretion onto forming stars can be efficiently sustained in low-metallicity environments.
items.citation: Katia Biazzo, Juan Manuel Alcalá, Felice Cusano et al.. LBT-MODS spectroscopy of young stellar objects in the distant metal-poor star forming region Sh2-284: Stellar and accretion properties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Kidney function and kidney failure prediction in a large multiethnic population
items.summary: This study examined how different equations for estimating kidney function perform across a large, ethnically diverse population, with the goal of informing clinical decision-making for chronic kidney disease management. Using a retrospective multicenter cohort of nearly two million adults with serum creatinine measurements, the researchers compared four glomerular filtration rate estimation equations—two older race-stratified versions and two newer race-neutral versions—assessing their ability to predict kidney failure and estimate disease prevalence over a decade of follow-up. The newer race-neutral equations diverged substantially from one another, with one producing lower and the other higher kidney function estimates compared to prior equations, while the older race-stratified equations remained similarly calibrated. The oldest equation proved the most discriminative for predicting kidney failure within five years, whereas the newer European equation performed least well in this regard. Estimated chronic kidney disease prevalence varied meaningfully depending on which equation was used and differed across patients' regions of birth, highlighting broad clinical and epidemiological consequences of equation selection.
items.citation: James A. Diao, Morgan Sanchez, Adir Sommer et al.. Kidney function and kidney failure prediction in a large multiethnic population. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the alleged chaos in periodically forced traveling-wave reductions of fractional WBBM models: a quantitative re-examination
items.summary: This paper critically examines a widespread methodological pipeline in the nonlinear waves literature, whereby fractional evolution equations are reduced via traveling-wave substitution to planar Hamiltonian systems, periodically forced, and then analyzed through visual inspection of phase portraits to claim chaos, quasi-periodicity, and bifurcations. The authors argue this approach is fundamentally problematic because the resulting systems are undamped, near-integrable oscillators governed by KAM theory, which strictly confines any chaos to exponentially thin stochastic layers, raising the evidentiary bar far above what visual inspection can satisfy. Using a specific published study of the fractional Wazwaz-Benjamin-Bona-Mahony model as a representative case, they applied four independent quantitative diagnostics—Lyapunov exponent calculations, separation-growth tests, stroboscopic Poincaré sections, and spectral analysis—across extremely long integration times. They found that every claimed chaos signature fails all diagnostics, with Lyapunov exponents indistinguishable from zero and separation growth that is linear rather than exponential, while the unforced system's "quasi-periodicity" claim is impossible by construction since planar autonomous Hamiltonian systems must be periodic. The paper additionally documents a false positive produced by the Gottwald-Melbourne 0-1 test on a regular orbit and provides a methodological checklist intended to establish minimum standards for chaos claims in this class of models.
items.citation: Kaixuan Niu. On the alleged chaos in periodically forced traveling-wave reductions of fractional WBBM models: a quantitative re-examination. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Pulsatile poromechanics in layered soft media controls fluid flow and solute transport: from fundamentals to brain clearance
items.summary: This paper investigated how layered structure in soft porous biological media affects fluid flow and solute transport under periodic mechanical loading, with a particular focus on brain tissue clearance. The researchers developed a bilayer poromechanical model and systematically compared layered configurations against a homogeneous reference case, carefully selecting material property combinations that preserved the same poroelastic timescale across all configurations to isolate the effect of layering alone. They found that although the poroelastic timescale governs behavior in homogeneous media, identical timescales in bilayer systems produce non-trivial and counterintuitive patterns of strain localization, fluid flow, and solute transport. These results suggest that layered tissue architectures may confer functional advantages for cellular homeostasis compared to homogeneous structures. Furthermore, the study demonstrated that pathological changes to the brain's layered organization substantially impair fluid flow and metabolic waste clearance, offering a mechanistic explanation for transport deficits observed in neurological disease.
items.citation: Matilde Fiori, Sylvie Lorthois. Pulsatile poromechanics in layered soft media controls fluid flow and solute transport: from fundamentals to brain clearance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Human-Augmenting Agentic Workflow for Observational Causal Inference
items.summary: This paper introduces an open-source Python package designed to support observational causal inference through a human-in-the-loop agentic workflow. The tool automates technically demanding but repetitive steps in causal analysis — such as covariate balance checking, propensity score trimming, and sensitivity analysis — while reserving higher-order judgment tasks, like assumption scrutiny and results evaluation, for human analysts. The system supports doubly robust estimation of average treatment effects, heterogeneous treatment effect estimation, and partially linear models for multiple continuous treatments. Evaluations on public data and internal case studies show that the agent outperforms less structured baselines and remains competitive with carefully hand-tuned analyses. The package has seen substantial real-world adoption, orchestrating a large number of causal inference analyses per month in a production setting.
items.citation: Winston Chou, Adrien Alexandre, Lars Olds et al.. A Human-Augmenting Agentic Workflow for Observational Causal Inference. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A closer look at the WISPIT 2 host star. Evidence for a spectroscopic binary
items.summary: The paper investigated the host star of WISPIT 2, a rare system where giant protoplanets have been directly detected still embedded within their protoplanetary disc. Using optical and near-infrared spectroscopy, the researchers characterized the stellar properties, accretion rate, and searched for close stellar companions through radial velocity measurements. They discovered that the host is actually a spectroscopic binary with a short orbital period, comprising a solar-mass primary of spectral type K3 and a significantly less massive secondary companion. Emission line analysis revealed an accretion rate below the chromospheric noise floor, indicating little to no active accretion onto the young stars. This finding makes WISPIT 2 the first known circumbinary disc system hosting directly imaged protoplanets, establishing it as a unique laboratory for understanding planet formation and disc evolution in binary star environments.
items.citation: Cade J. Bürgy, Myriam Benisty, Hala Alqubelat et al.. A closer look at the WISPIT 2 host star. Evidence for a spectroscopic binary. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Modular in vivo antibody–ADC click to reverse drug resistance in tumours
items.summary: This paper investigated a strategy to overcome drug resistance and tumour heterogeneity that limit the effectiveness of antibody–drug conjugates in cancer therapy. The researchers developed an in vivo bioorthogonal click chemistry platform in which therapeutic antibodies and ADCs are separately modified with complementary reactive chemical groups, then administered sequentially so that they ligate together after systemic delivery within the body. This approach was evaluated in preclinical tumour models characterized by co-expression of HER2 and EGFR, including tumours with low, ultralow, negative, or heterogeneous HER2 expression that are resistant to or ineligible for conventional HER2-directed ADCs. The antibody–ADC click constructs demonstrated superior antitumour activity compared to standard ADC monotherapy or simple antibody plus ADC combinations, without requiring extensive re-engineering of existing clinical antibodies. The authors propose this as a flexible, modular platform that exploits receptor biology and bioorthogonal chemistry to address antigen heterogeneity and resistance across multiple tumour types.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it demonstrates a strategy of chemically linking existing therapeutic antibodies to antibody–drug conjugates directly inside the body using bioorthogonal click chemistry, offering a modular way to overcome drug resistance in heterogeneous tumours without requiring entirely new drugs.
items.citation: Cristina Simó, Alexander C. Vanover, Ricardo D’Oliveira Albanus et al.. Modular in vivo antibody–ADC click to reverse drug resistance in tumours. Nature. 2026

items.title: A queen odour mediates reproductive suppression in a eusocial mammal
items.summary: Naked mole-rats represent one of the very few examples of eusociality in mammals, yet the chemical mechanisms by which a single queen suppresses reproduction in all other females have remained unclear. This study investigated whether a specific chemical signal produced by queens is responsible for maintaining this reproductive hierarchy. The researchers identified isopropyl myristate, a low-volatility ester highly enriched in queens, as a key pheromone that is detected by olfactory neurons, triggers avoidance behaviour in high-ranking females, and alters prolactin and progesterone levels in non-breeders to inhibit reproduction. Experimental addition of this compound to queenless colonies prevented other females from assuming reproductive dominance, while its withdrawal prompted aggression and reproductive competition. The compound was also detected in breeding females of related mole-rat species, but at higher concentrations in naked mole-rats, consistent with their uniquely extreme reproductive skew, thereby drawing a parallel between the chemical regulation of eusociality in insects and mammals.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a specific chemical signal produced by a queen mammal that actively suppresses reproduction in other females, revealing a molecular mechanism underlying the strict social hierarchy of a eusocial species. The finding draws a striking parallel between chemical reproductive control in insects and mammals, suggesting this form of pheromonal dominance may be more widespread across animal societies than previously understood.
items.citation: Mohammed A. Khallaf, Daniel W. Hart, Wenhan Luo et al.. A queen odour mediates reproductive suppression in a eusocial mammal. Nature. 2026

items.title: Highly fragmented European wetlands with uneven restoration needs
items.summary: This paper investigated the condition and spatial distribution of wetlands across European countries to support the European Union's Nature Restoration Law, which mandates restoration of degraded wetland ecosystems by 2030. Using high-resolution satellite imagery combined with machine learning, the researchers mapped six types of seminatural open wetlands and quantified the extent of land-use disturbance across the continent. They found that European wetlands are highly fragmented, with a substantial proportion of total wetland area occurring in very small patches that coarser mapping products would miss, and that human activities affect roughly one-fifth of all wetland area—particularly inland wetland types—with potentially large associated losses of soil carbon relative to undisturbed baselines. When restoration targets derived from their disturbance estimates were compared against national commitments, some countries' pledges aligned reasonably well while others lacked quantified goals despite having significant areas in need of restoration identified by the new maps. The resulting high-resolution, standardized dataset provides an EU-wide baseline for tracking restoration progress and linking satellite-derived condition assessments to policy targets.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it provides a comprehensive, high-resolution picture of the fragmentation and condition of European wetlands, revealing that restoration needs are unevenly distributed across the continent. The combination of satellite imagery and machine learning to map multiple wetland types and their disturbance levels offers a new empirical foundation for prioritizing conservation and restoration efforts.
items.citation: Gyula Mate Kovács, Xiaoye Tong, Dimitri Gominski et al.. Highly fragmented European wetlands with uneven restoration needs. Nature. 2026

items.title: Food systems transformation would reshape global agriculture
items.summary: This paper examined the large-scale agricultural consequences of transforming global food systems toward healthier and more sustainable outcomes by the middle of this century. The researchers modeled a scenario combining adoption of the EAT–Lancet reference diet, improved agricultural productivity, and halving of food waste, using an ensemble of ten global economic models to project impacts out to 2050. They found that such a transformation would fundamentally restructure global agriculture in ways that diverge from historical trends, including a meaningful reduction in total agricultural land use compared with current levels. A particularly striking finding is that livestock production value would fall dramatically relative to business-as-usual projections, while the value of vegetables, fruits, nuts, and legumes would rise substantially. The authors argue that the magnitude and distributional complexity of these shifts underscores the need for active food policy that weighs the health and environmental benefits of transformation against its significant economic and sectoral disruptions.
items.why_notable: The work is drawing attention because scenario simulations project that shifting food systems toward healthier diets, greater productivity, and drastically reduced food waste could fundamentally restructure global agriculture by mid-century. This offers quantitative insight into how interconnected changes across consumption, production, and waste could collectively reshape the world's food supply.
items.citation: Matthew Gibson, Marina Sundiang, Daniel Mason-D’Croz et al.. Food systems transformation would reshape global agriculture. Nature. 2026

items.title: Quantum statistical plasmonic metacrystals
items.summary: This paper introduces a new class of engineered optical materials called quantum statistical plasmonic metacrystals, designed to control the multiparticle dynamics of light based on its quantum statistical properties. The structures consist of plasmonic nanoantennas arranged as meta-atoms, whose optical near-field interactions mediate multiphoton dynamics among incoming light fields. The key finding is that these structures produce allowed and forbidden bands in quantum photon statistics, analogous to electronic band structures in conventional crystals, such that multiphoton fields with statistics falling within allowed bands propagate undistorted while those in forbidden bands are suppressed or redirected toward the nearest allowed statistical state. Crucially, these statistical bands are determined by the geometry and collective arrangement of the meta-atoms, offering a deterministic design route for engineering quantum statistical transport at room temperature. The authors propose that this platform has implications for coherence-sensitive photonic applications including energy harvesting and scalable many-body quantum technologies.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because it introduces a fundamentally new class of materials capable of filtering light not by conventional optical properties but purely by the quantum coherence of photons, creating band structures defined by photon statistics rather than wavelength or polarization.
items.citation: Chenglong You, Riley B. Dawkins, Jannatul Ferdous et al.. Quantum statistical plasmonic metacrystals. Nature. 2026

items.title: Scalable quasi-pure MOF membranes for energy-efficient gas separations
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it demonstrates that metal–organic framework membranes can be fabricated at scale while retaining near-intrinsic separation performance, offering a potentially transformative route to energy-efficient industrial gas separations that could dramatically cut costs relative to conventional distillation.

items.title: A Bayesian framework for longitudinal EHR and genetic discovery
items.summary: This paper introduces ALADYNOULLI, a Bayesian generative framework designed to jointly model longitudinal electronic health record diagnoses, patient age, and polygenic risk in order to uncover latent time-varying disease signatures. Unlike prior approaches that treat diseases in isolation, the model is formulated as a mixture of probabilities rather than a probability of a mixture, allowing it to properly handle simultaneous and chronic conditions. Applied across three large independent biobanks encompassing hundreds of thousands of participants, up to decades of follow-up, and hundreds of diseases, the framework recovers a set of replicable disease signatures that are highly preserved across cohorts and align with established disease biology, including expected enrichments for known genetic risk variants. A signature-based genome-wide association study identifies numerous genome-wide significant loci, including cardiovascular associations not detected by single-trait analyses, and the framework also corrects for selection bias through inverse probability weighting. For disease prediction, ALADYNOULLI outperforms established clinical risk tools at both short- and long-term horizons, and its disease-level predictions complement existing code-level foundation models.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it offers a unified statistical approach that jointly models time-varying clinical records and genomic information, potentially uncovering hidden disease patterns that neither data source could reveal alone.

items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reframes elastic instabilities—typically considered a structural liability—as a deliberate design tool for engineering materials that are dramatically more resistant to fracture. By harnessing these instabilities in mechanical metamaterials, researchers achieved a striking increase in fracture energy, suggesting a fundamentally new principle for toughening structures.

items.title: Regression to the mean can explain saturation of geomagnetic storms
items.summary: This paper investigated the apparent saturation of Earth's geomagnetic response during extreme solar wind driving events, a phenomenon that has prompted numerous competing theoretical explanations over many years. The authors analyzed the statistical relationship between solar wind measurements and geomagnetic indices such as the polar cap index, accounting for random uncertainties in the timing and magnitude of solar wind observations. They demonstrated that the observed saturation is not a physical phenomenon but rather a statistical artifact known as regression to the mean, which causes extreme measured values to appear associated with weaker-than-true responses due to measurement uncertainty. Correcting for these uncertainties reveals that the Earth's geomagnetic response to solar wind driving is actually linear throughout the entire range of driving conditions, and that the true impact of extreme geomagnetic storms may be substantially larger than previously estimated. The authors argue that this statistical bias likely affects data analyses in other fields involving uncertain measurements of extreme values, including climate science and medicine.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reframes a long-standing phenomenon in space weather — the apparent saturation of geomagnetic storms at high solar wind strengths — as a statistical artifact rather than a physical limit. The implication that extreme geomagnetic storms could be twice as severe as previously estimated significantly raises the potential threat they pose.
items.citation: Nithin Sivadas, D. G. Sibeck, Varsha Subramanyan et al.. Regression to the mean can explain saturation of geomagnetic storms. Nature. 2026

items.title: Metabolite glues as a means of purine sensing and chemotherapeutic response
items.summary: This paper investigated whether molecular glue mechanisms operate endogenously in human cells to regulate metabolic processes. The researchers discovered that purine nucleotides act as metabolite glues, physically tethering the rate-limiting enzyme in purine biosynthesis, PPAT, to its inhibitor NUDT5, thereby creating a feedback mechanism by which cells sense purine levels and control their own synthesis. They also found that thiopurine chemotherapeutics, which have been in clinical use for decades, exploit the same protein complex but bind in distinct orientations that enhance their inhibitory function. Notably, the binding pocket of the PPAT–NUDT5 complex displays conformational flexibility that accommodates substantial chemical modifications, suggesting it can be exploited to develop more potent and selective compounds. The study thus establishes endogenous metabolite glues as a previously unrecognized mode of nutrient sensing and reveals a structural rationale for improving existing chemotherapeutics targeting this pathway.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that purines themselves can act as natural molecular glues, locking a key biosynthetic enzyme together with its inhibitor—a previously unrecognized sensing mechanism. The finding also opens a potential avenue for enhancing the effectiveness of existing thiopurine chemotherapy drugs by exploiting or modifying this interaction.
items.citation: Samuel R. Witus, Megan M. Kober, Heegwang Roh et al.. Metabolite glues as a means of purine sensing and chemotherapeutic response. Nature. 2026

items.title: Rising dust pollution across Europe in a changing climate
items.summary: The paper investigated the sources, trends, and health impacts of mineral desert dust transported to Europe, focusing on whether observed increases in dust pollution are consistent across the continent and whether they are driven primarily by desertification and aridity or by changes in atmospheric circulation. Researchers compiled a database of daily dust metal concentrations from European monitoring sites, used robust elemental ratios to characterize transported dust, and developed a machine learning model to estimate daily fine particulate matter concentrations from dust over a decade-long period. The study found that dust concentrations vary substantially between northern and southern Europe, with southern populations exposed to elevated dust event levels associated with a measurable rise in daily mortality. Over the past decade, intensified dust intrusions were linked to shifts in atmospheric circulation, while an Alpine ice core record revealed a dramatic long-term increase in dust concentrations since pre-industrial times, attributed largely to North African desertification. The authors conclude that accelerating climate change, by promoting land degradation and altering weather patterns, is likely to worsen dust pollution and pose growing threats to public health and air quality targets across Europe.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it links rising dust pollution across Europe to both shifts in atmospheric circulation and increasing North African aridity since pre-industrial times, combining a large observational database, machine learning, and ice-core evidence to reveal how climate change is driving the trend.
items.citation: Petros N. Vasilakos, Abhishek Upadhyay, Manousos I. Manousakas et al.. Rising dust pollution across Europe in a changing climate. Nature. 2026

items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it challenges prevailing assumptions about how the brain organizes information, finding that cortical circuits favor diverse, high-dimensional representations over the categorical structures long thought to dominate neural coding. The findings suggest a fundamentally different computational logic across the cortical hierarchy, with important implications for understanding how the brain achieves flexible, separable representations.

items.title: People use fast and flat simulation to reason about new games
items.summary: This paper investigated how people reason about entirely unfamiliar decision-making problems, using novice gameplay on novel two-player strategic board games as a model domain. Through large-scale behavioral experiments with over a thousand participants playing or evaluating more than a hundred games most had never encountered, the researchers examined whether people show systematic and adaptive rationality when facing new problems for the first time. They found that participants were indeed capable of both playing new games sensibly and evaluating their properties, such as fairness or enjoyment potential, even before playing them. To explain these capacities, the authors developed a computational cognitive model called the "Intuitive Gamer," which relies on fast and flat, depth-limited, goal-directed probabilistic simulation rather than deep strategic search. The work suggests that this lightweight simulation mechanism underlies human flexibility with novel problems and has implications for designing artificial intelligence systems that can assess whether a task merits attention, not merely how to solve it.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because it reveals that people use a specific cognitive strategy—described as "fast and flat simulation"—to reason systematically and adaptively when encountering unfamiliar games. The findings also have implications beyond human cognition, potentially guiding the development of more flexible artificial intelligence systems.
items.citation: Katherine M. Collins, Cedegao E. Zhang, Lionel Wong et al.. People use fast and flat simulation to reason about new games. Nature. 2026

items.title: Cell-type signatures of Alzheimer’s disease shared across population groups
items.summary: This study investigated whether cellular and molecular signatures of Alzheimer's disease are consistent across different population groups, addressing a gap left by prior genomic research that had not examined cross-population generalizability. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing and chromatin accessibility profiling on post-mortem brain tissue from Latin, white, and African American individuals, the researchers characterized cortical and subcortical regions through both discrete clustering and continuous gene-expression analyses. They identified specific subtypes of microglia, astrocytes, and neurons associated with Alzheimer's disease in a region-dependent manner that were shared across all three population groups, alongside continuous gene-expression programs in astrocytes and oligodendrocytes linked to lipid processing and neurotransmitter reuptake. The study further revealed six molecularly distinct subgroups of individuals with cognitive impairment that transcended population boundaries and were not explained by standard neuropathological measures, but were instead defined by molecular signatures associated with ante-mortem cognitive decline. Taken together, the findings demonstrate that representative, multi-population sampling can uncover both shared disease mechanisms and disease heterogeneity, providing a foundation for prioritizing specific cell types and molecular programs for future therapeutic investigation.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because it identifies molecular signatures of Alzheimer's disease that are consistent across racially and ethnically diverse population groups, addressing a longstanding gap in neurodegenerative disease research that has historically focused on less diverse cohorts. By examining multiple cell types in post-mortem brain tissue, the study offers a more broadly applicable understanding of the cellular mechanisms underlying cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
items.citation: Tain Luquez, Jonathan Algoo, Rebecca Chiu et al.. Cell-type signatures of Alzheimer’s disease shared across population groups. Nature. 2026

items.title: An encyclopedia of human enhancer–gene regulatory interactions
items.summary: This paper set out to comprehensively map the regulatory relationships between transcriptional enhancers and their target genes across the human genome. The researchers integrated multiple data types from the ENCODE Consortium—including predictive models, chromatin states, three-dimensional genomic contacts, and large-scale CRISPR perturbation experiments—to develop a systematic benchmarking pipeline and a new machine learning model called ENCODE-rE2G. This model was trained and evaluated against tens of thousands of experimentally validated enhancer–gene pairs, fine-mapped expression quantitative trait loci, and genome-wide association study variants with known causal genes, achieving state-of-the-art predictive performance. Applying this model, the authors produced an encyclopedia of tens of millions of enhancer–gene interactions spanning hundreds of cell types and tissues, revealing global properties of enhancer networks and differences in regulatory complexity among genes. Beyond enhancer activity and three-dimensional enhancer–promoter contacts, model interpretation highlighted promoter class and enhancer–enhancer synergy as additional determinants of enhancer–promoter communication, and the resource improves the linking of noncoding disease-associated variants to their target genes and relevant cell types.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it delivers an unprecedentedly comprehensive catalog of enhancer–gene regulatory interactions, offering the research community a large-scale resource to advance understanding of gene regulation and its links to human genetics.
items.citation: Andreas R. Gschwind, Kristy S. Mualim, Alireza Karbalayghareh et al.. An encyclopedia of human enhancer–gene regulatory interactions. Nature. 2026

items.title: Magnetic character of the low-energy enhancement in 70Zn
items.summary: The paper investigated the electromagnetic character of the low-energy enhancement observed in the gamma-ray strength function of a zinc isotope, a feature that influences both stellar nucleosynthesis and nuclear structure theory. The researchers performed an experiment specifically designed to probe the gamma-ray strength function and determine whether the enhancement at low photon energies arises from electric or magnetic transitions. They found that the low-energy enhancement in this nucleus is magnetic in nature, arising from magnetic dipole transitions between nuclear states. This result resolves a longstanding open question about the origin of this feature in gamma-ray strength functions and has direct implications for predictive models used in nuclear science and our understanding of element creation in stars.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it resolves the physical origin of a puzzling feature in nuclear γ-ray emission, demonstrating that the low-energy enhancement observed in a specific nucleus arises from magnetic dipole transitions rather than electric ones, a distinction with significant implications for understanding nuclear structure and reaction rates.
items.citation: E. K. Ronning, A. L. Richard, S. N. Liddick et al.. Magnetic character of the low-energy enhancement in 70Zn. Nature. 2026

items.title: Catalyst-free, microdroplet-mediated waste plastic conversion to diacids
items.summary: This paper investigated a catalyst-free approach to converting waste plastics into valuable carboxylic acids, addressing longstanding challenges in plastic upcycling such as catalyst deactivation, feedstock variability, and limited economic feasibility. The researchers exploited the spontaneous generation of hydroxyl radicals at microdroplet interfaces to achieve oxidative cleavage of a wide range of waste plastics, including polyolefins and rubbers, under mild conditions without requiring any added catalyst. The method achieved complete conversion of polyethylene with high selectivity toward short-chain diacids and was demonstrated to work on mixed commercial plastics at meaningful scale. Mechanistic analysis revealed that water plays a central role in mediating a distinctive oxidative degradation pathway involving sequential hydroxyl radical addition to alkyl radicals, which differs fundamentally from classical liquid-phase aerobic oxidation of alkanes. The authors propose this microdroplet-based strategy as a scalable and infrastructure-light blueprint for industrial implementation of interfacial radical chemistry, with broad implications for oxidation processes in organic acid synthesis.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it offers a way to convert waste plastics into useful diacids without requiring any catalyst, instead harnessing hydroxyl radicals naturally generated at microdroplet interfaces using only water and oxygen under mild conditions. The approach promises efficient, scalable polymer upcycling with minimal infrastructure, representing a potentially transformative simplification over conventional chemical recycling methods.
items.citation: Ruiliang Gao, Liwei Zhang, Richard J. Lewis et al.. Catalyst-free, microdroplet-mediated waste plastic conversion to diacids. Nature. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide-polydopamine membranes with controlled interlayer spacing
items.summary: The study developed composite graphene oxide membranes pillared with polydopamine, designed to achieve precisely controlled subnanometre interlayer spacing for selective ion transport and water filtration. The fabrication method exploited the difference in freezing temperature between nanoconfined water and bulk water, allowing dopamine molecules to rapidly assemble into nanopillars within the membrane interlayers while the surrounding environment was frozen; the process could be halted at any point to fix the desired spacing, after which slower polymerization and covalent bonding reactions rigidified the structure. The resulting membranes achieved interlayer spacings as small as the dry-state value reported, enabling the sieving of hydrated rubidium and potassium ions that differ in size by less than a tenth of an ångström, with an exceptionally high separation factor between the two ions. The membranes also demonstrated high-flux water permeance substantially exceeding that of conventional membranes, sustaining continuous freshwater production over an extended period. These findings establish a versatile strategy for fabricating structurally robust graphene oxide membranes with subångström tunability for demanding separation applications.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it demonstrates composite graphene oxide membranes whose interlayer spacing can be precisely tuned and stabilized, enabling the selective separation of hydrated ions and sustained high-performance freshwater production.
items.citation: Youhua Lu, Laiyang Wei, Zi-an Xie et al.. Graphene oxide-polydopamine membranes with controlled interlayer spacing. Nature. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper studied the detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* infection in freshwater snail intermediate hosts, which is critical for controlling schistosomiasis transmission. The researchers developed a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of the parasite, optimized for a simple single-temperature incubation. The assay was benchmarked against conventional parasitological methods, standard PCR, and real-time PCR using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two endemic African countries. In laboratory settings the LAMP assay achieved perfect specificity and outperformed microscopy in sensitivity, while in field surveys it detected more positive snails than conventional PCR and identified infections entirely missed by parasitological examination. The authors conclude that this LAMP assay is a sensitive, specific, and practically deployable diagnostic tool suitable for routine snail surveillance and early warning of shifts in schistosomiasis transmission.

items.summary: This paper addressed the problem of subjective and error-prone visual interpretation of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostic results, which can lead to false-positive and false-negative outcomes. The researchers developed a machine learning approach using the YOLOv8 object detection algorithm to automatically locate reaction tubes in images and classify them as positive or negative for DNA amplification. The trained model was evaluated on a test set and demonstrated strong classification performance, with high accuracy, precision, and recall for both positive and negative cases. The findings suggest that this automated image-based approach can reduce human subjectivity in LAMP result interpretation and is suitable for real-time diagnostic deployment with minimal operational complexity.

items.title: Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.
items.summary: This paper investigated the development of a nucleic acid amplification method capable of functioning across a wide temperature range, addressing limitations of both conventional PCR and standard isothermal techniques. The researchers used a Bst polymerase with strong strand displacement activity and broad thermostability to enable LAMP-based amplification spanning from near-physiological to high temperatures. They demonstrated that amplification could be initiated at either high or low starting temperatures and sustained under dynamic, fluctuating thermal conditions rather than requiring precise temperature maintenance. The system was validated for the detection of SARS-CoV-2 and Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomic targets. The authors propose this broad-temperature amplification platform as a practical solution for point-of-care and field diagnostics in settings where strict thermal regulation is unavailable.
items.citation: Hamidizadeh M, Bier FF. Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.
items.summary: This review examines isothermal amplification technologies as diagnostic tools for detecting pathogens in both livestock and companion animals. The authors synthesize recent advances across multiple isothermal amplification methods, evaluating their design innovations, analytical improvements, and integration into portable, field-deployable platforms. The motivation is to address key limitations of conventional and PCR-based molecular diagnostics, which typically demand expensive equipment, dedicated laboratory infrastructure, and specialized expertise that restrict their use in field and resource-limited settings. Isothermal methods are highlighted as rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly alternatives that operate without thermocycling equipment, making them well suited for point-of-need veterinary diagnostics. The review also identifies current challenges and outlines future directions for embedding these technologies into routine veterinary practice and integrated animal disease surveillance programs.
items.citation: Tooryan F, Enyertornye B, Choudhury FJ et al.. Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Development of a digital loop-mediated isothermal amplification using a digital polymerase chain reaction device.
items.summary: This study developed and optimized a digital loop-mediated isothermal amplification workflow by adapting a commercial digital polymerase chain reaction platform to perform absolute quantification without standard curves. The researchers targeted a mitochondrial gene region of an aquatic invasive species and refined reaction conditions using a diluted intercalating dye master mix to make the isothermal chemistry compatible with the nanoplate-based partitioning system. They compared this approach against conventional turbidimetric bulk amplification and found that the digital format provided more stable and consistent detection at very low template concentrations where the traditional method exhibited variability and delayed amplification signals. The high partition density of the platform helped reduce molecular dropout and extended the quantifiable dynamic range, though minor saturation effects emerged at elevated concentrations. The authors conclude that this approach offers a practical, precise tool applicable to diagnostics, food safety testing, and environmental DNA monitoring, particularly when target molecules are scarce.
items.venue: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
items.citation: Fukuta S, Suzuki R. Development of a digital loop-mediated isothermal amplification using a digital polymerase chain reaction device.. Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize, as it provides only a report citation and a URL without any description of the study's methods, scope, or findings.
items.citation: V. Kotov. Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package. Dokumentenrepositorium der RUB (Ruhr University Bochum). 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent innovations in microfluidic chip technology, also called lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine. The authors surveyed advances in chip design and fabrication approaches, including three-dimensional printing, modular architectures, and flexible substrates, alongside the integration of biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of smart diagnostic platforms that support self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision-making across applications ranging from cancer diagnostics and infectious disease detection to point-of-care testing and personalized medicine. The review also highlights emerging uses in neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling as evidence of the technology's broad clinical potential. The authors additionally address ongoing challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration that must be overcome to translate these next-generation platforms into routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
